News.title: Exact time the King’s birthday gun salute takes place today as cannons set to fire across the capital
News.content:
Next

ROYAL fans flocking to London this weekend can catch a very special military honour for the King’s birthday.

King Charles III celebrates his 78th birthday today (November 14), and to mark the occasion the Tower of London will fire off a special gun salute.

Visitors can catch the action from viewing spots on the Tower Wharf, next to the Gun Park outside the Tower and looking over the River Thames.



The gun salute will start at 1pm today and will fire 62 rounds of blanks from four 25 pounder guns.



It is free to watch, but be aware the Wharf will close to non-authorised personnel at least an hour before the salute.

There will be no access to parts of the Wharf during the set-up and duration of the firing, which is being carried out by the Honourable Artillery Company.

There is a long and proud history of the gun salute, used to celebrate special days in the Royal Family including birthdays and anniversaries.



Royal salutes take place across London and in other parts of the UK to mark the occasion. In the capital, Hyde Park and Green Park are also used by gunners.

“Just as an open hand salute was used historically to demonstrate that no weapon was being held, a gun salute indicated the friendly intent of an empty ammunition chamber,” the Royals website explains.

The next scheduled gun salutes after the King’s birthday are for Coronation Day on May 6, 2027 followed by Charles’ Official Birthday (Trooping the Colour) on June 12.

Queen Camilla’s birthday on July 17 will also be marked by a gun salute, as will Accession Day on September 8.



Guns will be fired for the State Opening of Parliament next summer, as well as any state visits in the next few months.

News.title: How many hours Brits will spend wrapped up on the couch this winter are revealed
News.content:
COLD COMFORT How many hours Brits will spend wrapped up on the couch this winter are revealed







Next

BRITS will spend 177 hours curled up on the sofa this winter, a study has revealed.

That’s the equivalent of seven days and nine hours lounging on the couch over a 13-week winter – or almost 10 BILLION HOURS collectively across the UK.



And it seems we can’t wait to get cosy, with more than nine in 10 Brits (94 per cent) having something they look forward to about winter.

Cosy nights at home top the list on 62 per cent, followed by the anticipation of Christmas (37 per cent), big Sunday roasts (34 per cent), hot chocolate (33 per cent) and watching favourite winter films (32 per cent).



Snow falling while you’re safely inside (31 per cent), getting under a blanket on the sofa (30 per cent), Christmas markets (29 per cent), crisp winter walks (29 per cent) and hearty food (29 per cent) make the nation’s winter favourites.

The average Brit will spend almost 14 hours a week on the sofa, more than 12 hours watching films, TV and box sets and nearly nine hours preparing home-cooked food.



The typical adult expects five cosy nights in and almost five films each week – around 67 nights in and 63 movies over the season.

Home Alone is the nation’s ultimate winter movie, chosen by 48 per cent, ahead of Elf (30 per cent), Harry Potter (28 per cent), Love Actually (27 per cent) and Die Hard (27 per cent).

But the poll of 2,013 UK adults for Metro Plumb found that while Brits put plenty of effort into getting themselves winter-ready, the same cannot always be said for their homes.

Despite more than nine in 10 (92 per cent) feeling confident their property is ready for colder temperatures, three quarters (75 per cent) admit they only really think about their heating and plumbing when something goes wrong.



More than one in five (22 per cent) have ignored a dripping tap for at least a week, while 10 per cent have lived with a continuously running toilet, 10 per cent mould or recurring mould and 6 per cent an unexplained damp patch.

Steven Chambers, Managing Director of Metro Plumb, said: “Winter is when our homes really become our sanctuary. We get the jumpers and coats out, cook warming meals and rewatch favourite films.

“But while we put plenty of effort into getting ourselves ready for winter, three quarters of us only think about the heating and plumbing when something actually goes wrong.

“A dripping tap or running toilet can seem like something you can put up with, but wasted water quickly adds up. Finding and fixing a leak early can help reduce wasted water and unnecessary costs.”

Norwich has meanwhile been crowned Britain’s sofa capital, with residents expecting to spend 17 hours a week lounging on the couch this winter – around 221 hours.



Gen Z are embracing hibernation too, with young adults set to spend around 132 hours curled up this frosty season.

Nearly three quarters of Gen Z (73 per cent) look forward to cosy nights at home, 44 per cent hot chocolate, 38 per cent the anticipation of Christmas and 36 per cent big Sunday roasts.

Hibernation is spilling into the working day too, with almost half (49 per cent) of Gen Z home workers answering emails from bed first thing and 37 per cent staying under the covers longer to keep warm.

But not everyone is ready to surrender to the cold, however, with almost half (49 per cent) trying to go as long as possible before switching on the heating, 28 per cent refusing to get their winter coat out until absolutely necessary and 23 per cent sleeping with the window open even when it is freezing.

One in six (17 per cent) continue wearing shorts, while 13 per cent claim they will try to get through the whole winter without turning on the heating.



And almost half (49 per cent) simply expect their heating and plumbing to keep working when the mercury drops, despite 19 per cent having experienced a room which stays colder than the rest of the house, 15 per cent a radiator which takes a long time to heat and 12 per cent cold patches on radiators.

Another 16 per cent have experienced banging, knocking or gurgling from radiators or pipes.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Steven added: “If you’re noticing cold spots on radiators, rooms that never seem to warm up or a heating system that appears to be working harder than it should, it may be worth having the system assessed for a powerflush. Removing accumulated sludge can improve circulation throughout the system and help restore heating performance.”

For anyone unsure whether their home is winter-ready, Metro Plumb has created a Home Health Checklist offering four simple places to start.

News.title: Terrifying moment monster explosion erupts from chemical plant in huge blast as workers flee
News.content:
Next

THIS is the horrifying moment a monstrous explosion rips through a factory, leaving at least 12 people injured.

Terrifying footage showed a massive fireball engulfing the chemical plant in Brazil – sparking urgent evacuations of nearby homes.



The fiery blast went off at the Pyrozzar factory in Salto, São Paulo, on Friday morning.

In the shocking footage, several people can be seen walking away from the inferno.



Moments later, it erupts into an apocalyptic fireball, sending plumes of thick smoke billowing into the sky at breakneck pace.

Gobsmacked bystanders are seen running for their lives as the flames continue to grow larger by the second.

Other staggering clips showed the vicious flames shooting up from the site of the horror.

The 12 injured victims included one of the company owners, military police officers, firefighters and civilians.



Emergency services rushed to the scene near the Prefeito Hélio Steffen Highway and raced wounded people to hospital.

At least 60 firefighters were deployed as well as 22 response vehicles.

Teams are still working to combat the flames and ensure the nearby area is safe.



A helicopter was also scrambled to help monitor the situation.

Nearby residents were evacuated from their homes to ensure their safety.

Reginaldo Rodrigues, a bystander who recorded the blast, told of his harrowing experience fleeing the blaze.

He said: “We tried to run and it seemed like we couldn’t get to where we wanted to go.

“The fire was really close. It’s a feeling of despair. I had never been through anything like that before, it was the first time as a cameraman that I encountered this situation… very sad.”



The factory, owned by Pyrozzar Indústria Química e Comércio, specialises in producing industrial paints, varnishes, and solvents.

It also works with reused chemical waste such as paint sludge and contaminated products.

The firm said it had launched a probe into the disaster.

They said: “Our technical team and the relevant authorities are already working on site.

“All emergency protocols were activated immediately. The Fire Department is on site and the area has been isolated.

“We are providing full assistance to the employees directly involved and their families.”

News.title: Student overstayer tricked more than 70 girls as young as 10 to send naked photos and videos & used them as blackmail
News.content:
TWISTED FIEND Student overstayer tricked more than 70 girls as young as 10 to send naked photos and videos & used them as blackmail







Next

AN Indian student who tricked more than 70 girls across the UK to send naked photos and videos has been jailed for 30 years.

Bilal Kazi, 27, who had overstayed his visa, preyed on his victims by pretending to be a 14-year-old white, blond-haired schoolboy named Reece.



The predator then posed as their boyfriend, pressuring them, even while they were at school, to send explicit pictures and videos of themselves on Snapchat.

Kazi would then threaten to leak the material online, so victims sent more indecent images out of fear, Chester Crown Court heard.



He admitted to 33 child sex offences relating to 19 victims, including causing a child to engage in penetrative sexual activity, making indecent images of children and six counts of blackmail, between 2021 and 2025.

But police fear Kazi, who targeted young girls on apps including Snapchat, Wizz and Wink, and while playing Roblox, could have as many as 180 potential victims who have not been identified.



The 27-year-old victimised vulnerable teens in particular with many left with psychological trauma, feeling broken and their innocence stolen, a court heard.

He twice leaked indecent images online, leaving the young victims suicidal.



The vile predator told a 13-year-old girl that he was preparing her to have sex with him, and told others that sending naked images is what people did for each other if they were in love.

Kazi met another teen victim on an app called Wizz, before grooming her on Snapchat.

Some of her friends logged into her account and saw a video she had sent to ‘Reece’, which was shared around her school and others, and she said her “whole world fell apart”.

In a victim impact statement, she said: “I was young and I didn’t know any better. I became a joke overnight, like I had done something wrong. I was just a kid.”

It was heard the girl lost all her friends, was bullied, fell into severe depression, and took an overdose.



Kazi hacked the Snapchat account of another girl and publicly posted on her profile the indecent video she had sent him, which was viewed by 93 users.

The girl’s mother found the messages from ‘Reece’ in May 2022 and alerted police.

Kazi, a chemical engineering PhD student originally from Mumbai, was traced, living in Chester but had left the country.

He was then arrested at Heathrow Airport in July 2023, when he came back from visiting family in Kuwait and his mobile phone was seized.

The paedophile, at the time living in Birmingham, continued to target teenage girls while released on bail.



Kazi was finally rearrested and remanded into custody in August 2025 and police found hundreds of category A child sex abuse videos involving teenage girls, along with 9,000 messages exchanged with one girl alone in the space of three weeks.

Cheshire Police said their investigation into Kazi became the force’s largest ever online child sexual abuse case as 70 victims, aged between 10 and 17 at the time of offending, were identified across 28 of the UK’s police force areas.

Judge Steven Everett, Recorder of Chester, jailed the defendant for 30 years, with an extended sentence of eight years on licence, saying: “That’s the sad feature. He’s taken away their childhoods.

“You took advantage of what appears to me a lack of proper security on social media sites which should have been there to prevent young persons being taken advantage of by sexual predators like you.

“It is incomprehensible why any person would do what you did to these 19 different young girls and we have no idea how many others.



“We will never know how many victims have fallen prey to you. You are a very dangerous person.”

Detective Sergeant Ross Peel said: “Victims should never feel ashamed of what they have experienced. The responsibility for these offences lies solely with the offender, and we want anyone who has been subjected to this kind of abuse to know that they will be listened to, supported and taken seriously.

“Our message to parents is to speak to your children and take an interest in the apps and platforms they are using. The potential for online offending is vast, and offenders can target children from anywhere in the world.

“By educating yourselves and your children about online safety and the risks associated with communicating with people they do not know online, you can help protect them from becoming victims of crime – the impact of which can be profound and long-lasting.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“I hope this case demonstrates our commitment to protecting vulnerable people and bringing an end to the sexual exploitation of children. It should also serve as a warning to those who, like Kazi, believe that hiding behind a screen makes them anonymous and untouchable.



“No matter where you are or how you choose to offend, those who target children and vulnerable people will be identified and brought to justice.”

News.title: Small boat migrant raped woman twice after dragging her into tent beneath London bridge
News.content:
Next

A SMALL boat migrant who dragged a woman into his tent in a homeless encampment and repeatedly raped her is facing years in jail.

Moustafa Elbohy targeted his victim after she had been out drinking with work colleagues on September 20 last year.



She stopped to chat to the 32-year-old Egyptian and his friends near Embankment tube station in Central London because she lived near “a lovely Middle Eastern community” and enjoyed listening to them speak Arabic, a court heard.

But Elbohy pulled her into his tent and used Google Translate to threaten her.



He then forced the woman to the ground and raped her twice.

Prosecutor Richard Milne told Southwark crown court that she thought Elbohy might kill her in the tarpaulin encampment under Hungerford Bridge.

He said: “She was scared and fearful, and told him she needed to get home to her husband and children.”

When the woman got away, she contacted an actor friend who had just finished in a play.

He arrived within 15 minutes and took her to Charing Cross police station to report the attack.

The woman told police: “I was really scared. It was dark and there was no one else around.



“He was a really volatile, angry man.

“I felt fear and scaredness. I felt disgusting.”

Speaking with her head in her hands, she told police officers: “He was really rough.”

Elbohy, whose address was formerly given as the Doubletree by Hilton Reading in Wokingham, Berkshire, claimed his victim consented to sex.

But he was convicted of two counts of rape yesterday by a jury after seven hours and 57 minutes of deliberation.



Elbohy — who entered the country on a small boat three months before the attack and was housed in a hotel where he made an unsuccessful asylum claim — will be sentenced on Tuesday.

News.title: US soldier suspected of spying for Russia served alongside SAS in Afghanistan before arrest in Britain
News.content:
Next

A US soldier suspected of spying for Russia served with the SAS in Afghanistan, The Sun can reveal.

Lt Col Brandon Tyner spent a year with a special forces task force that included SBS, Navy Seals and Delta Force.



The married dad-of-two, 41, was arrested on Tuesday at his four-bed home in Innsworth, Gloucs.

He was one of around 30 US personnel at Nato’s Allied Rapid Reaction Corps (ARRC) at nearby Imjin barracks.



In 2013 he served with the elite Special Operations Joint Task Force in Kabul.

As deputy head of its personnel branch, he was never a “badged” special forces operator and did not go out on missions.

But he would have had access to Special Forces soldiers’ names, roles and units.

The taskforce was led by Delta Force Gen Scott Miller, a hero of 1993’s Battle of Mogadishu which inspired the book and film Black Hawk Down.

Sources close to the Tyner investigation are “confident” he didn’t share anything with any genuine Russians.

One said: “He was intercepted before any damage could be done.”



Counter Terrorism Police said he was arrested under the National Security Act 2023.

He can be held for up to 14 days but is expected to be charged within days.

News.title: British CNN war reporter who dodged bombs & gun ordeal sues for £1.6m after breaking ankle outside restaurant in London
News.content:
Next

A WAR reporter who survived guns, bombs and grenades is suing for £1.6million after breaking his ankle outside a restaurant.

Brit telly newsman Matthew Chance, 56, claims his career was torpedoed by a patch of grease.



The CNN correspondent, on £425,000 a year, fell over in Christmas 2022, slipping on “greasy and oily” food waste at a stall in Borough Market, London Bridge.

Mr Chance, who was heading to the nearby Roast Restaurant to book a table, suffered a “Bosworth Fracture”, where ligaments are torn from the bone.



He claims he was forced to move back to the UK from Moscow, raising his tax bill and hitting earnings.

He is suing the Borough Market Trustees at London’s High Court for his injuries and lost past and future income.

Barrister James Byrne said it “has caused a substantial loss to him”.

The trustees have admitted liability, but are set to contest the amount of damages.

Mr Chance has had several brushes with death, including being held at gunpoint in Libya.

He also interviewed Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky in his Kyiv bunker as Russian bombs landed.



Live from Ukraine in another report, he saw he was crouching next to a grenade by a road, telling viewers: “Let’s move away from that.”

Barrister James Hogg, for the trustees, said he must prove “incidence, causation, nature and extent of the pain, injury, loss and damage alleged”.

He said “credibility was an issue” as Mr Chance was able to return to report from Ukraine in 2023.

The case is scheduled for a five-day trial in early 2028.

News.title: Brit flight to America cancelled after FAA grounds planes with weekend journeys likely to be affected
News.content:
Next

BRITS travelling to America have seen their flights cancelled after the US grounded all planes on Friday night.

The US’s Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) halted all flights nationwide “due to extraordinary circumstances”, sparking fears it will cause travel chaos this weekend.



British Airways cancelled a flight to New York which had been due to take off from London Heathrow at 10.30pm on Friday.

A spokesman for Manchester Airport confirmed three US-bound flights scheduled to leave on Saturday morning – all operated by Virgin Atlantic – are likely to be affected if the issue is not resolved soon.



A Virgin Atlantic spokesperson said: “We’re aware of the ground stop order issued by the Federal Aviation Administration for all US airports.

“We’re closely monitoring the situation and assessing any impact to our flights. We advise any customers due to travel to check their flight status at virginatlantic.com.”



US transportation secretary Sean Duffy said the FAA is investigating a communications issue affecting regional air traffic control centres – the incident has left millions of US passengers stranded.

It is only the second time flights have been grounded across the US since the September 11 terror attacks in 2001.



Flights were halted by the FAA in January 2023 because of a system error.

US homeland security secretary Markwayne Mullin said: “There is no reason for the public to be afraid or scared for your loved ones.

“This isn’t another 9/11… This is a telecommunications outage.

“Throughout FAA, out of abundant of caution, we have grounded all the flights, and all the flights are accounted for.

“As incoming flights, either internationally or the flights that are currently still in the air, we’ll be dealing with those case by case.



“As you can imagine, there will be a priority list as they start coming in.”

He added: “Everybody is safe. There is no reason to be concerned about your loved ones if they’re flying or anything like that. I just want to make sure everybody’s at ease about that.”

He went on: “There is no indication as of yet that this was a nefarious attack against us. It’s just a telecommunication outage as of right now.”

A spokesperson for American Airlines said: “The FAA has temporarily paused departures nationwide.

“Flights already in the air can continue to their destinations.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“We expect disruption to our schedule for the rest of the day, depending on the length of the FAA’s nationwide ground stop.

“It will be all hands-on deck across American to get customers on their way as soon as possible when the FAA lifts this ground stop.

News.title: US Air Force responds to major suspected drone alert at RAF Lakenheath
News.content:
US Air Force responds to major suspected drone alert at RAF Lakenheath

The Ministry of Defence said the situation “is now resolved” and it is “working closely” with the US Air Force to establish the facts

View 3 Images RAF Lakenheath in Suffolk (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

The US Air Force said it has responded to “suspected unauthorised drone activity” over RAF Lakenheath in Suffolk.

‌



‌



It added that “no personnel, aircraft or infrastructure were affected” and encouraged people to report “any unusual or suspicious activity to local authorities”.

‌



The Ministry of Defence said the situation “is now resolved” and it is “working closely” with the US Air Force to establish the facts.

‌



Downing Street insisted earlier this week that British air bases are safe and their security is a “top priority” after US aircraft were moved from nearby RAF Mildenhall, also in Suffolk.

View 3 Images British Royal Air Force base RAF Lakenheath, which hosts the near the 48th Fighter Wing of the US Air Force, near the village of Lakenheath (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

‌



RAF Lakenheath said in September that it was on “Charlie alert”, the second-highest threat level that can be issued by the US department of defence.

It is home to the 48th fighter wing, also known as the Liberty Wing, with almost 7,000 active-duty personnel making it the largest US fighter operation in Europe, according to the official base website.

‌



A US European Command spokesperson said on Friday evening: “I can confirm that this evening US Air Force Security Forces personnel responded to suspected unauthorised drone activity over RAF Lakenheath.

“No personnel, aircraft or infrastructure were affected. We continue to work closely with our host nation counterparts to ensure the safety and security of our US service members, US and host nation civilians, contractors, and all of our families.

‌



View 3 Images Signage warns of Ministry of Defence land as a US military jet takes off from RAF Lakenheath

“Protecting our shared community is a joint responsibility and we encourage everyone to support this effort by reporting any unusual or suspicious activity.

‌



“We work closely with our host nation counterparts to keep a vigilant and proactive security posture around our bases and installations.”

An MoD spokesperson said: “We are co-ordinating with all relevant parties regarding reports of unauthorised drone activity at RAF Lakenheath this evening. USAF Security Forces personnel responded to the reports and the situation is now resolved. We are working closely with them to establish the facts. We will provide updates in due course.”

‌



Mr Timothy, the MP for West Suffolk, posted on Facebook: “Following the speculation about the alarm at RAF Lakenheath, I have been in touch with the authorities at the base. I am told there is no threat to the public, and the incident is now resolved.

"Given the raised threat level, I continue to encourage everyone to report anything suspicious or out of the ordinary to the authorities.

Article continues below

“And I also encourage the Ministry of Defence and US air force to communicate as freely as operational security constraints allow them.”

Suffolk Police has been approached for comment.

News.title: Horrifying video shows passengers clinging onto American Heritage cruise ship after tanker crash
News.content:
Horrifying video shows passengers clinging onto American Heritage cruise ship after tanker crash

Between 180 and 190 passengers were aboard the cruise ship, New Orleans Mayor Helena Moreno said at a Friday news conference

View 2 Images The tanker Atlantic Ashphalt is seen after crashing into a river cruise in New Orleans, Friday (Image: AP Photo/Matthew Hinton)

Passengers were filmed clambering over boat rails to get to safety as the American Heritage cruise ship sank.

‌



‌



Every passenger has been accounted for after a frantic rescue mission that left 32 people hospitalised. The U.S. Coastguard has confirmed one was killed in the incident, in what the state's governor is calling the "miracle on the Mississippi".

‌



The Atlantic Asphalt tanker crashed into the side of the American Cruise Lines' American Heritage at around 12:30pm local time. The river cruiser was docked on the Mississippi River at the Port of New Orleans when it was hit.

‌



View 2 Images Investigation is underway, Landry says (Image: AP Photo/Gerald Herbert)

Footage caught the moment passengers screamed as the ship began falling to its side and sinking rapidly. In other videos circulating on social media, several people are seen in the water wearing life jackets as helicopters fly overhead.

To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

‌



A video shared on KSLA News 12 showed passengers in lifejackets clinging onto the ship as it continued to take on water. The video was shared at 2.10pm ET time and has had over 300 comments.

‌



The latest statement from the U.S. Coastguard reads: "Working closely with our partners, the USCG has confirmed all passengers are accounted for, with no reported casualties following the collision on the MS River. Our focus now shifts to safely reopening the river and coordinating salvage operations."

New Orleans Mayor Helena Moreno says an American Cruise Line vessel "toppled over and flipped" after a tanker ship navigating the river lost control. Louisiana Governor Jeff Landry praised the quick emergency response to the crash, dubbing it the "miracle on the Mississippi"

‌



The cause of the crash is unclear and the mayor says an investigation is underway, though it appears a "loss of steering" may have been involved.

The Mississippi River, the second-longest river in North America, is a major commercial waterway carrying 669 million tons of cargo across the US every year, according to the US Army Corps of Engineers.

The river will at first likely be reopened to one-way traffic, with the Coast Guard's vessel monitoring service helping direct all the traffic coming through, says Burnham.
