News.title: US ground stop lifted after FAA order halted air traffic and left thousands waiting at airports
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

After hours of airport chaos, confused passengers and little information, federal officials ended a ground stop order that halted planes across the U.S.

The Federal Aviation Administration issued the order around 4 p.m. Friday “due to extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety.” Around 8:30 p.m. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy announced the order was lifted, though he said it would take a while for the skies to return to normal.

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said there was no evidence of a cyberattack, but the root cause remained under investigation.

Duffy pinned the blame on an outdated air traffic control system and described the problem as a network that got “overloaded with data.”

Thousands of flights were delayed or canceled, leaving passengers waiting at airports. Photos from nearly every city showed packed hallways and lines with passengers searching for any information about when they might be able to travel.

open image in gallery Thousands of passengers were left waiting for hours November 13 after the FAA officials in the US issued a ‘ground stop’ order that halted planes from leaving airports ( REUTERS )

According to FlightAware, more than 9,000 flights were delayed Friday. However, some could have been for weather or other issues before the order was issued.

“There was never any lives at risk,” Mullin said. “There was no flights at risk. FAA was able to handle it. We did it out of an abundance of caution.”

He added that he understood internet conspiracy theories, but there was no indication of something larger at play. He later admitted that as of late Friday there was “nothing completely certain.”

During a White House briefing late Friday, Duffy blamed the nation’s aging air traffic system for the outage. He said the nation relies on an analog system and it got overloaded with data — which Mullin said came from new technology overwhelming the older system.

open image in gallery Officials blamed an outdated air traffic system for the problem ( Reuters )

open image in gallery Roughly 3,000 planes were in the air when the ground stop was issued ( AFP/Getty )

“We have old switches, old routers. It's an old system that went down and went down everywhere. It got overloaded. I don't want to rule out that we didn't have nefarious activity here,” Duffy said.

Reporters pressed the Trump administration officials on what caused the overload, but neither offered specifics. They also could not explain why the system failed on Friday rather than on any other day.

Duffy used the briefing to rant about Congress and called for more funds to replace the nation’s aging infrastructure. He demanded for $50 billion — up from the $30 billion Trump asked from Congress — to update the nation’s air traffic system.

“Let’s not do a patchwork fix to a system that’s critical for every single family,” Duffy said. “This is a continual problem that we have, and it should be fixed.”

open image in gallery The outage lasted five hours and officials said it will take time before US skies return to normal ( Getty Images )

open image in gallery Passengers search for any information about when they might be allowed to travel as they waited ( Reuters )

The FAA ground stop order caused problems for passengers nationwide during the five hours it remained in place. College football teams couldn't travel ahead of Saturday games. That led some programs to find alternative ways to travel before kickoff.

For those that waited, Duffy encouraged them to contact officials about their travel plans.

“I would encourage those football teams to reach out to the FAA, to schedule their flight times and make sure they can move” their start time, Duffy said.

Passengers at airports were left waiting for information about when they might be allowed to travel to their destination.

In Atlanta, Ashley Aylward told local outlet WSB-TV that she was on the runway when she got word of the order.

“It brought me back to 9/11. I was definitely nervous, but, I mean, we’re still here. We’re still sitting on the runway and still no word on what’s going on and if we were going back to the gate,” Aylward told the station.

In Boston, Dara Albrecht told The Boston Globe she was on a Dallas-bound flight when passengers were given the option to disembark or wait it out and hope for an eventual takeoff. She said many passengers thought they were in danger and rushed to leave.

After she left the plane, the airport was packed and rideshare lines wrapped around the outside of the terminal. She described it as a “madhouse” as she left and rebooked a flight for Saturday morning.

“I was just glad to get out of the airport,” she told the Globe. “When you got into the terminal it is apocalyptic.”

News.title: France pull off one of their greatest wins as Erasmus mind games backfire
News.content:
Given Les Bleus’ injuries, only the 1999 World Cup semi-final victory over New Zealand can come close to this win over the back-to-back world champions, South Africa. The Nations Championship, with the Springboks previously unbeaten, has been blown wide open. Crikey, given these two could meet in a World Cup semi-final next year, rugby’s blue-riband event in Australia has been blown wide open.

And how lucky are we. France did not score a point in the second half and South Africa’s comeback befitted a champion side, but these audacious hosts regaled their Parisian audience with a rugby feast. Rassie Erasmus, the Springboks’ head coach, said that he was nervous before the game and so he should have been. Fabien Galthié, his counterpart, had promised some fun and games, but Erasmus could not help himself: not long before kick-off, he pulled the coup de théâtre, switching his starting and replacement front rows. Time will tell whether such a move was legal.

“We didn’t play well,” said Erasmus. “I can’t find a lot of excuses. They were on top of their game and we were a little bit off. It was one point here and there. They took their opportunities and we didn’t. We weren’t just outplayed, we were outsmarted.”

“I think we’ve killed our dreams for the Nations Championship with this result,” he added, suggesting he thinks New Zealand will beat England next week.

Demons were present for both sides, mainly France. South Africa lost Jasper Wiese to a 20-minute red card for a nasty ruck clear-out – just as Lood de Jager had received in the visitors’ win last year – and, at the end, there was a reverse of that utterly compelling World Cup quarter-final on the same turf. This time, it was South Africa desperately searching for victory, having dominated the scrum and scoring all three of their tries from close range or mauls.

News.title: England’s batting capitulates in defeat to lift Australia’s spirits
News.content:
“We weren’t quick enough to adapt to the conditions, we talked extensively leading into the game about the surface here at Optus,” Brendon McCullum, England’s coach, said. “It’s a bit like batting on a trampoline, there are certain shots that are very difficult to execute. We talked about trying to put those away.”

McCullum called for his team to scrap a bit more, and at least acknowledged this time that driving on the up was unwise.

“KP has got such a nice manner about him,” he said. “He sees his role to get the talent to perform on the world stage. His message will be measured but firm – adapting to conditions, what could we have done, trying to drive the ball on the up is not wise. Next time we hit a surface like this we have to try and work it better.”

After a quiet start, both openers fell tamely. Ben Duckett prodded Johnson to point, then Banton had a booming drive at Bartlett and was caught behind.

Enter Beardman. When he came on to bowl the 10th over of the innings, there was palpable excitement from his home crowd, who had watched another West Australian, Mike Hussey, present his ODI cap before the toss. Later in the day, Hussey was probably glad he rebuffed England’s recent approach to work with their Test batsmen.

Beardman, who is a mentee of Dennis Lillee and has a gorgeously rhythmical action that helped him touch 90mph, started with a maiden to Root, then found just another movement away from Brook to invite the edge. On the occasion of his 200th ODI, Root had been dropped badly on three off Bartlett, and his only boundary came when Beardman found his an inside edge and the ball flew past his stumps.

The pressure told, and Root edged a big drive behind, where Josh Inglis took the third of his five catches. That sparked a collapse of five for 10, with Jordan Cox edging behind prodding in defence, before Curran was caught on the fence hooking for nought. Beardman’s five-fer was completed when Liam Dawson – selected ahead of Adil Rashid again – skewed a flat-footed drive to backward point. Overton followed in the next over, leaving England 65 for eight, with their lowest ever ODI score, 86, inevitably recorded against Australia in 2001, appearing a distant possibility.

A stand of 37 from Will Jacks and Gus Atkinson averted that particular indignity, and the fear of being bowled out for double figures. But the total was never enough and, despite Atkinson bowling Head first ball, the chase was painfully routine thanks to Marsh’s early barrage.

News.title: Kane bends game to his will on record-breaking night
News.content:
Good evening and welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of England vs Croatia in the Nations League, with the hosts’ captain Harry Kane set to become the country’s most-capped player.

The 33-year-old has enjoyed a memorable few weeks, becoming the first English Ballon d’Or winner in 25 years and following it up with a new Bayern Munich contract, and an appearance at Wembley tonight will take him clear of Peter Shilton’s record of 125 England caps.

Kane scored twice in his record-equalling appearance against Czech Republic at Wembley last month, extending his international tally to 91 goals – a total that is unrivalled for England.

“It’s not about me – it’s about the team,” Kane said before tonight’s landmark moment. “I love coming to every England camp. I love playing every game and representing the country in the best way possible.”

The 3-0 home victory over Czech Republic left England on nine points after four Nations League group games, with a 2-0 win in the away contest and a 7-0 thumping of Croatia coming after a 3-2 defeat against world champions Spain.

Thomas Tuchel will be hoping that his side can inflict another heavy defeat on Croatia this evening, but a draw will be enough to book their place in the quarter-finals, with the group’s top two teams progressing.

While Kane will collect plaudits for his 126th cap, attention will also be on a potential first, with Jude Bellingham’s younger brother, Jobe, included in a senior England squad for the first time.

The two Bellinghams appearing together in a senior match would be a new experience for them, while it would be the first time that brothers have taken to the field together for England in 19 years.

“I can’t ignore it, but obviously with Jude being here too, it’s a great, great feeling for the family,” Jobe said on the Football Association’s England app. “It’s quite special, to be honest. It’s such a huge bonus on top of something that’s already so special and so great.”

News.title: Experts hail a “milestone” as TB deaths fall by more than a third in 10 years
News.content:
The number of people dying from tuberculosis has dropped by more than a third over the last 10 years but progress against the disease is still too slow, according to the World Health Organization.

Figures from WHO’s annual TB report showed that the lung disease took the lives of an estimated 1.13 million people in 2025, down from 1.7m in 2015, a drop of 35 per cent.

While WHO hailed this as a major milestone in achieving global targets - albeit five years too late - it said that progress in wiping out TB was still too slow.

Africa and Europe have made the greatest progress in reducing deaths, with numbers halving on both continents over the 10-year period. India and China - countries that have high burdens of the disease - also cut deaths by 35 per cent.

The report also showed that an estimated 10.6million people contracted the disease in 2025, a reduction of just 75,000 since 2024.

TB - still the world’s leading infectious disease killer - is preventable and curable, and is caused by the bacillus Mycobacterium tuberculosis, which is spread when infected people cough or sneeze.

The disease has been around for centuries, and has been described as the quintessential disease of poverty as it spreads in areas of low quality housing, among people with poor nutrition and immunity. It is a particular risk to people who are HIV positive.

Treatment requires a six-month long regimen of medication, and while treatments have become less toxic in recent years, they still take a heavy toll on patients and have a range of side effects, including at the most extreme deafness. Adherence to medication is also a problem.

News.title: Low-cost parenting app halves rates of sexual violence amongst teenagers in Tanzania
News.content:
A low cost parenting intervention has more than halved rates of sexual violence among teenage girls in Tanzania, a study has shown.

The ParentApp digital parenting programme for families is aimed at reducing rates of violence experienced by teenagers of both sexes.

Researchers found the programme helped bolster family relationships and enabled mothers and fathers to better communicate with their children at what is often a tricky stage of their development.

The programme, led by Oxford University and the University of Cape Town in partnership with the Tanzanian government, the World Health Organization and Unicef, combines in-person and mobile parenting support.

Parents have an introductory session with a facilitator and then undertake 12 weekly sessions online. They also join a WhatsApp group with other parents where they can discuss problems and support one another.

The randomized controlled trial, published in The Lancet, included 2,396 children aged 10–17 and 2,396 parents and carers across 80 urban and rural areas.

Families were randomly assigned to receive either ParentApp or a comparison app focused on safe water and hygiene. Researchers analysing the results did not know which app each family received.

At the 14-month follow-up, girls in families participating in the ParentApp initiative reported a 67% reduction in sexual violence; a 54% reduction in sexual exploitation and an improvement in parent-child relationships. The successes were less marked in boys, however.

Violence against children is widespread globally: Unicef data shows that around one in five girls and women and one in seven boys and men globally have experienced sexual violence as children.

Lucie Cluver, professor of child and family social work at Oxford University and one of the authors of the study, said the intervention was aimed at helping parents and children talk to one another and discuss situations before they arise.

In Tanzania, for example, teenage girls might get a motorbike taxi late at night, potentially putting them in a dangerous situation.

“What you’re doing is making plans and problem solving ahead of these risky situations that teenagers end up in. And you’re building trust and the relationship so you can have these difficult conversations,” said Prof Cluver.

She said she was surprised at how big an impact the intervention had on sexual violence: teenage girls reported that because the app helped improve communication with their parents and carers they did not feel the need to go out as much.

The programme cost around $6 per family but researchers calculated that it goes up to around $10 per family if 20% are given smartphones. A traditional in-person parenting intervention generally costs around $120 per family.

Engagement in the sessions was high - around 70 per cent of participants completed the course - and some parents kept in touch with one another after the programme.

However, the authors of the study stressed that while the app focused on families there remains a need to prevent violence against children in other settings, such as schools and religious institutions. There also needs to be a broader societal push to address the scourge.

“The app isn’t the answer to everything - it’s just one part of the puzzle,” said Prof Cluver.

Prof Cluver said she hoped future versions of the programme would include greater focus on digital harms and test whether parents could take the lead themselves.

The programme is being rolled out in other countries, including Mexico, Panama and South Africa, and is easily adaptable for different contexts.

“Tanzania only has 20% smartphone use and we thought if it works in one of the hardest places to do a digital intervention it could work anywhere,” she said.

She said the study showed how parenting was a universal experience, with the majority focused on what is best for their children.

“Parents feel powerless. We live in a world where our kids are facing risks and parents just want to help,” added Prof Cluver.

News.title: AI fuels fastest economic growth in two years
News.content:
The Prime Minister and the Chancellor should not claim credit for the AI-fuelled expansion of Britain’s economy in the third quarter, a think tank said.

Julian Jessop, economics fellow at the Institute of Economic Affairs, said the 0.7pc expansion in the economy was “a tribute to the resilience of the private sector in the face of the energy shock and policy headwinds”.

He said: “This resilience is despite rather than because of anything the Government has done. In particular, the persistent weakens of the construction sector underlines the failure of flagship policies to boost housebuilding and infrastructure spending.

“The Government’s clumsy interventions are also continuing to add to labour and housing costs, including rents. Instead, the key driver of growth and business optimism has been the rollout of AI. This is an area that the Government has not got round to messing up, though that may yet be coming.

“In the meantime, the Government is still borrowing more than expected and the labour market remains weak.

“The full impact of higher inflation and higher interest rates has also yet to be felt. Early surveys for the fourth quarter already show that consumer confidence, retail spending, private sector hiring and housing market activity are all starting to slide again.

“2026 will still be a year when the economy performed much better than expected – at least in terms of GDP. But the new year will start with further increases in energy bills and high levels of job insecurity, which will matter far more to most people.”

News.title: Bird flu viruses ‘gaining function’ through natural mixing, warn scientists
News.content:
The bird flu virus’ resurgence began with an 11-year-old. In February 2023, the schoolgirl was admitted to a hospital in Phnom Penh with severe pneumonia – within a day, she was dead.

Tests soon revealed that she had contracted avian influenza: Cambodia hadn’t reported a human case of bird flu since 2014, but the hiatus was over. Since then, 39 more people have been infected and 15 have died in the Southeast Asian country – a case fatality rate of roughly 40 per cent.

Researchers have been scratching their heads as to why, after nine years, this particular stain of H5N1 suddenly started jumping from birds to people again. The strain or clade called 2.3.2.1 had been circulating for almost a decade without spilling into humans. What changed?

Now, a paper in Emerging Infectious Diseases offers clues.

Scientists say the apparent rise in human cases has coincided with the virus gaining new genetic material and, potentially, new powers of infection, from a second flu virus via a process known as “reassortment”.

News.title: The country where diabetes is more feared than HIV
News.content:
Furthermore, even when antiretrovirals suppress the virus, the immune system can stay chronically activated, causing a low-grade inflammation that damages organs and blood vessels. The Lancet HIV Commission reported that, by one measure of biological ageing, people with HIV appeared about five years older on average than peers without the virus.

HIV also makes other infections more dangerous. For example, those living with the virus are more likely to contract human papillomavirus (HPV), the leading cause of cervical cancer, and they are less able to clear HPV from their bodies.

“With HIV, you don’t channel your mind into dying,” Ms Shongwe said. “But when I got to know that I have cervical cancer, I thought it was the end of the world.”

In 2018, Ms Ginindza moved from the Ministry of Health’s HIV programme to its NCD programme, but almost immediately, she asked to go back to her old job. “There is nothing here,” she recalled, “no tools, no data collection system, no guidelines”.

Even today, the ministry doesn’t have any dedicated NCD posts. While there are hundreds of people working on HIV, there are just 10 NCD staff, all borrowed from other programmes, Ms Ginindza said.

Although latest figures show that NCDs account for almost half of Eswatini’s deaths the government’s programme for NCDs, injuries and mental health received about one million emalangeni - roughly £45,000 - or 0.03 per cent of the health budget.

Foreign aid hasn’t filled the gap: international partners cover about five per cent of NCD spending, Ms Ginindza said, compared with 60 per cent of the HIV response. Donors “cannot give you money when they also need that money to address their own NCDs”, she added.

So, when it comes to these chronic diseases, patients struggle to get diagnosed, obtain their medicines or see a specialist for complications. In a 2024 government survey, fewer than 30 per cent of people with high blood pressure were on medication, and only 14 per cent had their hypertension under control.

The government’s own NCD report puts the stock-out rate for key medicines at 79 per cent, and the public system has no nephrologists, endocrinologists or cardiologists, Ms Ginindza said, relying instead on private specialists and Taiwanese medical missions to provide these services.

Faced with one of the worst HIV epidemics, Eswatini poured almost everything into fighting it. “The focus was HIV,” Ms Ginindza said, “so we forgot about the other conditions.”

Fighting on two fronts



Now, Eswatini is trying to turn its HIV machinery towards chronic diseases.

Since 2020, a government-led scheme has delivered NCD medication refills, blood pressure checks and glucose tests in hundreds of community settings, integrating this with existing HIV services. As it once did with antiretrovirals, the ministry is also shifting NCD care from hospitals to local clinics, Ms Ginindza said, aiming to train at least two nurses at each.

For Mr Mamba, that means he sees the same clinician for his HIV, diabetes and blood pressure. It saves time, he said, since he can get everything under one roof.

The challenge is not just extending HIV services to NCD patients but finding the money to sustain both. The Eswatini government aims to increase NCD funding to 20 million emalangeni, or £900,000, by 2028.

But last year, the Trump administration gutted the US President’s Emergency Plan for Aids Relief (Pepfar), the backbone of Eswatini’s HIV response.

In December, Eswatini signed a five-year deal with the US to restore some HIV funding - on the condition that the government shoulders more of the cost itself. So, as the country scrambles to protect its HIV gains, NCDs risk remaining a secondary priority.

With his diabetes and blood pressure medicines so often out of stock, Mr Mamba has come to dread his check-ups, convinced each one will show his numbers have climbed again - and that his luck is running out.

Many of his neighbours have the same conditions and probably share these fears, he said, but much as people once kept quiet about HIV, they rarely discuss such things.

Over 30 years ago, Ms Gwebu contemplated suicide after being diagnosed with HIV. But today, she hopes Eswatini can sustain its hard-won progress against the virus without leaving those with other diseases behind. “What is going to kill our people,” she said, “is not going to be HIV.”

MAX DOWMAN became the youngest-ever England Under-21 player as he made his debut aged just 16.

The teenager’s second-half introduction elicited the loudest cheer of the night at Ashton Gate as Lee Carsley’s side were sunk 1-0 by Portugal.



Dowman’s cameo – hailed as “outstanding” by Carsley – means he has broken the previous record held by Jude Bellingham by almost FOUR MONTHS.

The Arsenal prospect was unable to help turn the tide in England’s favour after being introduced at the hour mark, but still impressed with some classy touches.



England boss Carsley had stressed pre-match that this fixture was a chance to test his side of youngsters against a top side ahead of next summer’s U21 Euros.

It was certainly a test for the Young Lions, facing a Portugal team littered with top-flight players from the Portuguese Primeira, Ligue 1 and further afield.



Divin Mubama tried his luck early on, attempting to lob Portugal goalkeeper Joao Carvalho from 30 yards out after intercepting a wayward pass from Goncalo Oliveira.

But the Southampton loanee misjudged his distance effort and watched it sail well wide of the upright.

And Portugal took advantage before the half-hour mark when Bayer Leverkusen ace Alfonso Moreira wriggled into the box and flashed a venomous effort at Tommy Setford, which the Arsenal prospect effectively turned into his own net in a moment he will want to quickly forget.

It was always going to be an uphill battle from there for England, with Portugal boasting an incredible defence that conceded just TWO GOALS during their 10 European qualification games.

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel reacts to Morgan Rogers’ passionate rant in defence of axed Chelsea pal Cole Palmer after England snub

MORGAN ROGERS is not set to be punished after passionately defending Cole Palmer following his England snub.

The attacking midfielder, 24, bagged the opener as the Three Lions notched a 2-1 win over Croatia on Thursday.



But Rogers’ Chelsea team-mate Palmer failed to earn a call-up despite England supremo Thomas Tuchel being told he was fully fit.

And the German had no issue with the former Aston Villa siding with his pal during a bombshell rant following the Nations League victory over Croatia.



Tuchel said: “It’s totally fine. He’s his team-mate and, I guess, his friend, so why wouldn’t he?”

Rogers claimed Palmer was desperate to be rewarded with a recall after also missing the World Cup.

The ex-Middlesbrough man told BBC Radio Five Live: “It’s a lie. He wants to be here.

“He wanted to get called up and he wanted to come and represent his country as he always has done. People just see it as news and say the easy thing.

Sports.title: Jesus Owono slapped with maximum 12-MATCH ban by Spanish FA over tragic Jesus de Miguel incident
Sports.content:
Next

JESUS OWONO has been slapped with a 12-match ban following the tragic death of Jesus de Miguel.

The Tenerife striker passed away at the age of 30 following a sickening collision with the FC Andorra keeper earlier this month.



And the Disciplinary Committee of the Royal Spanish Football Federation has handed Owono, 25, the maximum suspension.

Article 102 of the disciplinary code, which covers violent conduct during play resulting in injuries or serious consequences, was applied.



But Owono is still considering retiring following his involvement in the horrific incident.

The shot-stopper was sent off after his knee collided with Jesus’ head and chest as he rushed to clear a long ball in stoppage time.



Medics rushed to the Tenerife frontman’s aid following the X-rated challenge in the Segunda Division showdown, which was locked at 2-2.

But Jesus’ condition deteriorated after being transported to hospital and he tragically died less than 24 hours later.

Owono broke his silence by releasing a heartbreaking statement via FC Andorra.

The Equatorial Guinea international said: “These are the most difficult days of my life.



“I am struggling to find the words, and it is very hard for me to process anything that has happened.

“I feel immense pain over the loss of Jesus. I am thinking of him, his family, and all the people who loved him.

“I know there will be many matters to address, and I will face whatever comes with complete respect.



“But right now, honestly, I cannot think of anything other than Jesus and the grief we are experiencing.

“Rest in peace, Jesus.”

After linking up for the international break, Spain’s big-name stars paid an emotional tribute to Jesus before their first training session.

Sports.title: Mauricio Pochettino is £10m gamble for Man Utd.. he must take sledgehammer to toxic culture and follow Arsenal blueprint
Sports.content:
Next

MANCHESTER UNITED have taken a £10million gamble in appointing Mauricio Pochettino — and it will be fascinating to watch.

This is one last shot for Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada, who have cocked up almost every big call they have made without being held to account by the owners.



Pochettino departs America, where I am based, with very little outcry from fans here that he is leaving.

But as he heads over the Atlantic on his jet in the next few days, picking over the squad with his staff there will be one overriding thought: ‘Holy f***, we’ve got a lot of work to do’.



I played against Pochettino’s Tottenham team, one of the hardest games each year for us in the Premier League. They had quality in bundles, but also togetherness, depth and — above all — intensity.

Getting that out of this Manchester United squad feels nearly impossible, which is why the biggest question is whether Pochettino and United are actually a good fit.



The Argentine is known across football for working his players hard, right to the edge — getting them fit as a fiddle but sometimes making them physically sick.

And here he is faced with a group who cannot seem to stay fit.

Carlos Baleba has arrived and broken down, Harry Maguire comes off constantly and Luke Shaw — who Pochettino was like a father to at Southampton — can no longer be relied upon. That relationship will be different now he’s plagued by injuries.

Even further forward, big signings like Benjamin Sesko — he is never around and has knees as reliable as mine!



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

These players are about to get the biggest volley up the backside they have ever experienced — and I doubt they will be able to handle it.

You look at the team he built at Spurs, with Moussa Dembele, Dele Alli and Christian Eriksen. Can anyone in this United squad match or replicate their skill set? No.

But beyond a huge squad rebuild and a lack of quality, we all know the underlying problem at Old Trafford.

We have enough evidence now to know Jose Mourinho cannot be wrong, Louis van Gaal cannot be wrong. Ralf Rangnick, Erik ten Hag and Ruben Amorim all saw it.

Poch must go in and take a huge sledgehammer to the toxic Carrington culture, accepting that things are not good enough.



Managers and those above need to stop fiddling around the edges and tackle the big problem, otherwise there will be no progress.

United supporters might not like it, but Arsenal have shown the way and offered the blueprint. Rather than repeating what has failed, they must make a brave change. Someone big has to go, even if it means short-term pain.

Mesut Ozil, Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang and Alexandre Lacazette were pushed out for the benefit of everyone.



They were good players but carried a stink with them around the place.

Cut them out and everyone else can breathe, focus in training and start growing.

For the Red Devils, that has to be someone like skipper Bruno Fernandes or, once again, Marcus Rashford.

They cannot move on players like Jadon Sancho or Tyrell Malacia any more — no one really cares about them.

I can guarantee it now, Rashford will suddenly be fit for the Liverpool game. He will see a new manager who likes energy and pace, he will think he can do all that.



He might even start well, get a few games, but then Pochettino will ask for more and he will not like it.

Then all the bad traits will come back — he’ll be out and about and late for training all over again. The cycle begins and the damage returns.

Pochettino must make a statement, give these players until January to prove they are on board or get rid.

LIVE REACTION AS POCH ANNOUNCED AS NEW BOSS

He has to set standards for everyone else to follow. The big challenge is, he must win alongside doing that.



The former Chelsea chief feels like a halfway house between the two other standout candidates, Eddie Howe and Antonio Conte.

He has the tactical acumen and man-management of Howe, with the edge of Conte, without the risk that he will bring the house of cards down with a tantrum.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

That feels like a smart route for United to go down in one sense, but he remains a gamble, seven years since he saw real success in the Premier League.

It will, as always at Old Trafford, be quite the ride.

Sports.title: Goalkeeper involved in fatal Jesus de Miguel collision receives huge ban from football
Sports.content:
Goalkeeper involved in fatal Jesus de Miguel collision receives huge ban from football

After the tragic death of Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel, the goalkeeper who was involved in the collision has been handed a huge ban from football

View 5 Images Jesus Owono has learned the length of his ban (Image: Getty)

The goalkeeper involved in the fatal collision with Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel has been handed a lengthy 12-game ban from football. De Miguel tragically died after he collided with FC Andorra shot-stopper Jesus Owono in a LaLiga Hypermotion game on November 2.

‌



‌



Spanish football entered a period of mourning when it was confirmed that Tenerife star De Miguel had died aged just 30. The striker and opposing goalkeeper Owono both competed for a loose ball during the match, and as the Andorra star attempted to clear it, he struck De Miguel in the chest.

‌



Owono was sent off for the incident. De Miguel went into a cardiorespiratory arrest on the pitch and, after being transported to hospital by ambulance, died at 8am on the morning of November 3. The 30-year-old was laid to rest in his parents' hometown of Navahermosa, Toledo last Thursday and is survived by his partner, Maria, and their daughter, Carla.

‌



A preliminary autopsy report stated De Miguel died from "accidental chest trauma." A police investigation has since been opened, as is routine under Spanish law when it comes to deaths from non-natural causes.

Jesus de Miguel's cause of death revealed after fatal collision with goalkeeper READ MORE :

Nearly two weeks after the horrific tragedy, Owono - who would have served a three-game suspension regardless for violent play - has been handed a 12-match ban by the Disciplinary Committee of the Royal Spanish Football Federation (RFEF).

Referee Manuel Angel Perez Hernandez explained in his report that Owono was dismissed for "making a violent impact with his leg raised high on an opponent with excessive force while the ball was in play."

‌



Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources

Determining the sanction, the Disciplinary Committee utilised Article 102 of the RFEF Disciplinary Code, which covers violent actions that cause serious injury or harm to an opponent during play. A ban between four and 12 games is associated with the regulation; thus, Owono has received the maximum punishment.

‌



In the wake of the incident, Owono released a statement which said: "These are the most difficult days of my life. I struggle to find the words, and I find it very hard to process what has happened.

View 5 Images Owono has been banned for 12 matches (Image: AP)

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

"I feel enormous pain at the loss of Jesus. I think of him, his family, and all the people who loved him. I know there will be many questions to address.

‌



"I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect. But right now, honestly, I cannot think about anything other than Jesus and the ⁠pain we are experiencing. Rest in ⁠peace, Jesus."

Owono deactivated his social media pages after he received a tidal wave of abuse. FC Andorra defender Lautaro Spatz recently supported his heartbroken teammate, saying: "I would also like to say a few words about my teammate, goalkeeper and friend, who is deeply affected by what has happened.

‌



"Those of us who know him are aware of the sort of person he is, how much he is suffering at this time, and that he would never have intended to harm anyone. In football, there are accidental incidents, but no one could have imagined that one of them could lead to such tragic consequences."

Earlier on Friday, FC Andorra owner Gerard Pique lambasted the RFEF for taking a lengthy period to announce the sanction. He said: "We're traveling with FC Andorra to Almería, where we play tomorrow at 6:30 PM. I wanted to send this video, and it's meant as constructive criticism, so you can see the situation we're in right now as a club.

‌



View 5 Images Tributes were paid to De Miguel across the Champions League games last week (Image: Getty)

"We have three players who were suspended for various reasons on paper for the Tenerife match. One of them is Jesus Owono, then we have Efe Akman with five yellow cards, and also Lautaro de Leon, who was sent off for two yellow cards on the Tenerife match.

‌



"This match took place two weeks ago. We play tomorrow, and even today, the day before the match, we have no confirmation or notification whatsoever that these players are sanctioned by the Federation. In other words, all three - Owono, Lautaro de Leon, and Efe Akman - could play tomorrow.

"I called the president of the RFEF to inform him of this situation and I'm waiting to hear back. We've tried every possible way, through every possible channel, to understand their situation because, of course, if they don't play this match and then tell us they could have played it, they're going to be suspended for another match.

‌



"It's Friday now, we play tomorrow , and we have to get the players traveling. Obviously, Jesus Owono won't be traveling because he's not training , but Efe Akman and Lautaro de Leon are traveling with us.

View 5 Images Tributes were left for Jesus de Miguel (Image: 2026 Getty Images)

‌



"It's Friday, the match is tomorrow, it's been two weeks since the Tenerife game, and we don't know if these players are suspended or not because if the Federation doesn't notify us, it means they can play. We're waiting to see what happens."

While Owono has now learned the length of his ban, it remains unknown as to whether the goalkeeper will return to football. Speaking about his situation, FC Andorra head coach Carles Manso said: "What we have to do is support him in every way and be close to him.

‌



“We will give him space so that he feels completely free to make ‌any ⁠decision, whether he wants to return, when, or if he does not want to return. When he feels it is appropriate and when he feels genuinely ready to take a decision ⁠like that."

Meanwhile, Tenerife, who held a memorial for De Miguel at the Heliodoro Rodríguez López stadium last weekend, have committed to supporting his one-year-old daughter until she turns 18 following his heartbreaking death.

‌



View 5 Images The 30-year-old was laid to rest in his parents' hometown of Navahermosa (Image: 2026 Getty Images)

"We want to be there for her at least until she reaches adulthood," CEO Antonio Manuel Porro Granados told The Athletic.

‌



"This is a commitment we have made at the initiative of our majority shareholder, Rayco Garcia, and one that we all fully support. We will provide the maximum possible support in every respect, beyond what we are legally obliged to provide.

"We are also exploring other ways of increasing the financial support, so that, at least in material terms, the circumstances do not affect their lives quite so much -- although, of course, it is impossible for them not to have an impact."

Article continues below

Reports in Spain claim the family will also receive base compensation of around €360,000 (£300,000) following De Miguel's death.

Sports.title: England hold talks about leaving the pitch vs Spain if they suffer racist abuse
Sports.content:
England hold talks about leaving the pitch vs Spain if they suffer racist abuse

England are playing Spain in Madrid for the first time in 12 years following a shameful night in 2004 where black players were subjected to sickening racist abuse

View 2 Images Ashley Cole was one of the England players subjected to shocking racist abuse in 2004

Thomas Tuchel will remind his England players of UEFA’s anti-racism rules ahead of their Nations League showdown with Spain in Madrid.

‌



‌



It is the first time England will have played a fixture in Madrid since 2004 when the Three Lions' black players were subjected to shocking racist abuse in Real Madrid’s Bernabeu Stadium.

‌



England will be hoping there is no repeat when they play in Atletico Madrid’s Metropolitano Stadium on Sunday. But Tuchel confirmed that he will talk to the squad ahead of the fixtures and remind them of the protocols in place.

‌



England boss Tuchel said: “I still think the protocol is in place and it's important that the players know about the protocol. And then yes, we will give our answers if stuff like this happens. The best answers are on the pitch. I think we had the same discussion before the Serbia game.”

England player ratings in Croatia win as Harry Kane makes history and leads team with 8/10 READ MORE :

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

UEFA’s three step protocol starts with the referee pausing the match for a PA announcement to order the behaviour to stop. The second step is to suspend the game and both sets of players leave the pitch while the final step is to abandon the game.

‌



In November 2004, England players Ashley Cole and Shaun Wright-Phillips were subjected to repeated baiting and monkey chants by large elements of the 60,000 crowd.

Then Prime Minister Tony Blair and the Spanish prime minister José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero both condemned the racist abuse. But the Spanish FA was only fined only £44,750 for the racist chanting.

‌



View 2 Images Thomas Tuchel will remind England players of UEFA's three-step protocol

England played in Spain in 2009 but the FA refused to play the game in Madrid because of the previous issues. It was played in Seville and England have subsequently played in Seville and Alicante with no issues.

‌



But Spain have had high profile issues with Real Madrid star Vinicius Junior subjected to over 20 incidents of racism in Spain over the years.

Tuchel added: “I think it's unacceptable. In any stadium, not even in stadiums, we will never accept racism. We will never be racist towards anyone.

‌

Sports.title: Mauricio Pochettino’s wife dragged into relegation sacrifice as couple went to extreme lengths
Sports.content:
Mauricio Pochettino’s wife dragged into relegation sacrifice as couple went to extreme lengths

Mauricio Pochettino will take charge of Manchester United when the Premier League returns, with the club currently in the bottom three of the table

View 2 Images New Manchester United boss Mauricio Pochettino is not afraid to go to extreme lengths in a relegation fight. (Image: Tiziana FABI / AFP via Getty Images)

New Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino, alongside his wife, have proven that he already has the head for a relegation fight, and is willing to go to extreme lengths to ensure his team survives. The Argentine has signed a two-and-a-half-year contract at Old Trafford, replacing Michael Carrick.

‌



‌



His first game in charge is on 22 November when United travel to take on rivals Liverpool. They go into the Premier League game in the relegation places, with some sensationally claiming they could be in for a fight to beat the drop this season.

‌



While the team will hope to be nowhere near the same position at the end of the season, nothing can be ruled out, given that United have recorded fewer wins than any other team in the league so far. The good news is that a relegation scrap is something Pochettino and his wife have experience with.

‌



Marcus Rashford causes issue as Man Utd set to trigger his team-mate's contract clause READ MORE :

In January 2009, Pochettino took charge of struggling Spanish side Espanyol. With just 10 weeks of the season left, the team were bottom of La Liga, eight points from safety.

It was widely believed that it would take a miracle for the team to escape the drop. So that’s what Pochettino searched for.

As reported by The Guardian at the time, Pochettino, his wife and his assistant manager packed their bags and hiked 12km to Montserrat. It was a pilgrimage to the religious mountain, which is slightly bigger than Mount Snowdon.

‌



View 2 Images Pochettino started his managerial career with Espanyol. (Image: MANUEL QUEIMADELOS/Getty Images)

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



It is also home to the black virgin shrine, which was rescued from looting during the Spanish Civil War. Pochettino is said to have pleaded with the shrine to help his side pull off a miracle and survive relegation.

In their last 10 games of the season, Espanyol produced an incredible turnaround to haul themselves out of the relegation places. They won eight of those games, losing just once to Atletico Madrid, and drawing another.

‌



A 3-0 win over Malaga on the final day of the season saw them secure a 10th-place finish in La Liga. It is known as one of the great escapes in La Liga history and launched Pochettino’s managerial career.

The 54-year-old remained with the club until November 2012. He then made the move to the Premier League with Southampton three months later.

Article continues below

A successful five-and-a-half years with Tottenham was followed by spells with Paris Saint-Germain and Chelsea. Most recently, he managed the USA national side and will take charge of his final two games over the international break before arriving at United.

Sports.title: Marcus Rashford causes issue as Man Utd set to trigger his team-mate's contract clause
Sports.content:
Marcus Rashford causes issue as Man Utd set to trigger his team-mate's contract clause

Mauricio Pochettino has been named as Michael Carrick's successor at Manchester United, and the Argentine will have his work cut out for him when he arrives next week

View 2 Images Marcus Rashford's wage could be an issue at Manchester United (Image: Getty Images)

Marcus Rashford's staggering wages could pose a problem for Manchester United as they look to tie Bruno Fernandes down to a new deal. The Englishman has had a troubled time with the Red Devils over the past couple of years, falling out of favour under Ruben Amorim.

‌



‌



As a result, Rashford was carted out on loan to Aston Villa at the back end of 2025/26, before spending the entirety of last term on loan with Barcelona. While Michael Carrick reintegrated the forward back into the first team over the course of the summer, disaster struck when a hip issue flared up in the opening weeks of the season.

‌



As a result, Rashford has missed United's last six matches while recovering. That hasn't prevented the 29-year-old from collecting a whopping salary - thought to be in the region of £325,000 per week - from his parent club.

‌



Mauricio Pochettino faces immediate Man Utd problem already setting him up for failure READ MORE :

One issue facing United is that Fernandes, widely regarded as the club's best player, does not earn as much as Rashford and has been seeking improved terms for some time. The Sun report that the midfielder is earning £75,000 less than his teammate, but United remain confident they will be able to agree a deal despite seeing two offers rejected in recent times.

Fernandes is out of contract next summer, but United are said to be relaxed about the situation and planning to trigger an automatic one-year extension before the New Year to avoid the 32-year-old being able to strike a pre-agreement with foreign clubs in January.

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



That would also buy the club more time to negotiate with Fernandes, or sell him on in the summer if an agreement cannot be reached. Rashford's lofty wages, meanwhile, could lead to some high demands from the club captain.

It's no secret that there has been interest in Fernandes over the past couple of years, with both Al Hilal and Galatasaray sniffing around his services with lucrative contract offers. However, United have always been firm in their insistence on keeping the midfielder as part of their long-term vision.

‌



Mauricio Pochettino could also play a key part in securing Fernandes on a new deal when he arrives at the Theatre of Dreams next week. United made the decision to sack Carrick on Thursday morning, following a dreadful start to the new season which has left them 18th in the Premier League standings.

Pochettino was quickly snapped up as his successor, with the 54-year-old leaving his post at the United States national team in favour of a return to English soil - having previously thrived with Southampton, Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea.

‌

However, Pochettino will not arrive in Greater Manchester until Thursday, November 18, as a result of staying at the helm of the USMNT for their upcoming quarter-final double-header against Haiti in the CONCACAF Nations League.

The Argentine has his work cut out for him in terms of turning the tide at Old Trafford and will immediately face a daunting trip to rivals Liverpool in his first game in charge before a Champions League fixture away at Sporting CP.

Sports.content:
Man Utd 'complete signing of wonderkid striker' in first move of new era

Manchester United have completed a signing on the same day Mauricio Pochettino was named as the club's new manager

View Image Manchester United have completed a new signing (Image: Getty)

Mauricio Pochettino is not the only new face at Manchester United. The club have also signed 16-year-old England youth international Tyler Adjei.

‌



‌



This week has been a hectic one for United. Michael Carrick was sent packing on Thursday before Pochettino was officially confirmed as his successor on Friday. The Argentine will assume the role on November 18.

‌



But Carrington will welcome another new arrival, with promising young forward Adjei joining from Reading. He is set to link up with Darren Fletcher's Under-18s side and has been registered as a No. 9.

‌



Sources have praised the athletic teenager after United beat a whole host of other top clubs to secure Adjei's services from the League One club.

Michael Carrick breaks silence on Man Utd sacking with emotional open letter READ MORE :

Adjei can play across the front three but United view him as a striker. One source told The Athletic: "He's got an athletic profile. He's got more to come physically.

"He moves well. He has a good temperament, mentality and demeanour. He has a good energy to train. He's got a way to go technically, as is the norm for a player of his age."

‌



Adjei is not yet match-fit and will take some time to settle in Manchester after the registration process between the two clubs concluded.

Fletcher's Under-18s have been in fine form this season. Opening up last month after a 6-0 thrashing of Burnley, the coach shed light on his philosophy to MUTV.

‌



"We play attacking football, I know it is in the club's identity and the DNA," Fletcher said. "We want to play fast, direct, attacking football but there is a lot more controlled possession element, that is just the way football is going these days.

"When you attack quickly, fluidly, get people into the box who make really good decisions. The key to football is decision making, so when we got into the final third, the decision making was brilliant today [against Burnley].

Sports.title: Mauricio Pochettino bursts into tears in first interview after getting Man Utd job
Sports.content:
Mauricio Pochettino bursts into tears in first interview after getting Man Utd job

Mauricio Pochettino was announced as Manchester United's new manager on Friday, with the outgoing USMNT boss explained the decision in an emotional press conference hours later

View 2 Images Mauricio Pochettino became emotional during his press conference ahead of the USMNT's game against Haiti

Mauricio Pochettino was in tears during his first press conference since being unveiled as Manchester United's new head coach as he expressed how difficult it is to leave his role with the United States men's national team.

‌



‌



United confirmed that the 54-year-old had agreed to succeed Michael Carrick at Old Trafford on Friday afternoon, just hours before Pochettino was scheduled to address the United States media in a press conference ahead of their upcoming game against Haiti.

‌



Pochettino cut an emotional figure as he addressed his departure and spoke through tears before taking a moment to compose himself.

‌



He said: “A decision that in some part is a very sad decision and in another part that we are professional and are trying to find the next step, try to make your dreams come true and I think the most important thing is what we leave here. The moment that we shared together, all the things that we accomplished and put in place and the standard that we increase in that foundation.”

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



Pochettino swiftly emerged as the leading candidate to replace Carrick, who was sacked on Thursday after overseeing just one win from 10 Premier League games this season.

Reports outlining that Pochettino and United were close to an agreement were rife prior to Carrick being officially removed from his post and the former Tottenham and Chelsea manager shed some light on the process, which includes an agreement that Pochettino will oversee the double-header against Haiti before starting his new role on November 18.

‌



“We were very transparent,” he said. “ We were talking with the federation. Yesterday when things were positive in the way that the agreement was, we had a meeting and I communicated to the player and the whole staff.

“ The decision is between the federation and Manchester United that we continue with our job in the camp.

‌



View 2 Images Pochettino will bid farewell to the USMNT after a game against Haiti next week (Image: Luke Hales/Getty Images)

“ I think we will have time next week to talk about the job at Manchester United. Now I think it is better to talk about USA soccer and the national team. We have two games ahead and the focus is completely on this.”

‌



Pochettino has agreed a two-and-a-half year contract to take charge at United, who came close to hiring him twice in the past.

Though Pochettino has made no secret of his desire for a Premier League return, he signed a contract extension with the USMNT until 2030 after guiding them to the last 16 of a home World Cup in the summer.

Article continues below

Asked why he signed an extension if he craved a return to Europe, Pochettino replied: “I think it's obvious, I never said that I wanted to go back. They know that there is not too many opportunities can happen in your career like the size of Manchester United. When that arrives it is difficult to turn down that situation.”

Sports.title: Mauricio Pochettino's first job must be getting rid of Bruno Fernandes - he's trouble at Man Utd
Sports.content:
Mauricio Pochettino's first job must be getting rid of Bruno Fernandes - he's trouble at Man Utd

If Mauricio Pochettino wants to succeed at Manchester United, he needs to be bold and kick troublemaker Bruno Fernandes to the curb

View 3 Images Mauricio Pochettino has a big Bruno Fernandes problem (Image: Adam Davy/Press Association)

When Mauricio Pochettino walks through the doors at Manchester United, his to-do list will stretch from Stretford all the way to Buenos Aires. But his first, most urgent task shouldn't require much deliberation.

‌



‌



He needs to call Bruno Fernandes into his office, shake his hand, and tell him to pack his bags for January.

‌



News that Fernandes has turned his nose up at United's latest contract offer this week has sparked an understandable flutter of anxiety within Old Trafford's leaking corridors. With his current deal expiring at the end of the season, albeit with a one-year extension option sitting in United's back pocket, the conventional wisdom says Pochettino must move heaven and earth to keep his captain sweet.

‌



But conventional wisdom at Manchester United has been dead wrong for over a decade. Fernandes isn't the solution to the club's malaise - he's one of its primary carriers.

Mauricio Pochettino's wife had brutal four word reaction after press conference READ MORE :

When will Mauricio Pochettino first take charge of Man Utd and his likely starting XI? READ MORE :

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Of course, the standard defence of the 32-year-old is always the same: Look at his goals and assists. This is the great Fernandes illusion - the soothing myth that because the numbers on his Wikipedia page look healthy, he must be some sort of lone genius propping up a crumbling empire. Take five minutes to actually watch him, though, and the whole thing unravels like a cheap suit.

‌



Strip away the penalty kicks - harvested with that little theatrical hop once the hard work has already been done - and the corners dutifully aimed at Casemiro's forehead, and what are you actually left with? A midfielder who pads his stats when the pressure is off, when the points are already in the bag, or when the stakes couldn't flatter him more.

For nearly seven years, Fernandes' gaudy chance-creation statistics have served as a convenient smokescreen, disguising a fair-weather talisman in a midfield that cannot keep the ball, control the tempo, or hold its shape against halfway-competent opposition.

‌



Worse still, when the roof is caving in, and United desperately need someone to grab a massive fixture by the scruff of the neck and twist it to his will, Fernandes simply evaporates. He doesn't boss big games - he merely attends them as an outraged spectator, hovering on the peripheries like a man furiously disputing an erroneous restaurant bill.

View 3 Images Bruno Fernandes behaviour on and off the pitch has sparked plenty of debate (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Another giant fly in the ointment is how wildly unsuited he is to the tactical regime about to arrive. Pochettino's entire managerial philosophy is built on relentless, lungs-on-fire pressing, synchronised sprinting, and ego-free collective graft. Asking Bruno Fernandes to function inside that kind of disciplined, high-velocity machine is like asking a grumpy cat to enjoy a bubble bath. He can't do it, and - most exhausting of all - he will spend 90 minutes moaning about being asked to try.

And that, really, is the rotting core of the whole enterprise. For all his padded goal contributions, Fernandes is a roaring net negative because of the thick atmospheric poison he pumps into the club. The signature arm-flapping, the theatrical scowls, the slumped shoulders of a wounded martyr. It isn't passion. It's performative con-artistry of the highest order.

‌



Every time Fernandes throws his hands to the heavens after a misplaced pass, he is cynically beaming a coded message to the Stretford End: Look at me. I'm the only one trying. These clowns around me are letting us all down. It's sneaky, deeply self-serving, and faintly villainous. While his team-mates absorb the brickbats raining down from the stands, the skipper stages a one-man pantomime of aggrieved perfection to keep his own halo polished.

We saw the mask slip entirely during his shabby little meltdown with Michael Carrick. Hooked off against Como after a poor performance, Fernandes didn't swallow his pride and take his seat on the bench like a grown-up. He threw his manager straight under the bus, openly slating Carrick's tactics in public with all the petulance of a toddler spitting out lukewarm broccoli.

‌



There was a nauseating whiff of late-stage Cristiano Ronaldo about the whole episode: Look at how I have suffered. I am the most important person in this building, so to hell with the manager, the squad, and the badge.

View 3 Images Bruno Fernandes could cause Mauricio Pochettino a big headache (Image: Omar Vega, Getty Images)

‌



And this, remember, is the man wearing the captain's armband at Manchester United. A club that has spent over a decade drowning in an excuse-making, accountability-free dressing room culture is being led by a chief whinger who actively models the exact behaviour that has ruined them. Instead of whipping slackers into shape, Fernandes legitimises sulking as a leadership style.

Pochettino's greatest trick as a manager has always been alchemy - welding a group of fresh, hungry players into a tight-knit unit where everyone pulls in the exact same direction. Keeping Fernandes around makes that impossible. You cannot build a church while the bell-ringer is setting fire to the pews.

‌



Fortunately, this contract standoff hands United and Pochettino a gift-wrapped escape hatch. With his current deal expiring in June, the temptation among the bean-counters might be to trigger that one-year extension option just to protect his transfer value.

But United must resist the urge. Extending his deal only drags out the soap opera, keeps his gargantuan wages on the books, and chains Pochettino to a mutinous skipper for another 18 months. It would be a triumph of accountancy over common sense.

‌



Instead, they must be ruthless. Stick him in the shop window and sell him in January while someone, perhaps in Saudi Arabia, is still willing to pay good money for him. Rip the armband off, hand it to someone whose first instinct in a crisis isn't to throw a strop, and let Pochettino stamp his authority on the place from day one.

United won't miss Fernandes half as much as the G/A fetishists and YouTube highlight-reel fans will claim. Football isn't played on paper or in Excel columns, and matches aren't won with hollow individual statistics.

Article continues below

Manchester United have spent far too long mistaking a noisy soloist for an orchestra. If Pochettino is to get this broken ensemble playing in harmony, his very first act must be to politely, but firmly, escort the soloist off stage.

Sports.title: McGinn double seals win for ragged Scotland
Sports.content:
Match report as John McGinn scores twice in Scotland's win over North Macedonia at Hampden; Aston Villa midfielder gives hosts lead after McTominay and Gilmour go close; Rastoder's header levels scoring; McGinn penalty seals win after Gannon-Doak fouled; Scotland face Switzerland next

John McGinn's double rescued Scotland as they toiled to a 2-1 win over North Macedonia to keep their Nations League promotion hopes alive.

The hosts were booed off at half-time with the game goalless but there was a sense of relief - rather than joy - at the final whistle after McGinn's penalty secured the three points after Elmin Rastoder's header cancelled out the Aston Villa midfielder's opener.

The win means Scotland can still finish second in Group B1 after Slovenia were held by Switzerland, but will have to win in St Gallen on Monday and hope North Macedonia do them a favour in their final game.

Image: Andy Robertson equalled Sir Kenny Dalglish's appearance record

Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli secured his first win at Hampden on a night when skipper Andy Robertson earned his 102nd cap to equal the appearance record held by Sir Kenny Dalglish.

The returning Scott McTominay nearly grabbed an opener after 16 minutes but he was denied by Stole Dimitrievski in the North Macedonia goal after turning and shooting sharply. The keeper then denied Che Adams and McTominay again before the Napoli midfielder attempted to recreate his famous Denmark overhead kick to no avail.

Boos rang around Hampden as the players trudged off at the interval and Billy Gilmour did little to lift the collective mood straight after the break when he fired over with the goal gaping following good work by Adams.

Image: Scotland's Scott McTominay goes close

Scotland did take the lead soon after, however, Adams outmuscling his North Macedonian counterpart to set the onrushing McGinn away into the box before he curled his effort into the net.

Rastoder stunned Hampden less than three minutes later, leaping highest to glance his header past Angus Gunn from a corner, but Dimitrievski went from hero to villain with a little over 15 minutes remaining, bringing down Ben Gannon-Doak when the winger seemed to be running the ball out of play.

Image: North Macedonia's Elmin Rastoder scored to make it 1-1 against Scotland

A VAR review followed, allowing McGinn to step up and deliver a first win in Glasgow for Pocognoli, but it is a performance that will raise more questions than answers.

The key moments from Hampden Park

16: BIG SAVE! Scott McTominay controls the ball with his back to the goal, then turns sharply and shoots but Stole Dimitrievski gets down well to his left and keeps it out.

22: OVER! Andy Robertson delivers a free-kick into the box but Kieran Tierney's header loops over the bar.

27: SAVE! John McGinn's corner is met by Che Adams at the front post before his header takes a big deflection. It looks like it's heading in but Dimitrievski is equal to it again.

35: OVER! McTominay tries an acrobatic effort with an overhead kick but it sails over the bar and out of play.

39: MCTOMINAY DENIED! The ball is threaded into the feet of McTominay and he shoots from a tight angle but the goalkeeper makes another save to keep it level!

46: HOW HAS HE MISSED?! Adams capitalises on a loose back pass and squares the ball to Billy Gilmour. All he has to do is guide it on target and it is a goal but he skies it over the bar!

54: GOAL! Adams outmuscles the defender before poking the ball forward allowing McGinn to race onto it before curling the opener into the back of the net.

57: GOAL! North Macedonia shock Scotland with a quickfire equaliser. The corner is whipped into the box and Rastoder is there to glance it into the bottom corner.

75: GOAL! McGinn scores from the spot to restore Scotland's lead

Pocognoli 'satisfied' with first home win

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sebastien Pocognoli was pleased after his first home win with Scotland against North Macedonia in the Nations League, hoping that it will 'helps build a winning culture'.

Scotland head coach Sebastian Pocognoli:

"I'm happy to get the first win at home. It's important and we knew before the game that it will help to build a winning culture.

"In terms of what we produced on the pitch, I know exactly what we worked on this week. I'm quite satisfied about what I saw in some moments of the game, the work on the ball and off the ball.

"It was not always perfect, but I know that what we worked on in the last two days happened many times on the pitch. And for me that's very important. On top of that, we created a lot of chances that we should score.

"Off the ball, I think we were quite aggressive. We recovered a number of balls that we managed well in some moments of transition. We created a big chance for Billy (Gilmour) from this also. So that's a new approach of the game. Not everything was perfect, but there was a lot to take to move forward.

Image: Scotland head coach Sebastien Pocognoli was satisfied with the win over North Macedonia

"After the first goal, I think we need to learn to not drop the intensity. Because after the first goal, for five minutes, I really feel like we dropped the intensity and the focus. And we conceded a goal from a set-piece. And I had the same feeling after the second goal. So, it's something that we need to fix."

Robertson: We have to be patient with new style

Scotland captain Andy Robertson speaking to BBC Sport:

"I thought we showed glimpses of good stuff. We tried to be patient on the ball, tried to keep the ball, I think we did that well at times, but also at times it broke down because the quality wasn't there at times so we're still trying to piece it all together.

Image: Andy Robertson says Scotland are adapting to a new style

"It's a different way of playing and that's what we are working on in the training ground. It wasn't always perfect, but no international game is easy and we're all delighted in the changing room to get that win and hopefully other people have a smile on their face too.

"Every formation can be played differently, there are so many different variations of this formation. We're trying to implement what the manager and coaches want us to do on the training ground and we're working really hard.

"Yes, it's not going to be perfect right away but everything is working towards us going into the qualifiers for the Euros. We're still trying to learn it and we believe in what the manager is trying to teach us to do and we have to be patient with that.

"I know people don't see us train and see the work we're doing in the background, so I can get why people are frustrated but there is an idea behind what we are doing and like you say at times we lacked that quality.

Image: Andy Robertson applauds the fans after Scotland's win over North Macedonia

"Obviously the Slovenia at home game made it unrealistic, or tougher [to qualify]. We'll go over to Monday and we'll give everything we can to win that game. We're in a position where we have to rely on other results."

On equaling Dalglish's appearance record: "It feels amazing for me and my family, it's an amazing achievement. I've been around here for a long time. I've had highs, I've had lows, I've sometimes had praise and had criticism."

McGinn praises 'amazing' Robertson

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player John McGinn hails Andy Robertson after he matched Kenny Dalglish’s caps record against North Macedonia.

John McGinn to Sky Sports on Andy Robertson's record-equalling night:

"Amazing - he deserves everything that is coming his way. The biggest credit I can give him is that he is always available, always willing to help his country. Whether he is at 60, 70, 80 per cent, or 100.

"I'm sure Monday will be a special occasion for him but he'll give the boring answer that it will only be special if we get three points."

Analysis: McGinn takes centre stage on record-equalling night for Robertson

It will be a night that Andy Robertson never forgets but a game most Scotland fans will blank from their collective memories fairly quickly.

Image: Andy Robertson and John McGinn celebrate after Scotland's win

The skipper equalled Sir Kenny Dalglish's record of 102 caps but it was fellow Scotland stalwart John McGinn who spared the home side's blushes on a drab evening in Glasgow.

Scotland looked slow in their build-up, even if there were first-half chances, but when the goal finally did come the floodgates did not open. Instead, North Macedonia, who hadn't scored since November 18, 2025, equalised and could have gone in front.

The natives were understandably restless but were ultimately relieved when Stole Dimitrievski clumsily brought down Gannon-Doak, allowing McGinn to be the hero again.

Image: Scotland head coach Sebastien Pocognoli celebrates

The Aston Villa captain was quick to remind everyone that a new style takes time to bed in and that is true. Scotland are moving away from the comforts and success of the Steve Clarke era, but questions will be asked of Pocognoli's insistence on using wing-backs and one upfront at home with a comfortable win expected.

Scotland have something to play for when they travel to Switzerland for their final Group B1 game, with promotion still up for grabs. Robertson should play on Monday to become Scotland's most-capped player outright. How sweet it would be if his 103rd appearance for his country was a winning one.

Sports.title: France put injuries behind them to stun Springboks
Sports.content:
Nations Championship - France 21-19 South Africa: Les Bleus put injuries behind them to hold on and stun Springboks in Paris

Aaron Grandidier-Nkanang was among the try-scorers as France pulled off an epic victory over South Africa

France put a raft of injuries behind them to withstand huge pressure and defeat South Africa 21-19 in a stunning Nations Championship victory in Paris.

The win is only the second for Les Bleus over the Springboks in the last 11 contests, with the hosts playing sensationally in the first half and digging in to survive and get over the line in the second.

Back-three Aaron Grandidier-Nkanang, Théo Attissogbe and Louis Bielle-Biarrey each scored tries in the opening half, with France belying the fact they had to play Antoine Dupont at 10 due to four fly-halves being out injured (Matthieu Jalibert, Romain Ntamack, Thomas Ramos, Antoine Hastoy).

All three tries were converted by Maxime Lucu, with France 21-7 ahead at the half-time break, but the second half proved entirely different.

France 21-19 South Africa - Score summary France - Tries: Grandidier-Nkanang (15), Attissogbe (24), Bielle-Biarrey (32). Cons: Lucu (16,24,33). South Africa - Tries: Wessels (30), Reinach (51), Marx (72). Cons: Feinberg-Mngomezulu (31,52).

Though South Africa were shown a 20-minute red card to back-row Cobus Wiese for an illegal ruck clear-out, France coughed up sin-bins to Lucu, Grandidier-Nkanang and Régis Montagne - the latter as a result of scrum penalties which kept flowing the visitors' way.

Scrum-half Cobus Reinach and hooker Malcom Marx scored tries in the second half for South Africa - adding to a first-half Jan-Hendrik Wessels effort - but Manie Libbok crucially missed the third conversion and the chance to draw level.

Twitter Due to your consent preferences, you’re not able to view this Privacy Options

South Africa's wholesale front-row changes less than an hour before kick-off - swapping their starting front-row for their replacements - had ​little impact on France's fast start, with Dupont floating between fly-half and scrum-half from the off in a marvellous individual performance.

The match was considered a potential preview of the final at Twickenham in two weeks, but while France are closing in on representing the northern hemisphere - England and Ireland are now six points behind with two games to play - South Africa may not make it.

The Springboks will be overtaken atop the southern hemisphere standings and lose their No 1 world ranking if undefeated New Zealand beat Wales on Saturday in Cardiff, as expected.

On Friday, the Springboks closed to 21-14 with 30 minutes to go, revving up their power game for a grandstand finish.

France were bleeding penalties - nine in the scrum alone - but desperate scramble defence roused a packed Stade de France.

South Africa's Pieter-Steph du Toit was held up over the try-line late on, while Lucu - France's goalkicker with an 85 per cent success rate - ramped up the tension when he missed a straightforward penalty attempt that would have given France a 10-point lead.

Springboks hooker Marx inevitably scored from a rolling maul but Libbok, on for Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu, botched the conversion attempt that would have levelled the score with eight minutes left.

The Boks had one last chance in the final minute, but Bielle-Biarrey stopped the charge and Dupont jumped on the loose ball, earning Lucu the chance to kick out and end a gripping Test match.

Dupont: We kept intensity up the whole match - 'That's huge for us'

France fly-half Antoine Dupont told ITV:

"I feel tired! They [South Africa] are really intense during the 80 minutes.

"It was so hard today with the yellow cards. We kept the intensity the whole game, and that's a huge thing for us today.

"We tried to adapt [Dupont at fly-half], we just had one day of training this week.

"I tried with Max [Lucu] to have the best combination possible. In attack and defence.

"With the energy of the entire team, it worked."

What's next?

For France, they next face Argentina in their third Nations Championship Test of the autumn at the Stade de France in Paris on Saturday, November 21 (8.10pm kick-off).

South Africa travel to face Ireland at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin for their next Test, also on Saturday November 21 (4.40pm kick-off).
