What role does the Christian faith play for footballers? What impact is the groundswell of belief having on dressing rooms? And what should teams do when ancient creeds clash with modern culture?

For months, Daily Mail Sport has been speaking with Christian players, chaplains, and academics. We have found that some footballers are still mocked in dressing rooms for their beliefs. We have also heard tales of elite stars praying with non-League journeymen, and of faith sustaining players through injury crises and rescuing them from dark places after their retirement.

Borussia Dortmund midfielder Felix Nmecha attracted controversy in Germany for his 'The King's Return' celebration against Elversberg last Saturday

Manchester City winger Jeremy Doku is one of a growing number of practising Christians in the Premier League

For many players, their beliefs and careers are inextricable. Brentford forward Igor Thiago thinks it was part of God's plan for his father to die so that he would become a footballer and share his beliefs internationally.

'If my father were alive, I do not think I would have become a footballer, because I think he wanted me to be someone else,' Thiago tells Daily Mail Sport. 'It wasn’t until later that I understood there was a purpose for me to come here and be someone else. To be Thiago, who is a footballer, who can speak about God for so many people, in another language.'

Thiago worked as a fruit-carrier, bricklayer, and rubbish collector from the age of 13 in the streets of Gama, Brazil, to provide for his family after his dad passed away. A career in the Premier League was unimaginable back then. Now he is the main man at Brentford and one of several players at the club professing a Christian faith.

And they are not alone in their devotion. Across the top six divisions, 75 per cent of clubs have a Christian in the first team and almost half regularly host Bible studies or prayer meetings, according to a survey of 134 outfits by Christians in Sport.

Their director, Graham Daniels, remembers being told in the 1980s that he was one of just four openly practising Christians in the professional game. An impossible claim to verify, but yes, you read that right, just four. Now you have starting XIs containing more believers than that – and we hear some managers have even been attending church with their squad members. 'There’s a real movement of God within football,' one chaplain at a professional club tells us.

Perhaps God is dwelling in the treatment room, too. Bournemouth winger Ben Gannon-Doak has had three major injuries in his career – to his knee, then quad, then hamstring – and credits his growing faith for helping him recover from each blow.

'With the first, that was before I was strong in my faith – I didn't cope with that one well. I was 17 and felt lost without being on the pitch,' the 21-year-old tells Daily Mail Sport.

'The quad injury, I coped better because I started slowly practising my faith more. When my hamstring injury came, I was closer to God than I had ever been before and I coped with that very easily, it was much easier mentally than the other two. I was able to play in the World Cup after that.

Brentford forward Igor Thiago thinks it was part of God's plan for his father to die so that he would become a footballer and share his beliefs internationally

Arsenal's 'Bible Brothers' are the most famous band of Christian players – around 10 of their stars including 'pastor' Jurrien Timber (left) pray together before matches

'I believe all my injuries happened for a reason and I coped with them the way I did for a reason. I just need to trust God. It makes you stronger, prepares you for things, tests your character. It changes you. Faith has impacted my life in the best way possible.’

Multiple footballers interviewed for this piece cited the Bible verse Philippians 4:13 – 'I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me' – as a key driver in their life. Gannon-Doak has it tattooed on his left arm.

Football has always had crossover with religion – Manchester City and Everton are among the many clubs to have started as church teams, for example – but the past few years have seen it assume more public prominence.

Arsenal's 'Bible Brothers' are the most famous band of Christian players – around 10 of their stars including 'pastor' Jurrien Timber and Noni Madueke pray together in the hotel before matches, and regularly share Bible verses on social media. Organisations such as F3 and Ballers in God, who hold daily prayers and weekly Bible studies, have built Christian fellowship across the divisions.

'Premier League players are on the same call with guys who are semi-pro at step four,' Omar Beckles, a player for League Two Gillingham, tells Daily Mail Sport. 'Lads got together virtually during the pandemic and have been consistently since.' But why the explosion of Christian expression now?

‘An important factor has been the increasing number of players coming from Africa or Latin America, where pentecostalism and other forms of evangelical Christianity are strong,’ Hugh McLeod, Emeritus Professor of Church History at the University of Birmingham, explains to us.

‘Chaplains interviewed for an academic study in 2011 claimed that elite footballers had “a disproportionate passion for the faith” compared with the average member of society, and they saw the players who had come in from other continents as having a big influence on this.’

An earlier generation of Christian players graduating into management positions, as well as a broader shift in Gen Z asking the cosmic questions in life, has opened up football to the tender matters of faith. Group Bible studies, or even stoppages for Muslim players to break their Ramadan fasts, were unheard of until recent years.

'Christians in a changing room can be frowned upon,' says Steven Sessegnon, the Fulham academy graduate who now plays for AFC Wimbledon. He was mocked for being baptised

Marc Guehi was reprimanded by the FA after writing 'Jesus loves you' on Rainbow Laces armbands enforced by the Premier League in support of the LGBTQ+ community

Daniels, who is now a director at Cambridge United, says Christian values have earned players respect in the dressing room – and thinks faith could alleviate the turmoil players face when the final whistle blows on their career.

‘There was tremendous bullying in the 1980s and 1990s, but the more people saw authentic Christianity, the more they realised that it didn’t harm the changing room, but made it better,' he tells Daily Mail Sport. 'Their integrity shone through – players felt if they talked to Christians, they wouldn’t gossip, and they’d be caring, and they wouldn’t be judgmental.

‘In football your identity is achieved. You're as good as your last game. It’s too much pressure for players. That’s why people gamble, drink, and divorce when they retire, because you spent your life having to prove yourself and you don’t know what to do with yourself when you can’t anymore.

'Or think about the academy players who are released at 16. You were the best kid in your class, then your town, your city, your region, the academy system. Then they are released and disappear from the game. Their identity is shot. They feel shame and failure for the rest of their lives.

'If you know your identity and your purpose is a received gift from God, it’s a complete contrast to everything you’ve ever imbibed. He's going to use your highs and lows in sport to draw you closer to Himself. He’s given you this vocation – this is your gift from Him and He loves you.'

Beckles concurs. ‘Being a Christian actually gives you an unfair advantage in football because you’re always living with some form of optimism and hope,’ he tells Daily Mail Sport.

‘You know there’s no despair. Setbacks are an opportunity to improve and go again. When my dad died, I really saw God show up. He granted me a level of peace and grace and joy just to function at that time when I was grieving.’

That said, there is clearly an occasional tension between faith and football, which can bring fame, wealth, and temptations untold. Pele, for example, was very open about his low-maintenance relationship with Christianity's bedroom bylaws.

Meanwhile, Daily Mail Sport has heard of stars who have felt compelled to switch church after becoming Premier League regulars as they had become too recognised and overwhelmed by their original congregation.

City star Antoine Semenyo has a close relationship with pastor John Thompson and was baptised on a beach in Bournemouth last December

Then there's the minefield of political and social issues which footballers are scrutinised over. When playing for Crystal Palace in 2024, Marc Guehi was reprimanded by the FA after writing 'I love Jesus' and 'Jesus loves you' on his Rainbow Laces captain's armband, the wearing of which was enforced by the Premier League in support of the LGBTQ+ community.

And that brings us back to Nmecha. He could have simply pointed to the sky, or made a sign of the cross, when celebrating against Elversberg last Saturday. It wasn’t his expression of faith, but rather the specific King’s Return action associated with Ballers in God, which riled a certain crowd. No matter that other players, such as Nottingham Forest's Jair Cunha, have deployed the celebration without incident. Klopp says that after their talks, Nmecha will not be repeating it. Dortmund executives will be breathing a sigh of relief.

The website for The King’s Return campaign initially linked to a live counselling chat run by conservative evangelical organisation Groundwire. There, counsellors espoused the beliefs that homosexuality is sinful and abortion is ‘Satan’s plan’. When Daily Mail Sport investigated the chat service, we were met with similar views.

It is not fully clear if Ballers in God agree with Groundwire, or if their members even assume a uniform theological position on such issues, but the network celebrated the scrapping of the Rainbow Laces initiative by the Premier League last year. They appear to have removed the link to the Groundwire chat in the wake of the Nmecha controversy. Daily Mail Sport made repeated requests for an interview with founder Bostock, who has been described as ‘hard to pin down’ and a ‘busy man’, but was turned down.

While high-profile incidents are a PR headache for clubs, there is no need for contrasting moral codes to disrupt a team’s cohesion. ‘You might not agree with someone, but you can respect them and treat them in a non-discriminatory way,’ says Dr Keith Parry, Principal Academic in Sport at Bournemouth University.

‘We’ve had openly gay players and referees at the top level in rugby. It is strange that men’s football is different, but questions around sexuality and inclusion go deeper than religion.

‘There are so many barriers (to players potentially coming out) such as toxic masculinity, fans making homophobic remarks, and so on. There are a lot of Middle Eastern and conservative North American owners in football – how might that impact on inclusion? It depends on the owner.’

Beckles, who has represented 14 clubs, believes Christian players have a duty to let love rather than division shine through. ‘Footballers are constantly in a world where there’s someone not far from them who will want something from them. Their manager and fans want them to perform, people want their signature, people want them to give them money, their agent wants commercial growth,' he tells us.

Bournemouth and Scotland star Ben Gannon-Doak (right) has the verse 'I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me' tattooed on his left arm

The young winger credits his faith with helping him through three major injuries

'It’s nice to meet someone that doesn’t want anything from them and genuinely cares for them eternally. That level of love should set people apart.'

Despite dressing rooms becoming more tolerant of faith, some players still face derision. 'Christians in a changing room can be frowned upon or mocked,' says Steven Sessegnon, a player for League One side AFC Wimbledon, who was taunted after being baptised while at a previous club.

'You hear some real nasty things. Some boys don’t understand, which we give them grace for. What scares me the most is why people get so worked up about footballers who are believers.

‘We’re not bothering anyone. We’re going about our business in a loving and caring way. It really rubs people the wrong way and it can cause arguments inside the changing room. One boy was told he will never play because he’s too soft, because he’s a Christian.'

On matchday, faith is increasingly visible and impacts how players go about their business. The temples are not always glamorous – we hear that some players have even met in the sanctuary of a broom cupboard to squeeze in prayer. Clubs offer what they can. At League One Plymouth, they take the analysis suite – at Arsenal, they have a multi-faith prayer room. Across the pyramid, prayers often ask for protection from injury and the chance to glorify God – but not for a win.

At Championship Charlton, six to eight players read the scriptures and pray together. 'They have God-given talents and want to use them as an act of worship,' says club chaplain Matt Baker, who is also on hand at the training ground on Fridays to pray with players. 'When you see players do the sign of the cross after scoring a goal, they see it as evangelistic, but it's also expressing to God that I'm doing this for you, for your glory.'

At Exeter City in League Two, chaplain George Baker tries to spread the love around the club. 'I'll do the rounds of the stadium and chat to the stewards and grounds staff,' he says. 'It's a great opportunity to value the people who are making matchday happen.’

Beckles says that religious considerations even factor on the field. 'How do you live with a level of integrity when you want to win? It’s winning in the right way. The “dark arts” are really difficult to navigate,’ he tells Daily Mail Sport, and he is not the only player to express this feeling to us.

'Being a Christian actually gives you an unfair advantage in football because you’re always living with some form of optimism and hope,' says Omar Beckles (right)

‘In my heart of hearts, I’d like to think I wouldn’t dive to win a penalty – that’s deception. I try my best not to do any of that. But there is the heat of the moment that exposes our nature.’

Gannon-Doak adds: ‘Players losing their temper, starting fights, that's the stuff I try to avoid. But some of the dark arts, that’s just part of the game.’

A popular Christian slogan since the 1890s goes as follows: ‘What would Jesus do?’ Typically it is applied to quandaries in a believer’s life – how to treat somebody who has seriously wronged you, for instance.

Not as often has it been wondered: ‘Would Jesus go down if a sweaty centre-back tugged his shirt in the penalty box in the 90th minute?’ But the next time you catch a game, you might just catch an athlete wrestling with that kind of question. What would you do?

To read more about the relationship that Brentford players have with their faith, see here.

Sports.title: Arsenal star Max Dowman smashes Jude Bellingham's record - but a less-familiar name should catch Thomas Tuchel's eye ahead of Euro 2028: THINGS WE LEARNED from England U21's defeat to Portugal
Sports.content:
Max Dowman smashed Jude Bellingham's record on an icy cold night in Bristol to become the youngest player to ever play for England's Under-21s.

The 16-year-old was sent on with 30 minutes to go by Lee Carsley in a move that energised an Ashton Gate crowd that went home frustrated after a 1-0 defeat inflicted by Afonso Moreira's first half goal.

But this was to be Dowman's night, smashing the previous record set by Bellingham when he made his England Under-21 debut against Kosovo in 2020 aged 17 years, two months and six days old. Dowman does not turn 17 until December 31.

Under-21s boss Lee Carsley has been keen long before this international break to try to shield Dowman from the weight of expectation.

But on he came, replacing the lively Amario Cozier-Duberry with a smile on his face and a quiet confidence that he didn't take long to show off, bursting past two Portuguese markers before four huddled together to gang up on him.

Breaking records is nothing new to a player that already holds one for being the Premier League's youngest-ever goalscorer, thanks to his goal against Everton last season.

Max Dowman wrote his name into the record books once more, playing for England Under-21s

Dowman came on to rich applause on a cold night in Bristol to shatter Jude Bellingham's record

The Arsenal teenager was lively playing off the right as he now targets the 2027 U21 Euros

Dowman is both the youngest player to ever win the Premier League and his outing in the Champions League against Slavia Prague last season saw the then-15-year-old become the youngest-ever player to appear in that competition.

MAX DOWMAN IS THE YOUNGEST... Champions League player Premier League goal scorer Premier League starter Premier League winner Arsenal scorer Arsenal starter Arsenal u18 player Arsenal u21 player Arsenal u21 scorer Premier League 2 player UEFA Youth League scorer England u17 player England u17 scorer England u19 player England u19 scorer England u21 player

By the time next summer's European Championships, which England will attempt to win for a third successive time, rolls around, rising star Dowman could well have earned the right to be this team's main man.

'We've only got three games left before the Euros [next summer],' Carsley explained.

'So it's important that he puts himself in the shop window to be on the plane.

'It's important that he keeps playing well, getting minutes, showing a really good attitude, like he has done.

'I thought he was outstanding when he came on tonight. I thought all of the subs made a real impact.

'I thought Max was unlucky not to get an assist... he made a great pass to Mikey Moore.

'He took up some really good positions, both in the 10 and out wide, he's got a big future ahead.'

His immense talent was one reason why Arsenal sent Ethan Nwaneri, who Dowman played alongside for part of his cameo, to Marseille on loan, and then similarly to Borussia Dortmund, eager not to block the 16-year-old's pathway.

Carsley knows the diamond he has on his hands and will want to take great care in helping polish a player that this crowd, this England team and this management group know has genuine world class potential.

THE REDEMPTION ARC

Speaking of Nwaneri, this felt like a big camp for him. A big camp in the sense that he's falling down the pecking order at Dortmund and is back with a manager that has been so vital in his development.

Nwaneri was part of that 2025 group that won the Euros in front of Thomas Tuchel and he'll have seen the likes of Elliot Anderson and Alex Scott kick on to get to the seniors.

As previously mentioned, Nwaneri was moved out of the way by Arsenal to aid Dowman's development, not an easy pill for a player as talented as he is to stomach when his own development journey is at such a critical juncture given he is, to the surprise of many, still only 19.

'I think we have to remember his age as well,' Carsley added when asked about Nwaneri by Daily Mail Sport.

'He's very young is Ethan and he's another one that we've got a lot of hope for. He's got a lot of potential.'

Ethan Nwaneri was pushed to the side at Arsenal to benefit Dowman but England is different

Lee Carsley has been a crucial figure in the development of Nwaneri and this camp was timely

It was telling that even when Dowman came on, even with the groundswell of excitement at his introduction, it was Carsley's call to keep Nwaneri in his preferred No 10 position with Dowman slotting in on the right.

Nwaneri has only started four games on loan at Dortmund this season and has not managed a single start in the Champions League.

His close control, his quick burst over five yards and the fluidity of his movement was a timely reminder that yes, Dowman is the rising star everyone came out to see, but Nwaneri won't get pushed to the side again without a fight.

THE RISING STAR

Amario Cozier-Duberry is a name not all will be familiar with but come next summer, with the Euros in his sights and promotion to the Premier League on the agenda with Middlesbrough, that could all be about to change.

The 21-year-old has had to be very patient, waiting until last month to make his debut at this level after years of finding himself overlooked.

Here, in what was just his third Under-21 appearance, he showed over the course of 61 minutes why the days of being looked past should be over.

One of the big frustrations in the FA right now at Under-21 level is the lack of touchline wingers. Rio Ngumoha, still only 18, has never been capped at the level and has instead been catapulted into the first team, while many, like Ethan Nwaneri, prefer playing inside.

'The more we can get our wide players one v one the better,' Carsley said. 'I think sometimes we leave them isolated and the opposition are able to double up on them.

Amario Cozier-Duberry is not a household name at international level but his talent is immense

'It's important that our game plan can't just be to get the ball wide and hope for the best.'

Dowman, on in place of Cozier-Duberry is a 10, rather than a right winger which is where he came on, and so a player like Cozier-Duberry, who is on loan at Middlesbrough from Brighton & Hove Albion, is worth his weight in gold.

Here in Bristol he was routinely drawing two defenders and at times three; Portugal knew full well how a quick flip-flap of the ball, or one clipped pass over the top, was enough for the Englishman to take the top off the back-line.

His loan at Bolton Wanderers last season complicated an international journey that has seen him play at Under-16, Under-17, Under-18, Under-19 and Under-20 level, but that's all in the past.

England need a genuine, pacy threat out wide if they are to win a third straight Euros. Cozier-Duberry showed here exactly why he should be it.

Sports.title: Antoine Dupont is still France's Captain Fantastic as skipper spearheads famous victory for Les Bleus over South Africa and mischief-making Rassie Erasmus
Sports.content:
Antoine Dupont masterminded a famous French victory over double world champions South Africa and in the process hurt England’s Nations Championship hopes.

Fabien Galthie’s Les Bleus defied a catastrophic injury list of a mammoth 25 players to get revenge on the Springboks for their 2023 World Cup quarter-final defeat.

Captain fantastic and star man Dupont led France in totemic fashion in what was a game for the ages, the final result not helping England’s chances of topping the northern pool.

Dupont was named to start as an emergency No 10. As if things weren’t bad enough for Les Bleus already, they lost star hooker Julien Marchand in the warm-up. Dupont wore No 10, but played at scrum-half.

Maxime Lucu, meanwhile, was named No 9, but was at fly-half. Rassie Erasmus was up to his old tricks. He changed South Africa’s whole starting front row pre-game. A yellow card for Springbok lock Lood de Jager – sent off in this game last year – allowed Aaron Grandidier-Nkanang and Theo Attissogbe to put the hosts 14-0 up.

Jan-Hendrik Wessels’ close-range effort got South Africa on the board, but Louis Bielle-Biarrey made it three for the French. Erasmus responded by bringing on his front row which had been due to start.

France captain Antoine Dupont was on typically blazing form to lead France to an all-important victory against South Africa

The Springboks' head coach Rassie Erasmus took the opportunity to try and outfox Les Bleus with his late selections - but the plan failed

Lucu then saw yellow, but Kurt Lee-Arendse’s attempt at narrowing the South African deficit was ruled out for him being offside. Springbok No 8 Jasper Wiese was initially sin binned for a dangerous tackle before the incident was upgraded to a 20-minute red card.

Grandidier-Nkanang then became the fourth player to see yellow, Cobus Reinach getting South Africa on the comeback trail. Under relentless Springbok scrum pressure and after being warned for poor discipline, France were fortunate not to receive a third yellow.

But after holding their opponents up over the line, Lucu missed with a long-range penalty. Eventually, Italian referee Andrea Piardi had seen enough at the scrum and sent French prop Regis Montagne for a 10-minute break. Malcolm Marx then made it three tries each, but Manie Libbok’s missed kick meant France hung on and jumped for joy at the final whistle.

Sports.title: Kevin De Bruyne to leave Napoli 'the sooner the better', his wife announces: Man City legend, 35, desperate to quit his 'not nice existence' after rows with team-mates, bosses and fan issues
Sports.content:
Kevin De Bruyne to leave Napoli 'the sooner the better', his wife announces: Man City legend, 35, desperate to quit his 'not nice existence' after rows with team-mates, bosses and fan issues

Kevin De Bruyne's wife Michelle has opened up on her family's struggles in Naples and desire to move back home to Belgium one day.

De Bruyne, 35, joined Napoli in the summer of 2025 after leaving Manchester City following a legendary ten-year spell.

But things haven't gone to plan in Italy, with De Bruyne struggling for fitness in his first season, while he also clashed with former boss Antonio Conte.

The situation hasn't improved much this time around under Max Allegri as Napoli currently sit 10th in Serie A, and reports broke earlier this season that the Belgian midfielder was involved in a dressing room bust-up with team-mates.

And De Bruyne's wife Michele, who he married in 2017, reflected on the turbulence in an interview with Belgian magazine NINA back in September.

'Of course, we think about the future together,' he said. 'And increasingly often, we say to each other: "We are going to live here in Limburg. The sooner we get here, the better".'

Kevin De Bruyne's wife Michelle has opened up on her family's struggles living in Naples

De Bruyne moved to Napoli in the summer of 2025 after a glittering 10 years at Manchester City

Limburg is a province in Belgium, and although Michelle insisted that she thought Naples was a beautiful place to live with great weather and food, she spoke about the toll that life in Italy has had on her partner and their three children, Mason, Rome and Suri.

'Kevin leads a very restricted life in Napoli,' she added. 'It's not much fun for him. Besides, we can't do anything together as a family in the city. That's the other side of the coin, isn't it?

'In Manchester, it was different. Where we lived, people had seen us so often that it wasn’t special anymore. We could walk out the door there without a single photo being taken. In Naples, that is impossible.'

She later added: 'At a certain point, football is no longer the priority. You have achieved everything, done everything. Why would you then turn your children’s lives upside down?'

De Bruyne, who is one of the highest paid players in Italy, signed a two-year contract when he arrived at Napoli but it wasn't certain that he would make it into the second part of that deal in the summer.

Reflecting on his first year ahead of the World Cup, De Bruyne insisted he was 'happy' that Conte had departed.

'Obviously it was difficult for me because Conte has a very different vision of football to mine,' De Bruyne said.

'In truth, I never had the opportunity to play in my preferred position. In any case, I always tried to give my all for the team. We played very defensively. If you try to win every game by a one-goal margin with a 4-5-1 formation, you play a certain type of football.

De Bruyne signed a two-year deal at Napoli and is unlikely to extend his time in Italy

'At the start of the season, we sat back even deeper. Our centre-forward scored just 10 goals, so you know the statistics are not going to be great…'

He later added: 'For me, yes (I'm happy Conte has gone). As far as I am concerned, he was not obliged to stay. There were promises made last summer on the way that we would be playing, but at the end of the day not much of it happened.

'I found that a pity. Football needs to be enjoyable, and unfortunately, I found that aspect lacking.

'There’s no point beating around the bush, we have different visions of football. I never got to play in my position under Conte.'

Sports.title: Goalkeeper involved in fatal collision with Spanish footballer Jesus de Miguel given 12-MATCH ban - and may never return to football
Sports.content:
Goalkeeper involved in fatal collision with Spanish footballer Jesus de Miguel given 12-MATCH ban - and may never return to football

The goalkeeper involved in the collision that killed Spanish footballer Jesus de Miguel has been hit with a 12-match ban - but may never play again.

FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono has been sanctioned after a horrifying foul with Tenerife's De Miguel earlier this month.

Owono was sent off and the match was abandoned with De Miguel, 30, admitted to intensive care, where he later died.

The goalkeeper was subjected to chants of 'murderer' by Tenerife supporters and retreated from public view amid the significant backlash.

Now his manager Carles Manso has said: 'We will ​give him space so that he feels completely free to make ‌any ⁠decision, whether he wants to return, when, or if he does not want to return.

'When he feels it is appropriate and when ​he feels genuinely ready to take a ​decision ⁠like that [he will do so].

Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono has been banned for 12 games and could quit football for good after he collided with Tenerife's Jesus De Miguel, who died

The striker was struck in the chest by Owono's flying knee as the keeper attempted to clear the ball near the halfway line

De Miguel was rushed to hospital following the incident after appearing motionless on the pitch

'What we have to do is support him in every way and be close to ​him.'

Earlier this month, Owono issued a statement describing his 'enormous pain' following the tragic on-field collision.

Owono said: 'These are being the most difficult days of my life. I am struggling to find the words and find it very difficult to assimilate anything that has happened.

'I feel an enormous pain for the loss of Jesús. I think of him, his family, and everyone who loved him. I know there will be many issues to address; I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect.

'But right now, honestly, I cannot think of anything else except Jesús and the pain we are experiencing. Rest in peace, Jesus.'

The tragedy occurred as the game entered the seventh minute of stoppage time, when De Miguel looked set to race away on the counter-attack for Tenerife in search of a winner.

As he watched a long ball drop into his path, the striker was struck in the chest by Owono's flying knee as he attempted to clear the ball near the halfway line.

After initially rolling around on the floor, De Miguel became motionless, and medical staff rushed onto the pitch to attend to him.

Police are investigating the death of De Miguel due to protocol, and they are also now probing the emergency medical response

Owono said he could not 'think of anything else except Jesús and the pain we are experiencing' (Source: Instagram/Jesus Owono)

Tenerife striker De Miguel died in the morning following the horrifying clash with Owono

Owono was initially given a red card for the challenge before the decision was soon taken by the referee to abandon the fixture.

De Miguel was seen to for over five minutes while his team-mates were visibly distressed, with some appearing to be in tears.

The stadium had been in complete silence while De Miguel was being treated, but as he was taken off the pitch the striker was given a standing ovation by the crowd.

He had become a father just last year, and according to El Espanol, his wife and baby daughter were watching in the stands as the fatal incident occurred.

After being taken to an ambulance on a stretcher, there is believed to have been an approximate 15-minute wait before they made their way to the hospital.

De Miguel is believed to have suffered a cardiac arrest while being transported to hospital and had to be revived inside the ambulance, according to Spanish media outlet Marca.

Spanish newspaper AS reported that De Miguel's team-mates had travelled to hospital after he had been taken to intensive care.

In a statement, CD Tenerife confirmed the striker's death, saying: 'Broken with pain, with a lump in our throat and unable to believe that this is true, from CD Tenerife we communicate the tragic death, this Tuesday, November 3, 2026, at 8:00 a.m., of Jesus de Miguel Alameda.'

Tenerife stated: 'We are with his devastated family, with his loved ones, with all the people of Tenerife who today mourn this cruel outcome'

'There are no words of comfort; there is absolutely nothing to mitigate this feeling full of sadness.

'We are with his devastated family, with his loved ones, with all the people of Tenerife who today mourn this cruel outcome.

'The family of Jesus de Miguel is grateful for each and every one of the expressions of support received, and also requests, from the bottom of its heart, maximum respect for his privacy, in these terrible moments.'

Sports.title: Dubai T100 Triathlon: Georgia Taylor-Brown eyes top spot as finale nears
Sports.content:
Dubai T100 Triathlon: Georgia Taylor-Brown eyes top spot as finale nears

The Manchester triathlete is just three points off leader Julie Derron with two races remaining

View 2 Images Georgia Taylor-Brown celebrates victory in Spain

Georgia Taylor-Brown wants to seize top spot in the T100 Triathlon standings by claiming victory in Dubai, ahead of next month’s Grand Final in Qatar.

‌



‌



Taylor-Brown is just three points behind current leader Julie Derron with two races to go, and the pair are set to go head-to-head in Dubai in search of a slim advantage before the Grand Final, where double points are on offer.

‌



The Manchester-born triathlete has already tasted victory this season in Pamplona back in May before finishing third behind Derron and compatriot Kate Waugh in Vancouver three months ago. The 32-year-old is laser-focused on returning to the top of the podium and feels in good shape to do just that in Dubai.

‌



“I'm definitely thinking about the result here,” she said. “It would be nice to lead into the Grand Final, or at least be a little bit closer. There's a few points between me and Julie, so I would like to slim that down a little bit, if not be in front of her.

“Let's see where I'm at. We've still got the two races to go, so things can still happen but I do feel physically and mentally like I'm in a really good place. I'm still super motivated.”

View 2 Images Julie Derron claimed victory in Dubai in 2025

‌



Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources

The race in Dubai could shape up to be another battle between the top three from Vancouver, with Derron the one to beat after her victory in Canada.

‌



Derron was the winner in Dubai last year en route to finishing second overall, and the Swiss star knows she cannot start thinking about the Grand Final in Qatar if she wants to go one better this time around.

“I want to do well, but I see this race as an individual race,” said Derron. “I do this one, I check it off, and then I look towards the next one.

‌



“I can't control where Georgia [Taylor-Brown] ends up. If I beat her, that's an advantage for me but if she beats me, that's good for her. I think it will be exciting until the end of the year.”

A third threat to the title in Dubai could well be 2025 champion Kate Waugh, after her impressive second-place finish in Vancouver. Waugh’s early season has been beset by injuries, meaning she sits 10th in the overall standings, but the 27-year-old wants to continue to compete at the sharp end of races even if the overall title may be out of reach.

‌



She said: “I think I'm in pretty good shape now. I've managed to put together a good few weeks of training. I'm pretty happy with where I'm at. I kind of let go of the title chase a long time ago, so I just want to come and put down the best possible result.”

Usman Nurmagomedov sentenced to six months in prison for Merab Dvalishvili attack READ MORE :

Darragh O'Keeffe ruled out of Cheltenham with abdominal injury after Thurles fall READ MORE :

On the men’s side, reigning champion Hayden Wilde will look to continue his control of the overall standings. The Kiwi sits 38 points clear at the top courtesy of wins in France and Singapore, and a third win of the season would give him a huge advantage heading to Qatar.

‌



Wilde is set for a busy weekend as he takes on the World Triathlon Championship Series (WTCS) Abu Dhabi Sprint race on Friday ahead of the weekend’s T100 contest but the born competitor is embracing a hectic schedule of racing.

“I’m looking forward to getting back to racing,” said Wilde. “I enjoy coming to Dubai to train and race. There’s a chance to have a crack at both the WTCS Abu Dhabi and Dubai T100, so I’m all in. Doing the shorter race first should help. On the French Riviera last year it was the other way around.”

Article continues below

Wilde faces competition from German duo Rico Bogen and Mika Noodt, with the latter keen to bounce back from a crash in July. Noodt collided with an ambulance in Swansea while leading the IRONMAN 70.3 in Wales but avoided a head-on collision and has fought his way back to the Dubai start line.

He said: “I'm back to normal training and also back to a normal training routine, and that definitely helps. I don't feel like an injured guy again doing rehab all the time, but feel like an athlete again. That's why I'm just excited to get out there and race.”

Sports.title: Man City guilty verdict could impact transfer plans as banks 'shy away' from lending
Sports.content:
Man City guilty verdict could impact transfer plans as banks 'shy away' from lending

Manchester City are nervously awaiting the outcome of their appeal after being found guilty of flouting the Premier League's financial rules, but they are already experiencing impacts

View 2 Images Manchester City may struggle to get financing for transfers (Image: Dave Howarth - CameraSport via Getty Images)

Manchester City could find financing transfers more difficult in the wake of their guilty verdict, with reputational damage already taking hold.

‌



‌



City were found guilty in September of breaking the Premier League's financial rules over a nine-year period. An independent commission found them guilty of 114 of the 115 charges levelled against them, finding they had used "sham" contracts to disguise funding of more than £830million.

‌



City have always protested their innocence and they have appealed against the verdict. It emerged on Friday that their appeal would be heard in December, with the verdict then due in the New Year.

‌



But despite the process still playing out, the club are already experiencing some negative impacts, which could affect their plans for the upcoming transfer windows. City spent around £450million on transfers in the summer, splashing out to sign Elliot Anderson and Enzo Fernandez among others.

FOLLOW OUR MAN CITY FB PAGE! Follow our Manchester City Mirror Football Facebook page

‌



Yet their ability to spend big in the future could be hindered by banks' refusal to help finance deals. Bloomberg reports that banks are 'starting to shy away' from deals involving City while they await the outcome of their case.

It is reported that banks have been advancing money to clubs selling players to City, but are reticent to do so now due to reputational damage and potential credit risk.

‌



City could be relegated from the Premier League, hit with a significant points deduction, fined or slapped with a transfer ban in the wake of the bombshell verdict. Meanwhile, The Independent Football Regulator could strip the club from City's owners, the Abu Dhabi United Group.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



View 2 Images Elliot Anderson joined Man City for £116m in the summer (Image: Mark Cosgrove/News Images/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Bloomberg reports that City have already experienced the cold shoulder from banks after German lender Oldenburgische Landesbank AG pulled out of a deal to help finance the £34m signing of Allan from Palmeiras in the summer. Had it gone ahead, Brazilian side Palmeiras would have received an up-front payment from the bank secured against future transfer fees.

‌



The process, called transfer receivables, benefits both clubs and banks, but could become off limits to City, depending on the outcome of their appeal. Man City chief executive Ferran Soriano is convinced they will be cleared.

"The whole Premier League case against us is based on a single false accusation - that the owners' personal money was somehow and secretly put into the club via some sponsors from Abu Dhabi. This is just not true," he said in a video message to staff in early October.

Article continues below

"Irrefutable evidence has been provided to the Premier League commission that shows that it could not happen and that it did not happen. This includes bank statements, money transfers, witnesses and everything necessary to categorically demonstrate that the money did not come from the owner. Every other false charge that has been thrown at us - and aggressively marketed and promoted - comes from the simple, central, and completely false accusation."

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel warns England can’t repeat Argentina mistake if they want to beat Spain
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel wants his England players to prove they are winners - against a team which “has forgotten how to lose.”

England face the ultimate test in the Metropolitano Stadium on Sunday because world champions Spain are on a record-breaking 43 game unbeaten run.

Spain have already beaten England in the Nations League at Wembley but the rematch in Madrid has now become a winner-takes-all to top the Group. Tuchel believes England must go out with an attacking mindset and a belief they can beat Spain if they play to their own strengths.

But it is also about having the confidence they can beat the best and lay down a marker for the future that England can win against top opposition.

‌



England boss Tuchel said: “It's a massive stadium, it's a massive occasion. It's a team that has forgotten how to lose, so of course it requires a top performance first of all, and if we can deliver this performance, it will give us a big boost.

England hold talks about leaving the pitch vs Spain if they suffer racist abuse READ MORE :

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

“It's not a must-win game if you go to Spain. But I think the mindset is important that we got the win today to have this match would feel very, very different if not.

“So that is the first step, and now it's important that we play with the same mindset that we played at home, and attack them and try to make it a physical game, and try to impose our strength. I think that's what we want to see.

‌



“And then you can never predict the result in football, never. But it's important that we show the mindset that you speak of and the spirit, and we will. I'm very confident about that.”

England enjoyed a brilliant World Cup campaign until their undoing against Argentina in the semi-final when they retreated back into themselves and surrendered.

View 3 Images The world champions are on a 43-match unbeaten record

But since then, England beat France in the third-place play-off, lost to Spain at Wembley 3-2 but then beat Czech Republic, thrashed Croatia 7-0 in Rijeka and then beat Slaven Bilic’s side again at Wembley on Thursday night.

‌



Tuchel believes England have “come a long way since the summer” and have now set up the final that he wanted. It makes it a big pressurised occasion.

“Push our limits. See where we are,” said Tuchel. “We all feel that we deserved more in the first game, so we want to take it back in the second.

“I think we're there, and I think we're ready to to win on Sunday. I know what it takes, and like no one can ever guarantee it, but I think it's it's the moment to check how far we are and to push our limit and proof of concept.”

View 3 Images England suffered World Cup heartache after retreating in the semi final vs Argentina (Image: Julian Finney/FIFA via Getty Images)

‌



Tuchel also believes while Spain are daunting, they are not unbeatable. It was competitive at Wembley. Harry Kane missed a penalty at 2-1. It was there for England.

Tuchel added: “It took us a while in that game, and we had maybe the worst start that you can have going 1-0 down against a team full of confidence. But once we got our energy going and played with this for the equaliser, we were strong.

“Had a very good second half, and strangely enough, Harry missed the penalty, and it was maybe the key moment for us because we were very strong then and deserved to be 3-1 up. It would have been very difficult to come back against us on that day.

“We had too many big individual mistakes in our own half on the night. But honestly, if you deeply look into the matches, even of Spain, they had some crucial ball losses against Croatia. They got away with it.

‌

"They conceded some big, big chances against Croatia, and still managed to win the game in the end. So no one is unbeatable.

“We need a top performance, and we're full of confidence, and we're getting there. I think it's exactly what we wanted, and we feel that we have something to take that we that we lost the last time.”

Sports.title: 5 biggest issues Mauricio Pochettino will immediately face after arriving at Man Utd
Sports.content:
"We are trying to make our dreams come true."

Mauricio Pochettino burst into tears in his first interview since it was confirmed he would be swapping the United States for Manchester United.

"I never said I wanted to go back but they know there aren't too many opportunities that happen in your career like Manchester United," he said while explaining his decision. "When it arrives, it's difficult to turn down."

Pochettino has always wanted the United job. He'd been interviewed three times for it previously. Now he's finally got his wish, but the mess the club finds itself in following the sacking of Michael Carrick means it will be anything but straightforward.

Here Mirror Football assesses the most pressing concerns facing the Argentine before he arrives in Manchester next week, with just a few days to prepare for a trip to Anfield.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

1. His new bosses

Pochettino likely still has that new job glow. He presumably has a high opinion of the people who believe he's the man for the job. But that perception will soon change because Manchester United are a shambles behind the scenes.

Director of football Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada have come under intense scrutiny from supporters recently, having presided over some shambolic decision-making. But they are not the only culprits.

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

View 5 Images Sir Jim Ratcliffe, Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox are responsible for much of the mess (Image: Jacob King/Press Association)

Sir Jim Ratcliffe is the minority shareholder, but it is he who has the final say on decisions after the Glazer family ceded control of sporting operations to INEOS when they took over two and a half years ago. That has created a muddied picture behind the scenes, with reports of friction surfacing amid their dreadful start to the season.

Pochettino is currently viewed in a very good light by his employers, but in order to be a long-term success at Old Trafford, he will need more than that: a football manager, a politician and a diplomat all rolled into one.

2. Fractured dressing room

As is often the case towards the end of a manager's tenure, the dressing room becomes leakier. But we didn't even need discreet briefings to learn the feelings of some key players, with Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martinez letting us know in public interviews.

Ex-United boss Erik ten Hag recently said there was a "toxic culture" inside the dressing room during his spell in charge due to players like Cristiano Ronaldo, Casemiro and Raphael Varane having too much influence. It is easy to see comparisons with the current crop.

Another issue is that, despite their miserable results, Carrick left with plenty of lingering goodwill from the players. His "casual" approach - as Roy Keane put is last weekend - may have been problematic, but it also made him popular among the players. Pochettino now has to win them over.

View 5 Images Manchester United's players will need picking up (Image: Ed Sykes/Getty Images)

3. Leaky defence

United are 18th in the Premier League with eight points from 10 games, so there are obviously multiple issues on the pitch. But the most glaring is undoubtedly in defence, where they have been embarrassing at times.

One clean sheet all season, which came against Sabah. Thirty goals conceded in all competitions - the joint most of any side in Europe's top five leagues along with Crystal Palace and Sassuolo.

Pochettino has to start from the back. He is known for stressing the need for top-level fitness in order to implement his high-intensity pressing game. But he needs to sort out the basics first and foremost.

View 5 Images Manchester United's defence has been their biggest issue this season

For a team boasting experienced players like Martinez, Harry Maguire and Luke Shaw, there has been a distinct lack of leadership. Senne Lammens isn't a vocal presence in goal. The expensively-assembled new-look midfield isn't protecting the back four. And, as the inexplicable errors by Leny Yoro and Diogo Dalot against Aston Villa showed, confidence is at rock-bottom.

4. 'Lack of effort'

United have consistently been out-run by their opponents this season, with the issue coming into focus around their 1-1 draw with Fulham in September. Gary Neville branded the players an "absolute disgrace" for walking around. "I've never seen such a lack of effort," he raged on Sky Sports post-match.

Effort is the cornerstone of most teams - and is particularly important to Pochettino. Carrick, Ten Hag, Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, Jose Mourinho and Ruben Amorim all had to fight back against a perception of players coasting. And Pochettino will be no different.

Only Liverpool average less than United's average total of 102.4km per match in the Premier League this season. You suspect Pochettino will have something to say about that.

View 5 Images Mauricio Pochettino will get to work on the training pitch next week (Image: Omar Vega/Getty Images)

5. Paper-thin squad

Pochettino will be fully aware of the task facing him - and the players at his disposal. United's failure to sign a left-back or striker in the summer transfer window - in which they focused instead on midfield - has left them short of depth.

Benjamin Sesko's injury has forced Bryan Mbeumo to play up front, while Shaw's absence has seen Dalot fill in badly at left-back. Marcus Rashford, Carlos Baleba, Manuel Ugarte and Maguire are all also currently listed as injured.

The January transfer window can't come soon enough, but even then Pochettino is very unlikely to be backed with millions. The loan market is expected to be targeted, meaning expectations have already been tempered.

Sports.title: Usman Nurmagomedov sentenced to six months in prison for Merab Dvalishvili attack
Sports.content:
Usman Nurmagomedov sentenced to six months in prison for Merab Dvalishvili attack

GRAPHIC CONTENT - Merab Dvalishvili was left with a bloody face after he was attacked by Usman Nurmagomedov on Wednesday

View 4 Images Merab Dvalishvili was slapped by Usman Nurmagomedov (Image: @ChampRDS/X)

Eight people have been sentenced to prison following Usman Nurmagomedov's attack on Merab Dvalishvili, according to reports.

‌



‌



On Wednesday, former UFC bantamweight champion Dvalishvili was left with a bloodied face falling a brawl with Nurmagomedov and his crew in at the Yas Hilton on Wednesday. The Georgian star was conducting an interview ahead of Saturday's RAF Abu Dhabi - where he is due to face Marlon Moraes in a wrestling bout - when Nurmagomedov and a group of friends approached him from behind.

‌



A short exchange of words occurred before Nurmagomedov slapped Dvalishvili in the face, sparking an all-out brawl between the two sets of camps. Dvalishvili and his friend Saba Lazishvili were left severely injured following the physical altercation.

‌



On Friday morning, local reports stated that Nurmagomedov and his five associates were sentenced to six months in prison, slapped with a hefty 300,000 AED fine, and face deportation over the Abu Dhabi hotel attack.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources

The two people who filmed the brawl were also sentenced to six months in prison along with a 300,000 AED fine, and order to be deported after serving the sentence for "violating privacy by using information technology to film and publish footage of the brawl." Two others have also been fined for disturbing public security and assaulting others - ordered to pay 50,000 AED, but avoided jail time. Dvalishvili and Lazishvili were each fined 50,000 AED.

‌



Wrestling promotion RAF revealed on Friday that Dvalishvili has since been released from custody. Nurmagomedov was not due to feature on the RAF card over in Abu Dhabi, but was merely in attendance to support his older brother, Umar, who is expected to face UFC icon Urijah Faber.

On Friday, RAF CEO and co-founder Chad Bronstein issued the following statement: “I am pleased to share that Merab Dvalishvili is back with us in Abu Dhabi. We would like to express our sincere appreciation to the relevant authorities in Abu Dhabi for their professionalism and support. We remain focused on moving forward and are pleased to have Merab back with us."

‌



Conor McGregor clears up retirement confusion ahead of final fight READ MORE :

Conor Benn told Conor McGregor fight would not last long READ MORE :

UFC welterweight champion Islam Makhachev, who trains with Nurmagomedov, was eager to break his silence and share his side of the story. “To those who are now condemning Usman and the guys, [and] they are writing insults to them, why were you silent when Merab hit a Dagestani wrestler for nothing and hurt his honor?” Makhachev wrote. “The man approached him to talk without malice. Merab started what happened today in his homeland by allowing himself to hit a guest and insulting his mother.”

Dvalishvili was quick to upload a statement to social media following the brawl. He wrote: "Was doing an interview for RAF in hotel lobby and Usman and his buddies came up from behind and started punching me and my young friend. Security was holding me - They kept kicking us when we were down like losers."

‌



WARNING: GRAPHIC CONTENT

4 View 4 Images The brawl broke out in a hotel lobby (Image: @ChampRDS/X) 4 View 4 Images Merab Dvalishvili was left with a bloody face (Image: Instagram)

‌



The accompanying footage showed the Georgian bloody faced and receiving medical treatment, as he ranted: "What a sneaky way guys? Just two of us, me and my friend came here in Abu Dhabi and Usman Nurmagomedov and his friends came like snakes from behind. What kind of fighters you guys are? What kind of man does this, bro? If you want to talk fight, let's do it the real way, bro. You guys came from...There's just two of us and you guys were prepared, bro. What the f***?"

Dvalishvili then added: "We bleed, we fight, we war, but you guys are just sneaky guys, bro. You guys are not real men. That shows your guys' character, shows you guys aren't real men.

‌



"What the f*** guys? If you want to fight, fight. Let's f***ing fight. We are fighters, bro. I talk. I'm a real guy, I talk straight. But you guys came from behind bro. I don't know how many guys you was. All of your friends waiting for us in a sneaky way. Wow. I knew what kind of guys you are. I just came here in Abu Dhabi and Usman, Umar (Nurmagomedov's brother) and his friends came from behind and tried to beat us. So many guys. I'm fine guys. All my friends and family, I'm f***ing fine."

View 4 Images Merab Dvalishvili is supposed to wrestle on Saturday evening (Image: @ChampRDS/X)

‌



Dvalishvili has a long history with the Nurmagomedovs. Last year, the 35-year-old defeated Umar at UFC 311 by unanimous decision to defend the UFC bantamweight title. The rivalry ramped up even further a few months ago after Dvalishvili slapped Umar's friend, Akhmed Gadzhimagomedov, backstage after RAF Georgia. Dvalishvili, who had beaten Henry Cejudo in a freestyle wrestling match that evening, had shut down talks of a bout between himself and Umar.

Gadzhimagomedov then approached him to confront him about his comments, with Dvalishvili responding by slapping the Dagestani - leading to a similar scrap between camps. Speaking with Ariel Helwani, Dvalishvili explained his reasoning for the slap.

Article continues below

He said: "I was super relaxed, super chilled and then somebody came and grabbed my neck and pulled me over and started yelling at me in Russian language, which I hardly understand. And he mentioned Umar. It took me a couple of seconds to realise, 'Who is this guy to tell me what to talk about him? It's between me and Umar.' I have so much respect for all Dagestani people, especially fighters. The only guy who I don't like from Dagestan is Umar and his sneaky manager, Rizvan [Magomedov]. The guy who was helping Umar disrespect me on X and Threads."

Sports.title: Wayne Rooney made to wait for I'm A Celebrity debut because of England clash
Sports.content:
Wayne Rooney made to wait for I'm A Celebrity debut because of England clash

England legend Rooney made to wait for I'm A Celebrity debut - but might have hairdryer ready

View Image Wayne Rooney is preparing to enter the jungle on I'm A Celebrity Get Me Out of Here (Image: ITV)

Wayne Rooney is having to wait an extra 24 hours for his I’m A Celebrity debut - because of England’s Nations League showdown with Spain.

‌



‌



Former England captain Rooney will be the star turn for the hit ITV show in the Australian jungle and is already the red-hot favourite to win.

‌



The show normally starts on a Sunday night and is renowned as being a massive ratings hit and is one of the big TV events of the year. It kicked off last year on the Sunday but this year starts on Monday night as England’s game with Spain takes centre stage on ITV.

‌



The broadcaster has the rights to England’s Nations League game which kicks off at 7.45pm and will also be a big draw because it is against the world champions in Madrid.

It means the I’m A Celebrity show will launch on Monday night with Rooney alongside other celebrities like Big Brother’s AJ Odudu, Love Island’s Chloe Burrows and Gavin and Stacey star Joanna Page.

Rooney’s former Everton teammate Duncan Ferguson says Rooney will use a hairdryer as a bizarre luxury item.

“I’ll tell you the luxury item he’ll want to take in. His hairdryer. I used to have the room next to him sometimes in hotels, and I would be in my bed and I’d hear the television on, and the next minute the hairdryer would go on, all the way through, and I’d be going, ‘What’s that next door?’

Sports.title: Man City appeal date set as new fears emerge over Premier League sanctions
Sports.content:
Man City appeal date set as new fears emerge over Premier League sanctions

Manchester City face serious sanctions if an appeal against the financial breaches they were charged with earlier this year fails when it takes place next month

View Image Manchester City's appeal will be heard next month (Image: Nick Potts/PA Wire)

Manchester City's appeal against the ruling that the club breached financial rules will be heard next month, with a verdict to come in the New Year followed by sanctions if it is unsuccessful.

‌



‌



An independent commission found the club guilty of breaking Premier League financial rules over a nine-season period, with the ruling hitting out at "sham" sponsorship contracts. City have continued to protest their innocence in the wake of the verdict, as well as confirming they would appeal.

‌



Fresh details of the appeal have now been shared by The Financial Times, who reveal it will take place in December and could run for a number of days.

‌



An independent commission will then determine City's face, with a verdict expected in 2027. If City lose their appeal, that is also when sanctions will be placed upon them.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

However, the report adds that while Premier League rules give the commission the freedom to pass whatever sanctions it feels necessary, there is no indication as to when they come into effect. They would also be subject to appeals, meaning there may be further delays which could stretch beyond the conclusion of the current Premier League season.

‌



Manchester City have been defiant in their communications since confirmation that they had been found guilty on all but one of the charges laid against them.

A club statement responding to the news back in September read: “The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality. As such Manchester City FC’s position remains consistent with the club’s statement of February 2023.

Article continues below

“The club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis the Premier League board and executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair minded regulator, free from partisan influence.”
