Sports.title: Lawson to stay in F1 as Racing Bulls announces 2027 driver pairing
Sports.content:
Racing Bulls has confirmed Liam Lawson will stay with the team for the 2027 Formula 1 campaign, partnering Arvid Lindblad for a second, straight season.

They have formed a formidable duo this year having propelled Racing Bulls to fifth in the championship, which is set to be the Anglo-Italian team's best-ever result.

Despite sitting on 89 points, however, compared to 38 for rookie Lindblad, Lawson's future was in doubt thanks to junior driver Nikola Tsolov starring in F2 this year.

The 19-year-old Bulgarian is second in the standings and has been handed private testing opportunities and a rookie FP1 session in Mexico as part of his junior driver duties.

So Racing Bulls was weighing up its need for short-term performance against its explicit goal of training young drivers for parent team Red Bull.

But with Lawson rising to the occasion in recent weeks, performing some of his strongest races under constant pressure, the 24-year-old has effectively been too good for the team to ignore.

Nikola Tsolov Photo by: Simon Galloway / LAT Images via Getty Images

Sources indicated to Autosport in Brazil last weekend that amid a big push for the company's top leadership to back Tsolov, the pendulum swung back towards Lawson's favour with his performances over the Americas triple-header.

Read Also: Formula 1 How the Racing Bulls pendulum is swinging back towards Lawson

So the Kiwi has now signed a fresh deal for 2027 with team boss Alan Permane saying he had "no doubt" that the squad will field the strongest possible line-up next season.

"We’re delighted to be continuing with Liam and Arvid for 2027," he said. "Both have demonstrated their ability and potential throughout the season, and we’ve seen the progress they’ve made, both individually and as a pairing.

“I have no doubt that this is the best driver line-up for us, bringing a strong combination of experience and ambition.

“Together, we have a solid foundation to build on the progress made this year, continue pushing ourselves forward and take the next step towards achieving our ambitions in 2027."

Next year is set to be Lawson’s third, full season in F1 having made his debut at Zandvoort towards the back end of the 2023 campaign - having another partial season in 2024.

Arvid Lindblad, Racing Bulls, Liam Lawson, Racing Bulls Photo by: Rudy Carezzevoli / Getty Images

"I’m very happy to be continuing with Visa Cash App Racing Bulls next year,” he said. “We’ve had a brilliant season together and the team has worked very hard to produce a fast car, which I’ve loved driving.

“It feels great to be part of a historic season for the team as we continue our fight for P5 in the constructors' championship. It's a testament to the hard work of everyone both at track, and back at the factory.

"I’m looking forward to carrying this moment forward with Arvid through to 2027. We’re building something super positive and I’m excited by what we can achieve together.”

Lawson is currently eighth in the drivers’ standings with Lindblad in 11th ahead of the final three rounds: Las Vegas, Qatar and Abu Dhabi.

"Looking back on my first season in Formula 1, it's been a truly special year, full of new experiences and learnings since the very first pre-season test," said 19-year-old Lindblad.

"I can't wait to get started next year, building on everything I've learned during my rookie season. It's set to be an exciting year, and I look forward to continuing to drive alongside Liam."

Sports.title: What the Brazilian GP revealed about F1's ability to cope with rain
Sports.content:
The question of what might happen in a wet race has vexed Formula 1's stakeholders since before the beginning of the season. It's also prompted some unnecessarily hysterical commentary throughout the year, peaking in the run-up to last weekend's Brazilian Grand Prix at Interlagos, where rain for qualifying and the race was a virtual certainty for the first time this season.

Although the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia was interrupted by rain and the discovery of a software glitch, by the time the race got going the track was drying quickly. This was not the case in Brazil.

Qualifying at Interlagos was red-flagged for 80 minutes after a downpour coincided with the start of the session, and many media outlets alighted on a spicy George Russell quote in the aftermath.

"I love driving in the rain here but, at some point, if that was a race, there was no way we should be driving in that because the chances of seeing a really, really horrific incident are very, very high," he said.

Perfect headline material for a noisy story, but context was lacking. The general consensus within the paddock after that session was that the FIA made the right calls at the right time, immediately suspending Q1 during the initial downpour, then applying great rigour to identify a safe ‘window' to restart it.

"In general, I want to race, but yesterday [Saturday] I think it was the perfect call," said Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur after the race. "When we did the first [Q1] lap before the red flag, we came back with two centimetres of water in the car…"

Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Carlos Sainz, Williams, Arvid Lindblad, Racing Bulls Photo by: Simon Galloway / LAT Images via Getty Images

Those conditions were too wet to stage any kind of track activity beyond a boat race in the pitlane. The real questions surrounded how the cars and the latest generation of tyres would perform in the kind of wet and/or rapidly changing circumstances in which qualifying and the race could actually be staged.

Historically, Pirelli's heavily treaded ‘extreme' wet tyres are rarely seen, since too much of their operating window sits outside the margin of what is considered to be acceptable racing conditions. They displace massive quantities of water but the tread blocks overheat too quickly as the track dries. By the time the track is wet enough to justify the ‘extreme' tyre, a red flag is usually imminent.

The intermediate tyres have therefore been the wet-weather boots of choice, but this year's are understood to be too ‘hard' and slow to come up to operating temperature. Pirelli just hasn't been able to accomplish like-for-like running with the narrower wheels mandated for this season, given the testing restrictions.

It's long been feared that lack of grip from the new intermediates, combined with the more brutal torque delivery of the latest generation of engines, would make the 2026 F1 cars dangerously undriveable in the wet. Hence the outbreak of hysteria ahead of the Brazil weekend.

What actually transpired was less dramatic, and more nuanced. The nature of the track surface at Interlagos meant driveability was occasionally an issue, but not always. In the background, the FIA has been doing a lot of work since the beginning of the year to manage power delivery in these conditions.

Alexander Albon, Williams, Carlos Sainz, Williams Photo by: Colin McMaster / LAT Images via Getty Images

While qualifying – once it got started – offered some hope that the ‘extreme' wets are now more useable, the intermediates were a little more problematic. Kimi Antonelli went off at Turn 12 on his lap to the grid, and several other drivers reported their cars became a handful again when rain in the last 10 laps dictated a return to the intermediates.

"I think what is good is that we can use the 'big wet' much more than in the past," said Vasseur. "And this is good because it's not pushing you to use inter when it's a more 'big wet' situation, or mix between the two, and then you are taking risks.

"I think the quali was pretty good… but also the grip was completely different. You saw in the lap to the grid today that everybody was completely like hell. I think it's a difficult track with these conditions."

Pirelli's target for next year is to bring the performance of the wet-weather compounds closer together, so the intermediate warms up faster and the ‘extreme' is more resistant to wear. But this is a challenge to engineer because the tracks differ so much in terms of the energy going through the tyres.

"It was difficult to fire them up but they also wore quite quickly," said Alex Albon, who finished 15th in Brazil.

"So even when they're cold, they're wearing and it just feels like they never overheat, or they never level up to temperature. And then by the time you're circulating, the tread's already come off the tyre and then you're already struggling, you're sliding around. So, you never feel good at any point in the race; it never feels like it comes alive."

This would explain some of the peculiarities of the opening laps, where those at the front of the grid found themselves having to be super-cautious because they couldn't feel the grip – while some of those towards the rear, who spent less time waiting for lights-out, got strong getaways.

Even among those there was a variance: Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton quickly broke through to the top 10 from 20th and 21st on the grid, only for Hamilton to then go backwards as his car developed massive oversteer snaps. Verstappen, like Antonelli, then found his car less performant on the slicks.

Wet conditions added to the drama of qualifying Photo by: Sam Bloxham / LAT Images via Getty Images

This mixed spread of performance over the wet and dry tyre compounds will be tricky to unpick, but the consensus remained that the wet-weather rubber needs more development. There were minor gripes but not the disasters that were feared and noisily predicted.

"I think the level of the wet and the inter is not good enough and we need to work with Pirelli on finding a better tyre," said Carlos Sainz, "because in the mixed conditions the inter is still a very weak tyre at the rear. By the time it warms up, the front is gone.

"And the extreme, honestly, yesterday we had so much sliding and a big lack of rear grip, so still missing a bit of development on these two tyres."

While the data gathered through running in many different conditions this weekend will be useful, it's still an isolated example. What worked or didn't work at Interlagos may not translate elsewhere, given variances in surfaces and ambient temperatures.

"Quite tricky I would say," was Liam Lawson's take on racing in the wet in a 2026 F1 car.

"The biggest problem today is the [ambient] temperature was much cooler than yesterday. And so even though there was less water, on the laps of the grid the cars were nearly undriveable, and the temps were just going down.

"So, we survived the start of the race but at points when it rains a lot, the inter becomes... it's not that the standing water's too much, it's that you can't actually keep the temperature in it. So, if we're on a track like Vegas and it rains, honestly, I think we're in trouble.

"But overall, obviously we got through a weekend for the first time with these tyres."

Additional reporting by Roberto Chinchero and Guilherme Longo

Sports.title: F1 2026 calendar update: Imola off the table, no plan B if Iran war escalates
Sports.content:
The Qatar and Abu Dhabi grands prix which will conclude Formula 1’s 2026 season are set to proceed as planned, provided there is no dramatic escalation of the Iran war.

The Middle Eastern conflict, which started in late February as the United States and Israel launched strikes on Iran, has destabilised the region. The calendars of many motorsport championships have been impacted – not least F1’s, whose Saudi Arabian race was cancelled while Bahrain’s round was postponed and hosted in Malaysia.

F1 has been monitoring the situation closely, with a chilly Imola as an alternative season finale on the first weekend of December if Qatar and Abu Dhabi were unable to host their respective events.

Lusail did run its MotoGP round without major issues last weekend, though both Yamaha teams withdrew from the competition due to the geopolitical situation.

10 November was F1’s deadline to provide Imola with a final answer as to whether the Italian track would have to prepare for a grand prix in the next three weeks; it will not.

Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Isack Hadjar, Racing Bulls Photo by: Zak Mauger / Motorsport Images

So the 2026 season will end with the planned Las Vegas-Qatar-Abu Dhabi triple-header, with travel insurance and governments’ travel advice currently allowing it.

However, there’s a caveat: F1 is aware it cannot guarantee the situation won’t change by early December and insists it will prioritise safety if the conflict escalates.

Team bosses have been maintaining a straightforward stance on the matter – they trust F1 and the FIA to make the right calls.

“I trust them to take the best decision for all of us,” Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur commented in Mexico. “Me, personally, I want to race. It doesn't matter where, but I want to race. Now, I will go where they will tell us to go.”

“Stefano and Mohammed have been pretty clear about the situation that Formula 1 follows what the international guidelines are, whether there are travel restrictions, airlines not flying, any warnings in the region, the kind of feedback that local governments are making,” his Mercedes counterpart Toto Wolff added in Friday’s press conference at Interlagos. “So not only the promoters, but what the local governments are making. And this is what you need to rely on, in my opinion, and I'm fully with that.

Toto Wolff, Mercedes Photo by: Mark Sutton / Formula 1 via Getty Images

“I think that if riders stand up, who know nothing geopolitically about what's going on, but have an audience that listens, I think that is something that creates media value. But I would have done the same as MotoGP management has done. You want to ride or drive, go. If you don't want to, don't go. It's as simple as that, and everybody can take their personal decisions on that, and I respect that.

“Of course, you've got to be wary of what's happening in the next few days, a few weeks, and Stefano has his finger on the pulse to monitor that. If things were to get more dangerous and we would get that feedback, then he's going to be the first one, together with Mohammed, to protect the people that were meant to travel. So that's why I'm following their guidance.

“From what I'm hearing internally, it hasn't been raised. It hasn't been a topic. But also there, if someone feels they don't feel comfortable, he or she doesn't feel comfortable travelling, then it's something that I would always respect. And maybe that's an opportunity to give somebody else a chance. It wouldn't change anything for the relationship. I've always respected that some people didn't want to go to certain grands prix, and that's how I see it at the moment.”

Additional reporting by Ronald Vording

Sports.title: FIA reveals ADUO results in final review of 2026 F1 season
Sports.content:
The FIA has announced its final Additional Development and Upgrade Opportunities (ADUO) results for the 2026 Formula 1 season, with no changes granted for any of the power unit manufacturers.

From this season, the FIA installed a mechanism in the F1 regulations which allowed power unit manufacturers the ability to make updates, if they fell behind the leading engine, in the form of tokens permitted under a performance scale.

After the first period in 2026, which ran from the Australian Grand Prix to the Canadian GP, it was announced that Red Bull Ford Powertrains emerged as the benchmark, while Mercedes’ internal combustion engine trails by between 2-4%, which gave the German manufacturer to one additional upgrade this year and one more next season.

Ferrari, Audi and Honda fell into the category of being more than 4% behind on ICE power, which grants them two upgrades during the current campaign and two more in 2027.

Red Bull Ford Powertrains asked for a review of the ADUO analysis, which delayed the official publication of the first results, as it disputed the results and being considered the manufacturer with the strongest engine.

As agreed before the start of the season by the teams, the FIA only measures the internal combustion engine, but once a manufacturer qualifies for ADUO, it is also allowed to modify electrical components such as the battery and MGU-K.

Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Photo by: Colin McMaster / LAT Images via Getty Images

So while Red Bull’s rivals have been able to install power unit upgrades across this season, the Milton Keynes-based effort has effectively faced an engine freeze.

In the third and final FIA analysis of ADUO – which took engine data from the Dutch GP up to and including the US GP – there has been no change and therefore no manufacturer will gain or lose its current concessions.

There was also no change in the second ADUO period over the summer.

“For the third period, the relative performance gaps to the leading ICE evolved, but these changes did not result in any additional homologations being granted to the Power Unit Manufacturers,” an FIA report stated.

Given the dispute over how ADUO is measured, the FIA is open to changes in the system in the future, subject to approval from the power unit manufacturers, while FIA single-seater director Nikolas Tombazis is confident the concept is working as desired.

“The FIA has undertaken extensive analysis as part of the review of ADUO this year. Based on the quality of the data and the robustness of the assessment process, we are confident in our findings and the conclusions reached,” Tombazis said.

Nikolas Tombazis, FIA Photo by: Kym Illman / Getty Images

“The first year of implementation has also reinforced our belief that the ADUO concept is the right one for Formula 1.

“However, it is important that the system continues to evolve to ensure it remains efficient, relevant and fit for purpose. To that end, we have been working closely with the power unit manufacturers and teams to explore refinements to the methodology that will support the continued effectiveness of ADUO in future seasons.”

The next ADUO period will start in 2027, covering the opening six races of the F1 season from the Bahrain GP to the Miami GP.

Sports.title: On This Day: Racing rules in spotlight as Hamilton takes Brazil win from Verstappen | Brief
Sports.content: The Formula 1 world championship began in 1950 and is considered the world’s leading form of single-seater motorsport. The 2025 F1 season is the 75th time the championship has been held. Sports.title: Spotlight: FIA pulls F1 reporter’s pass over column calling Leclerc a ‘sneaky b*****d’ | Brief
Sports.content:
The Daily Mail says the FIA has barred its Formula 1 reporter from attending the final three rounds of the world championship as a media representative.

It quotes a letter sent yestreday by FIA general manager Alberto Villareal regarding an article the newspaper published about Ferrari driver Charles Leclerc , whom its F1 correspondent Jonathan McEvoy called a “sneaky little b*****d”.

“The FIA considers that your article falls short of the standards of professionalism expected of media representatives accredited to cover the FIA Formula One World Championship,” said Villareal, quoted by the newspaper.

“Accordingly, the FIA has decided to exercise its discretion under the 2026 FIA Formula One World Championship Accreditation Guidelines to withdraw your media accreditation for the remainder of the 2026 season, with immediate effect.”

Three rounds of the season remain in the USA, Qatar and Abu Dhabi.

Earlier this year Max Verstappen ordered the removal of another journalist, Giles Richards of The Guardian, from a Red Bull press conference. Verstappen was unhappy Richards asked him three months earlier whether he regretted colliding with George Russell during last year’s Abu Dhabi Grand Prix.

Sports.title: Grosjean admits his single-seater career is likely over after ending IndyCar season 19th | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Former Formula 1 driver Romain Grosjean, who survived a fireball crash six years ago in Bahrain, is preparing to call time on his single-seater racing career.

Grosjean raced in F1 between 2009 and 2020, then switched to IndyCar. He completed his fifth season in the series this year but the 40-year-old admits he is unlikely to return.

“The reality is, this is probably the end for me with single-seaters,” Grosjean told Racer.

Grosjean finished on the podium three times in his first season in IndyCar with Coyne, earning the attention of top team Andretti, who hired him for the 2022 season. The team replaced him after he finished 13th in the championship for two years running,

After spending one year at Juncos Hollinger, Grosjean lost his drive for 2025, but returned with Coyne this year. The season began promisingly when he reached the final round of qualifying in St Petersburg, but a string of finishes outside the top 10 followed.

The Coyne driver finished on the podium just once all year. He ended the season 19th in the standings ahead of just six other full-time drivers, including RLL’s Mick Schumacher, who replaced him at Haas in 2021.

Grosjean said it had been a “tough” season overall. “I had [a] few amazing moments. I got the chance to lead the Indy 500. I finished in the top 10. I ran [in] the top five most of the last 60 laps. Amazing! I got a podium in Markham, which was incredible with my ‘tractor.’

“But then we go to Milwaukee and Laguna Seca, and [at] Laguna Seca, I qualified dead last, almost. I know it’s one of my fastest tracks, so I’m like, ‘I don’t want that anymore.’ I’ve had enough of those moments where you just don’t have the tools to play.”

Grosjean was supposed to contest his final grand prix at Abu Dhabi in 2020. However the burns he suffered in his Bahrain crash forced him out early. His former team Haas gave him the opportunity to test one of its cars at Mugello last year.

Sports.title: Court of Appeal to hear Audi’s case over Tsunoda decision on November 25th | Formula 1
Sports.content:
The International Court of Appeal has set a date to hear Audi’s appeal over the Italian Grand Prix stewards’ decision regarding Yuki Tsunoda.

Audi is challenging the decision not to penalise Tsunoda, who finished the race in 10th position, for triggering an extra formation lap before the start of the race.

The ICA will hear the case on November 25th at the FIA’s headquarters in Paris.

Tsunoda, who substituted for Racing Bulls’ Liam Lawson at Monza, finished seven seconds ahead of Gabriel Bortoleto. Therefore the Audi driver could gain a point if Tsunoda is penalised.

Bortoleto previously said Audi’s case was “straightforward”.

F1’s sporting regulations state any driver who causes an extra formation lap must start the race from the pit lane and will receive a Stop-and-Go penalty if they fail to. As Tsunoda did not start from the pit lane, Audi believes he should receive a penalty.

The stewards ruled Tsunoda “was not the ’cause’ of the extra formation lap” and therefore did not have to start from the pit lane.

This is the second time this year the ICA has been asked to rule on a decision taken by the stewards at a grand prix. In September they reinstated two penalties which were originally issued to Pierre Gasly during the Monaco Grand Prix and later rescinded.

ICA hearing announcement

On 6th September 2026, at the end of the formation lap during the race restart following a red flag, the race director ordered an additional formation lap Following the race, the stewards investigated a potential breach of Article B5.9.4 of the 2026 FIA Formula 1 Sporting Regulations by Mr Yuki Tsunoda (driver of car number 22), which requires any driver who caused an extra formation lap to start from the end of the pit lane. Failure to do so, a Stop-and-Go penalty should be imposed on the driver. In decision number 69, the stewards decided to take no further action against Mr Yuki Tsunoda. On 9th September 2026, Audi Revolut F1 Team lodged an appeal against that decision, arguing that Mr Yuki Tsunoda had caused the extra formation lap and should therefore have received the prescribed Stop-and-Go penalty.

Sports.title: Racing Bulls keep Lawson and Lindblad as Tsolov gets Red Bull reserve role | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Racing Bulls has confirmed an unchanged driver line-up for the 2027 Formula 1 season.

Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad will continue to drive for the team next year.

The news ends speculation Red Bull’s second Formula 1 team would replace either of its drivers with Nikola Tsolov. The Red Bull junior driver lies second in the Formula 2 standings with four races remaining.

Shortly after Racing Bulls confirmed its driver line-up, Red Bull announced Tsolov as its reserve driver for 2027. Red Bull also announced Tsolov will be Racing Bulls’ reserve driver.

Racing Bulls is on course to score its best championship result under any of its identities, including its time competing as Minardi, before it was purchased by Red Bull at the end of 2005.

However Lawson’s future at the team came into doubt as Racing Bulls delayed its decision on its driver line-up for next year. Lawson made his F1 debut in 2023 and gained promotion to Red Bull in 2025 but the team dropped him after just two rounds. Lawson made a temporary return to Red Bull this year as a substitute for the injured Isack Hadjar.

During his time at Racing Bulls, Lawson has scored enough points to single-handedly put Racing Bulls fifth in the constructors’ championship. However he clashed with Red Bull driver Max Verstappen during a practice session in Mexico earlier this month, which his rival said was “not very smart behaviour” for a driver who was “fighting for [his] seat”. Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies denied his team would have any say in its junior squad’s driver line-up.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Racing Bulls team principal Alan Permane said Lawson and his rookie team mate Lindblad form “the best driver line-up for us, bringing a strong combination of experience and ambition”.

“Together, we have a solid foundation to build on the progress made this year, continue pushing ourselves forward and take the next step towards achieving our ambitions in 2027.”

Tsolov said he hopes to make the step up to F1 after next year. “My ambition is clear: I want to become an F1 driver,” he said. “Having the opportunity to spend next year preparing for that next step is incredibly exciting.

“I’m confident that with the team’s support and experience, I’ll have the best possible preparation to make sure I’m fully ready to take the next step onto the F1 grid when the time comes.”

Mekies said Red Bull has been highly impressed by Tsolov. “Nikola is an exceptionally talented young driver, and we have been hugely impressed by his development and performances over the past few years,” he said.

“To fight for the championship in F3 and now challenge for the F2 title in his first full season says a great deal about his ability and determination. What has impressed us just as much is his maturity, his approach to racing and his willingness to keep learning and improving.

“We have enormous belief in Nikola’s potential and see him as a driver with a very exciting future in F1. This appointment reflects our confidence in him and our commitment to his continued development. Our focus in 2027 will be on giving him the experience, tools and support he needs to be ready to race in F1 next.”

Sports.title: Stats: Verstappen claims second place from lowest grid position since 1983 | 2026 Brazilian Grand Prix stats and facts
Sports.content:
In 2024 Lando Norris’s championship hopes suffered a fatal blow when he failed to win from pole position at Interlagos.

Max Verstappen claimed an unlikely victory in a rain-hit race from 17th on the grid, putting him on course to retain his championship crown.

Norris has made amends since then, however, winning the next two grands prix at Interlagos from pole position. Both times he prevented Verstappen from completing another impressive back-to-front charge: the Red Bull driver finished second on Sunday from the penultimate place on the grid, just as he did 12 months earlier.

However as there are two more cars in the field this year, Verstappen’s charge to second place came from 21st position on the grid (he was actually the 20th car on the grid as Valtteri Bottas’s Cadillac was pushed into the pit lane). This is the lowest starting position anyone has taken second place from since the 1983 Long Beach Grand Prix, when Niki Lauda charged there from 23rd.

Lauda started one place behind his team mate John Watson, who led him home in a McLaren one-two, setting the record for the lowest grid position from which a grand prix has been won.

McLaren may not have managed a one-two last weekend but Norris took his 14th grand prix victory, giving him as many as a trio of multiple world champions: Jack Brabham, Graham Hill and Emerson Fittipaldi. This was also his 20th pole position, the latter giving him as many as Damon Hill and Valtteri Bottas.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Norris reached the podium for the 50th time in his career. Verstappen, meanwhile, took his eighth podium finish in a row, which is the longest streak any driver has managed this year.

Isack Hadjar equalled his best finish with another third place – this was his fourth. Although he briefly hit the front of the field after Norris pitted on lap 49 he did not officially lead a lap, as he pitted the next time by and Andrea Kimi Antonelli crossed the line in front.

Liam Lawson finished seventh for the second race in a row. He has now scored enough points for Racing Bulls to single-handedly put them fifth in the constructors’ championship.

Lewis Hamilton became the second driver in Formula 1 history to record his 400th grand prix start. He joins Fernando Alonso, who reached 400 two years ago:

For the second race in a row, Haas ran a new driver, but this time their rookie did not manage to bag a point. Rafael Camara made his debut in his home race, becoming the first driver to do so since Germany’s Markus Winkelhock in the 2007 European Grand Prix, held at the Nurburgring.

Camara raced with number 51 which last appeared in a grand prix at Abu Dhabi in 2020. It was also used on that occasion by another Brazilian driving for Haas: Pietro Fittipaldi.

Lance Stroll’s race ended in retirement yet again. That was the 14th time this year he has not been classified – failing to complete 90% of the race distance – equalling the all-time record which has been set on five other occasions by four drivers.

These are Andrea de Cesaris twice (in 1986 with Minardi and 1987 with Brabham), Piercarlo Ghinzani (in 1986 with Osella), Ivan Capelli (in 1989 with Leyton House) and Rubens Barrichello (in 1997 with Stewart).

It remains possible for Stroll to match or even exceed the record for most retirements in a season. De Cesaris set this in 1987 when he started but was not running at the end of all 16 rounds. In addition to his 14 non-classifications he ran out of fuel before completing the final lap at Spa (but was classified third) and spun out with four laps to go in the final race at Adelaide, taking eighth place.

Sports.title: Bradley Urges Shakur Stevenson to Take Hearn Fights Without Signing
Sports.content:
Tim Bradley recommends that Shakur Stevenson find out ahead of time what fights he can get, but not sign with his Matchroom company. Stay a free agent and fight twice for Hearn, and then move on.

The pickings are kind of slim for Shakur with Matchroom, though. Even if he doesn’t sign with them, there aren’t superstar fighters that will provide him the kind of money that he was reportedly asking for when he was signed with Zuffa.

He wanted $15 million per fight and reportedly turned down a $7 million offer to fight Raymond Muratalla. If Shakur cares about money, the biggest payday he potentially gets is fighting Jaron ‘Boots’ Ennis, but he might have to go up to junior middleweight to make that fight.

Given the big production Stevenson made about wanting a 144-lb catchweight for a fight with Devin Haney, he probably won’t be excited to move up to 154 to face a puncher like Ennis.

Note: Andy Cruz is no longer signed with Matchroom.

Bradley wants Shakur to try and get a deal with DAZN that would allow him to work with other promoters on their platform. From there, he could fight the opponent he wants that competes on that network. The big question is whether DAZN would support the paydays Shakur wants.

Hearn brought up the idea of Shakur focusing on the undisputed championship at 140, which would put him in fights against Raymond Muratalla, Dalton Smith, Gary Antuanne Russell, and whoever wins the vacant IBF title.

The immediate question is whether Shakur fights Muratalla or gives up his WBO light welterweight belt. That would be the second straight fighter he chose not to face after he failed to make a deal with Devin Haney.

“I don’t want to be, you know, solely tied to you, but let me get these two fights. Once I get done here, I can move on to do work with another promoter,” said Bradley to Fighthub TV, describing how he would have Stevenson approach those talks. “That way it’ll be easier for him to make fights, right? “Okay, Eddie, what do you got for me? Who do you got?”

Matchroom has some good fighters, but not the ones that would lead to the type of purses Shakur was hoping for. He was paid well for his last two fights on Turki Alalshikh’s cards, getting $10 million for Teofimo Lopez and $7 million for William Zepeda, according to Sportster.com and SalarySports.com.

Perhaps the best piece of advice Bradley gave Shakur was for him to fight more often, because the ideal way to increase his popularity to get the kind of paydays that he was hoping for at Zuffa. Fighting once a year isn’t going to get it. In 2026, Shakur has only fought once, beating Teofimo.

Sports.title: Hearn Wants Diego Pacheco on the Turnbuckle Calling Out Canelo
Sports.content:
Eddie Hearn wants Diego Pacheco to look so good in victory over Darius Fulghum on Saturday night that he can climb on the turnbuckle in Carson, California, and call out Canelo Álvarez and Jaime Munguia.

Super middleweight contender Pacheco (26-0, 19 KOs) will need to raise his game to look impressive enough against the big-punching Fulghum for Canelo, Munguia, and fans to take him seriously.

In recent fights, Pacheco, 25, hasn’t looked great, struggling to beat Kevin Lee Sadjo and Steven Nelson.

“Forget all this by any means necessary. You want to go and get those big fights. You want to shout out those big names. You come in here, you look sensational in front of the whole country,” said Hearn at the weigh-in on Friday about what he wants from Pacheco. “You got to be doing a job on Darius Fulghum tomorrow night and standing on that turnbuckle calling out Canelo Alvarez, calling out Jaime Munguia. And you got to get people believing in you.”

The problem is that even when the 6’4″ Pacheco is dominating, he still doesn’t look overly impressive. His game is built on jabbing, loading up on hooks, and holding. He looks awkward and gangly. Expecting him to shine against Fulghum is asking a lot, and could be dangerous because he’s going up against a big puncher.

Sadjo had Pacheco hurt several times in their fight last December. He dropped Pacheco in the eighth, forcing him into full safety-first mode for the rest of the 12-round contest. From the eighth round on, Pacheco fought to survive, prompting fans to boo.

Fulghum told Pacheco that he made a mistake by selecting him as his opponent for this fight. He says he plans on knocking him out. “Pressure bust pipes,” said Fulghum.

If Fulghum can get in close and battle him on the inside, Hearn’s hope for an impressive showing from Pacheco could go up in smoke. Fulghum could spoil everything, though there’s little chance he’ll get a fight against Canelo or Munguia next. Canelo has already mentioned Terence Crawford and Willy Hutchinson as the two on his hit list. For Pacheco, he may have to look elsewhere, toward Jacob Bank or Wilkens Mathieu.

Sports.title: Why Muhammad Ali Still Edges Joe Louis
Sports.content:
Joe Louis had the greatest heavyweight title reign. Muhammad Ali had the greater heavyweight career. Louis held the championship for nearly 12 years, and nobody has matched that run. But Ali beat Sonny Liston when few expected him to, took the title back from an unbeaten George Foreman a decade later, and won two of three fights with Joe Frazier. If the question is who proved the most against the best heavyweights of his time, Ali is my pick.

Louis gave up the title when he retired in 1949. Ezzard Charles was already champion when he beat Louis on points the following year, and Rocky Marciano knocked Louis out in 1951, before Marciano had won the title himself. Those losses are part of Louis’s record, but the fight that best explains his greatness took place in 1938. Max Schmeling had knocked him out two years earlier. Louis stopped him in the first round of their rematch.

What Ali proved after Liston

Ali was 29–0 when he was forced out of boxing after refusing military induction in 1967. He came back in 1970 and lost to Frazier the following year. Frazier could get inside, make Ali work at a pace he disliked, and hurt him with the left hook. Ali won the rematch and then the third fight in Manila. He also knocked out Foreman, who had taken the title from Frazier in two rounds. Ali’s third championship came in 1978, when he outpointed Leon Spinks seven months after losing the title to him.

Marciano has the cleanest record of the six at 49–0, with six successful title defenses. His best argument is what he did when he was behind. Jersey Joe Walcott dropped him in the first round of their 1952 title fight and was ahead on all three cards when Marciano knocked him out in the 13th. Larry Holmes makes a stronger case on longevity. He won the WBC belt from Ken Norton in 1978 and reached 48–0 before Michael Spinks beat him. Holmes’s jab was still good enough to help him outpoint an unbeaten Ray Mercer in 1992, at age 42.

Mike Tyson’s best years were spectacular. He took his first belt from Trevor Berbick at 20, collected the other two, and stopped Michael Spinks in 91 seconds. His first reign ended when Buster Douglas knocked him out in Tokyo. Foreman’s case runs in the opposite direction. His two-round demolition of Frazier showed what he could do in his prime. Knocking out Michael Moorer at 45, twenty years after losing to Ali, showed how much he could still do long after it.

Louis is the closest call because a champion has to keep winning after everybody has had years to study him. What puts Ali ahead for me is that the two best heavyweights he faced asked completely different questions of him. Frazier made him fight at close quarters for rounds at a time. Foreman had the power to end the fight if Ali made one bad mistake there. Ali found a way to beat both.

Sports.title: Raymond Ford’s Matchroom Deal Is Up. What Has He Earned?
Sports.content:
Raymond Ford’s contract with Eddie Hearn’s Matchroom has expired, and it now remains to be seen whether he’ll be re-signed for another stint. Hearn hasn’t said whether he’ll bring him back.

Ford is coming off a one-sided loss to O’Shaquie Foster last May, and you’ve got to figure out whether Matchroom will offer him less guaranteed money. It would make total sense for Hearn to re-sign Ford at a reduced price in a take-it-or-leave-it offer. Why pay similar money if he’s not producing?

The former WBA featherweight champion Ford, 27, has been with Matchroom his entire career since 2019, but he’s had a rough go since 2024. During that six-fight stretch, he’s been involved in four grueling fights, losing two of them and getting lucky with a questionable stoppage against knockout artist Otabek Kholmatov.

Ford (18-2-1, 8 KOs) took brutal shots from Kholmatov. He got hit with everything in the book, took them, but looked war-torn by the later rounds. He was losing that fight going into the 12th round when the referee suddenly halted the bout after the injured, hobbling Kholmatov briefly lost his balance.

“His contract’s up with us at the moment. We’ll see what happens,” said Hearn to iFL TV when asked about Ford.

The Foster fight was Raymond’s chance to redeem himself, but he failed miserably, getting outboxed, looking overmatched from the word go against the WBC super featherweight champion.

After that performance, Matchroom has to decide whether it’s worth bringing him back at any price. The company can sign other younger fighters with less mileage on the odometer who can handle pure boxers and sluggers better.

Unfortunately, Ford hasn’t shown the ability to deal with either type. His loss to the tiny 5’2″ slugger Nick Ball was another example of Ford’s inability to deal with a guy with power that brings pure heat for 12 rounds. Unlike Kholmatov, Ball wasn’t hampered by a knee injury that slowed him down in the later rounds.

At this point, Hearn might be better off letting Ford walk and finding another promoter willing to match him carefully and subsidize his career. Under the right circumstances, Ford can still win a title, but it would require rebuilding and waiting for the perfect style match-up.

Sports.title: Eddie Hearn in Contract Talks With Unnamed World Champion
Sports.content:
Eddie Hearn is hinting at signing two American fighters, including a world champion. He said he’s talked with WBO light welterweight champion Shakur Stevenson and former lightweight champion Keyshawn Davis. Hearn says he doesn’t have either ready to sign yet.

All told, Hearn says he’s in talks with 7 total fighters. Shakur and Keyshawn, plus 2 unnamed fighters at the contract stage, plus three others.

Signing Keyshawn and Shakur would still create problems for Hearn, since they would want to be paid a boatload of money for their fights. Yeah, it would be great for Hearn to have those two talents, but with the costs, it could be a nightmare if their cards hemorrhage dough repeatedly. Neither of them are PPV draws.

Hearn wants Shakur to focus on becoming undisputed at light welterweight. He’s talked about him fighting champions Gary Antuanne Russell and Dalton Smith in addition to whoever winds up with the vacant IBF title.

He’s also interested in matching him against Raymond Muratalla, who may be the toughest of the bunch because of his size and power. That would be a tougher fight for Shakur than the ones he’d had thus far in the pro ranks. It wouldn’t be a shock to hear him drag his feet at accepting it, which could cost him his WBO title if he refuses.

Hearn wants to get the 2020 Olympic silver medalist Keyshawn fighting often, as he believes he’s wasting his career. Although he has already fought twice this year, they were fights that he used to get his feet wet at 140 against Nahir Albright and Jamaine Ortiz.

The Albright fight seemed totally needless, though, because he’d already beaten him in 2023. Running it back seemed weird and wasteful.

“Get on the horse, man. You’re wasting your career,” said Hearn to iFL TV about Keyshawn.

Well, if Hearn does sign Davis, he should put him back in with his four-time conqueror Andy Cruz. That’s a fight that he should have taken by now, given that he was soundly beaten by the Cuban talent in the 2020 Olympics.

Cruz has been calling him “My son” since he turned pro, trying to instigate a fight. Keyshawn has shown no desire to get back in the ring with him, which looks bad for him. Why fight the likes of Jamaine, Nahir and Miguel Madueno when you’ve got Cruz, a guy that beat you four times? It comes across like Keyshawn has a confidence issue holding him back. If that is the case, Hearn would be signing a problem.

“I don’t have anything at contractual stage with Shakur Stevenson or Keyshawn Davis, but I would love to sign both,” said Hearn in an interview with iFL TV. He confirmed he had spoken to both fighters and said he would like to work with their teams.

With Anthony Joshua getting old and nearing the end, and Andy Cruz’s contract with Matchroom coming to an end, Hearn needs new blood to replace them. Losing Cruz would be a disaster because he’s only now on the cusp of winning a world title, and unlike Joshua, he’s at the top of his game and still young.

Sports.title: Ben Shalom Blindsided by Bakole’s Netflix Fight
Sports.content:
Things are already looking bleak for heavyweight Martin Bakole’s comeback fight on December 11th. He’s supposed to be fighting unbeaten Solomon Adebayo on the undercard of Tyson Fury vs. Anthony Joshua in Cardiff, Wales. It might not happen, though.

Bakole’s promoter, Ben Shalmon of BOXXER, reportedly found out after the fact that he’s on the card, and believes he’s still under contract with his company. According to Yahoo Sports, he’s going to alert his lawyers.

It’s fair to say few fans in the States have heard of Adebayo, so Bakole fighting him isn’t going to add much interest to the Fury vs. Joshua card. If Dana White of Zuffa gave the green light to Bakole’s fight with Adebayo, he’s misjudged the average fan. They’re not going to be excited to learn Bakole is fighting this guy. It is good that Bakole is finally fighting after a year out of the ring, because he hasn’t seen action since May 2025.

I can see why Shalom wouldn’t be pleased, especially if Bakole comes in out of shape and loses. Whatever value he still has would further plummet. He looked terrible getting knocked out by Joseph Parker in the 2nd round in February 2025. He looked equally bad in fighting to a questionable 10-round draw last year in May.

At this point, it’s hard to pick Bakole to beat anyone in absolute certainty, because he’s not the same fighter given his battle of the bulge he’s been dealing with.

“I saw the announcement at the same time you did,” said Shalom, as reported by Darshan Desai of Uncrowned. Shalom told Desai that BOXXER’s position on Bakole’s contract remains the same as it was in the spring.

Bakole’s weight was above or just below 300. He was way too heavy for an athlete to compete at that level. A fight was mentioned: Bakole vs. Guido Vianello on the Oleksandr Usyk vs. Rico Verhoeven undercard in Egypt, which BOXXER wanted for him. He didn’t agree to the fight, according to Darshan Desai, because he believed his contract was up.

It may have been a good thing that Bakole didn’t take that fight with Vianello. All that weight that he’s been carrying around since his upset win over Jared Anderson would be a real anchor, making him a sitting duck for a well-conditioned Vianello. I mean, I wouldn’t take that fight either if I were Bakole, weighing over 300 pounds. I hate to say it, but the Italian Olympian would be too much for him.

The question is, if Shalmon gets his way in blocking Bakole from fighting on the Fury-Joshua undercard, what is he going to do with him? His weight isn’t showing any signs of dropping, and he’s not getting any younger at 32.

Without him dropping a good 20-30 lbs, he ain’t beating any of the top-tier heavyweights, at least the ones that matter. Bakole has to show he can still beat contender-level fighters, because he has only one win over Jared Anderson.

Sports.title: Terence Crawford Flaunts Payment After Fans Call Him Broke
Sports.content:
Terence Crawford wants everyone to know his bank account is doing just fine without him stepping back into the ring. After some fans claimed the retired champ would eventually have to come back to boxing because he is running out of money, Crawford posted a video from a bank drive-through window to shut down that talk.

He held up a stack of checks topped with a bright yellow sticky note showing a handwritten figure of $111,353.60 before sending the deposit through, pointing out that the payout came from just a single stream of his income.

“I don’t know a lot of people that got a source of income like that… and that’s only 1 source of income,” Crawford said in the clip, which was shared by Source of Boxing on X.

Crawford walked away from the sport in December 2025 with a spotless 42-0 record right after defeating Canelo Álvarez for the undisputed super middleweight crown. Ending his career on its biggest victory naturally gave promoters an easy angle to pitch whenever comeback talk starts swirling. However, if Crawford is sitting around waiting for another $50 million payday like the massive haul he reportedly banked for the Canelo fight, he might as well forget about it.

The truth is that the first fight with Canelo was about as exciting as watching paint dry. Crawford fought a super cautious, safety-first style and showed zero interest in taking risks to make the bout entertaining.

The action dragged so badly that some fans in the stadium looked half asleep in their seats. Promoters are not lining up to hand out another mega-million check for a rematch when the original left the crowd nodding off.

If Crawford does not want to come back and volunteer for the rematch that Canelo and his trainer, Eddy Reynoso, called for after their win over Christian Mbilli, boxing will move right along without him. There are hungry go-getters like Willy Hutchinson and David Benavidez who would gladly step up to the plate to face Canelo for the final fight of his contract with Turki Alalshikh.

Sports.title: Pryor vs. Argüello: The Fight Behind the Black Bottle
Sports.content:
Aaron Pryor stopped Alexis Argüello in the 14th round at Miami’s Orange Bowl on November 12, 1982, ending his bid to become boxing’s first four-division world champion. Argüello landed one of his hardest right hands in the 13th. Sixty-six seconds into the next round, the unbeaten WBA junior welterweight champion had him helpless against the ropes.

Argüello entered as a 12-to-5 favorite despite moving up to challenge a champion who had stopped every man he’d defended against. At 30, the Nicaraguan had won world titles at featherweight, junior lightweight and lightweight. Pryor, 27, had taken his belt from Antonio Cervantes in 1980 and defended it five times. Argüello came to Miami chasing a fourth title. Pryor had his chance to beat one of the most accomplished fighters in the sport.

Pryor pressed from the opening bell, coming in fast and throwing several punches at a time. The taller Argüello stood his ground and looked for the straight right as Pryor crossed into range. When Argüello landed it cleanly, he could knock Pryor off his line of attack. He then had to get his feet set again before Pryor came back with another combination.

That made the early rounds difficult to score. Pryor could spend much of a round forcing the action, only for Argüello to land its hardest punch. Argüello also worked the body, where he found a target as Pryor leaned in to throw. “I never took harder shots to the body,” said Pryor afterward, as reported by The Washington Post.

A cut opened over Argüello’s left eye in the sixth. He continued to find Pryor with counters, and some of his best work came between the ninth and 11th rounds. Pryor kept coming forward, but every time he closed the distance he gave Argüello another chance to time him. A hard right in the 11th snapped Pryor’s head back. Argüello found him with another in the 13th, a shot heavy enough to make the final two rounds look dangerous for the champion.

Pryor was still ahead on two of the three cards after 13 rounds. Referee Stanley Christodoulou and judge Ove Ovesen both had him up 127–124. Ken Morita had Argüello ahead 127–125. The challenger had made the fight close enough that the last two rounds could decide it, and he had just shown he could still hurt Pryor with his best punch.

Pryor took the initiative as soon as the 14th began. A combination hurt Argüello and sent him back toward the ropes. Pryor followed him there and kept throwing, landing right hands as Argüello’s gloves dropped. The challenger was still on his feet when Christodoulou stepped between them at 1:06. Argüello slumped to the canvas after the stoppage. Pryor had made his sixth successful defense.

The black bottle controversy

“Give me the other bottle, the one I mixed,” said trainer Panama Lewis between the 13th and 14th rounds, as captured by HBO’s microphones. Pryor drank from the bottle. The recording caught Lewis asking for it immediately after Argüello’s big round, and viewers saw Pryor overwhelm him on the other side of that break. The bottle was never tested, and the Miami Boxing Commission collected no post-fight urine sample.

Lewis told The Washington Post that he had mixed Perrier and tap water to settle Pryor’s stomach. Bill Miller, Argüello’s manager, filed a protest with the WBA and the Miami Boxing Commission, alleging that Pryor had been given an illegal substance. Pryor denied wrongdoing. Before the rematch, he told United Press International he had been available for a urine test for two hours after the fight. The official result stood.

Lewis was banned from boxing in 1983 for tampering with Luis Resto’s gloves before his fight with Billy Collins Jr. Years later, Resto said in the documentary Assault in the Ring that Lewis had put crushed pills in his water. Resto was describing what happened in his own corner. The contents of Pryor’s bottle remain unknown.

Pryor wins the rematch in 10 rounds

Pryor and Argüello met again at Caesars Palace in Las Vegas on September 9, 1983. With Lewis out of his corner, Pryor dropped Argüello in the first and fourth rounds. All three judges had Pryor ahead when he knocked Argüello out in the 10th.

The Ring chose their first meeting as its Fight of the Decade for the 1980s. That night in Miami, Argüello came within two rounds of a decision in his bid for a fourth title. His right hand was still getting through in the 13th, and two judges still had Pryor ahead. The champion had spent the night making Argüello work whenever he wanted room to punch. In the 14th, Pryor finally drove him somewhere he couldn’t get it back.

Ghana News.title: NPA reduces price floor for petrol to GH¢13.69, but increases diesel to GH¢16.73
Ghana News.content:
The price of petrol per litre is expected to fall further from November 16, 2026, by some significant margin, while that of diesel could rise

This is coming after the National Petroleum Authority, together with industry players, reviewed the price floor for petrol from GH¢15.39 per litre to GH¢13.69 for the November 16 to 30, 2026, pricing window.

This actually represents an almost 13 percent decline from the old price quotes that the NPA put out some two weeks ago.

On the other hand, diesel will go up from the old price floor of GH¢17.41 to GH¢16.73 per litre.

LPG will also witness a significant increase, from GH¢13.73 per kilogramme to GH¢15.93.

According to the NPA, this excludes premiums charged by International Oil Trading Companies, operating margins of Bulk Import, Distribution and Export Companies, and margins charged by Oil Marketing Companies and LPG Marketing Companies.

The respective companies will determine those charges independently under the prescribed Petroleum Products Pricing Formula.

Implications

The adjustments could produce mixed price movements at the pumps during the next pricing window.

Lower price floors could give marketers room to reduce petrol and LPG prices. However, final adjustments will depend on the premiums and margins individual companies apply.

However, based on past developments, there are strong indications that the price of petrol could go down further, while that of diesel and LPG may go up.

Some of the oil marketing firms have already indicated that they will drop the price of petrol and even that of diesel.

The major oil marketing firm, Star Oil, for instance, had reduced prices three times over the past week and is now selling a litre of petrol at GH¢15.55 and diesel going for GH¢18.37.

Another player in the industry, Allied Oil, has also reviewed prices at the pumps, selling a litre of petrol at GH¢15.50 and diesel at GH¢18.20.

JP has also reduced its petrol price from GH¢16.43 quoted on October 16 to GH¢15.95. The price of diesel has also been reduced to GH¢18.35 from GH¢18.97.

Under the current regulations governing the pricing of petroleum products, prices are supposed to be reviewed on the 1st and 16th of each month.

However, the NPA has maintained that oil marketing companies can proceed with price reviews at the pumps, provided the adjustments are in line with the guidelines sanctioned by the market regulator.

The Ghana cedi has been fairly stable, while the International Energy Agency has projected that global oil markets will swing to supply surplus for the first time since the start of the Iran War as Persian Gulf exports recover.

Background

The Chamber of Oil Marketing Companies (COMAC) attributed the mixed reviews in prices of petroleum products to the cedi’s appreciation and the reduced prices of finished petroleum products and crude oil on the international market.

Ghana News.title: Ecobank JoyBusiness SME Fair 2026: Day 2 promises more shopping deals, networking and excitement
Ghana News.content:
The Ecobank JoyBusiness SME Fair 2026 enters its second day on Saturday, November 14, with shoppers, families and business enthusiasts expected at Ghud Park, Accra Mall, to explore a wide range of Ghanaian products and services.

The first day of the three-day exhibition ended on a high note on Friday, drawing attention to the growing range of businesses using the platform to reach new customers, promote their brands and expand their market presence.

Powered by Joy News in callabortion with Ecobank, the fair has brought together more than 80 brands across food and beverages, fashion, beauty, agriculture, technology, finance, household products, real estate and other sectors.

From locally processed foods and fresh farm produce to clothing, cosmetics, electronics and digital business solutions, the exhibition offers visitors the opportunity to discover and purchase products from different businesses at one location.

Food and beverage exhibitors include Didi Shito, Corki Ventures, Gold Coast Foods' Sankofa Spices, Manellah Foods, Adjoor Ventures, Yaapee Royal Foods and Nutrismart Ventures.

Visitors can also sample or purchase products from Delsoy, Orave Juices, Jussvina Drinks, Koa Impact Commerce, Pinnacle Coco and Green Cup, among others.

Fashion and beauty businesses are equally well represented, with brands such as Haute Xklusive, La Robe Classique, Regy Couture, Kofikyere Klothing, Asangenta, Haus of Lush and RNS Beauty displaying their products.

Technology and digital services also feature prominently. Galop Sea Limited is showcasing laptops and accessories, while Xfromo Hypermart has mobile phones and accessories, including Google Pixel devices. Katon 360 Technologies is presenting a digital platform for SMEs, with Solid Connect exhibiting an application designed for artisans.

Other exhibitors include Atlantic Meridian EV, showcasing electric vehicles; Sintex Tank, offering water storage solutions; and DBS, which specialises in housing and roofing products.

Ecobank, MTN, the Ghana Export Promotion Authority (GEPA) and Glico Life are among the major institutions participating in the fair.

Entertainment and business opportunities

Joy Prime's KMJ and content creator Quecy Official are expected to add to the atmosphere, engaging exhibitors and patrons as the exhibition attracts attention from shoppers and audiences.

Beyond the shopping experience, the fair provides participating businesses with an opportunity to introduce their products to new customers, generate sales and establish contacts that could lead to future partnerships.

The initiative, organised by the Multimedia Group in partnership with Ecobank, is also intended to give small and medium-sized enterprises greater visibility and access to the market.

The 2026 edition builds on the maiden fair held at the same venue in October 2025.

With two days remaining, patrons are being encouraged to visit Ghud Park, interact with the entrepreneurs behind the brands and take advantage of the variety of products and services on display.

The fair continues on Saturday and Sunday, November 14 and 15, at Ghud Park, Accra Mall.

Ghana News.title: US flights resume after FAA lifts hours-long nationwide ground stop
Ghana News.content:
The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has lifted a nationwide ground stop that halted departing flights across the United States for more than four hours after a “communication issue” affected air traffic control centres.

The FAA announced at 8:15pm Eastern time on Friday (01:15 GMT on Saturday) that it had lifted the order, after it issued the ground stop hours earlier at 3:54pm (20:54 GMT).

Airlines face delays and cancellations as they get aircraft and crews back into position.

The FAA said in a post on X in the afternoon that there had been a “temporary telecommunications outage” and that, as a precaution, all flights were being halted.

International flights would be handled case by case, it added.

More than 10,000 flights were delayed and over 4,000 cancelled, according to FlightAware, CBS News reported.Some 4,042 flights were in the air, heading to US airports, when the ground stop was ordered, according to the tracking site Flightradar24.

The communication issue affected all 22 air route traffic control centres, which guide aircraft.

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin told reporters there was no indication that the ground stop was triggered by a threat to the US.

“Everybody’s safe. The flights are accounted for,” he said. “This is not another 9/11.”

Trump’s silence questioned

US President Donald Trump has not addressed the situation and has remained absent from the public scene since the FAA announced the ground stop.

Trump has been “fully engaged” in responding to the nationwide flight shutdown, Mullin said after a reporter asked during a White House news conference why the president had not spoken publicly about the disruption.

“I don’t run the president’s comms,” Mullin replied, saying Trump had been in regular contact with senior officials since the crisis began.

Mullin also said the president had spoken with officials multiple times and had been briefed on developments throughout the disruption.

The homeland security secretary also defended Trump, saying the president had been pushing for an overhaul of the country’s ageing air traffic control infrastructure.

Passengers wait as flights are delayed at Seattle-Tacoma international airport in Seattle, Washington, on November 13, 2026 [Lindsey Wasson/AP]

Asked whether a planned rollout of a new AI tool meant to help air traffic controllers could be to blame, Mullin said officials have not ruled it out. “You just can’t rule out anything at this point. We are going through that process,” he said.

The FBI does not believe a cyberattack or criminal activity caused the failure, Bloomberg reported, citing an official familiar with the matter.

The cited official said investigators were examining whether a software update could have caused the outage, though the cause had not been determined.

Democratic Senator Tammy Duckworth has called for a “thorough and complete investigation” of the reported FAA communication issues.

“The safety of our skies is built on redundancies. Whatever led to the nationwide ground stop will warrant a thorough and complete investigation,” Duckworth wrote in a post on X.

“As Aviation Subcommittee Ranking Member, I’ll be demanding answers from the FAA,” she added.

The disruption is the latest sign of strain on the US air traffic control system, which has ⁠been beset by equipment failures, communications problems and ⁠shortages of controllers, as the FAA tries to replace ageing infrastructure.

Air Space Intelligence (ASI), the company behind the FAA’s AI-powered air traffic management system, said its technology was not responsible for the nationwide ground stop.

Travellers wait at Dallas Fort Worth international airport in Texas on November 13, 2026, after the Federal Aviation Administration grounded flights nationwide [Tony Gutierrez/AP]

“The current ground stop is not based on or a result of the SMART system, any product of ASI or our integration with FAA and ATC,” the company said in a post on X.

The FAA awarded ASI an $875m contract in June to develop and deploy the SMART system, which uses artificial intelligence to support air traffic management.

The agency announced an expansion of the system across its 22 air traffic control centres on November 10, just days before the nationwide flight suspension.

US rail service affected

Amtrak, the US national rail operator, announced that its website and app are showing error messages and that customers are having difficulty reaching a representative, as it faces higher-than-normal call volumes because of the nationwide disruption to air travel.

“We apologize for the error messages on both our website and app, as well as the difficulty reaching a representative,” Amtrak said in a post on X in response to a complaint.

“We’re currently experiencing higher-than-normal call volumes due to ongoing airline issues,” the company said.

It recommended that customers try the services later.

Passengers wait as flights are delayed inside a terminal at Seattle-Tacoma international airport on November 13, 2026, in Seattle, Washington [Lindsey Wasson/AP]

Pilot and former FAA safety team representative Kyle Bailey told Al Jazeera: “Whether you are an expert or not, the bottom line is we’re still trying to piece the puzzle together, and it would be impossible to have an answer to the issue quickly, in a few hours at least.”

“But it is very alarming what we saw, and possibly [rail operator] Amtrak is being affected too,” he added. “The FAA’s priority at the moment is keeping not only the American passenger safe, but everyone flying in the US flight system.”

Bailey said that “halting the flights on the ground is the safest thing to do until they could figure out what’s going on. If anybody says they think they know what’s causing this problem at such an early stage, they’re not being honest”.

Congress approved $12.5bn for the overhaul last year, and the Department of Transportation and the White House asked lawmakers on Friday for ⁠another $30.1bn.

This was the first nationwide US ground stop since January 2023, when a key FAA computer system malfunctioned. Before that, the last time had been after the September 11, 2001, attacks.

US authorities have yet to determine the cause of the telecommunications outage that prompted the ground stop.

Ghana News.title: Arrested generals and a threatened VP: President’s son fuels Ugandan succession fever
Ghana News.content:
In Uganda's military, even senior generals are finding that their rank offers little protection from the wrath of the country's powerful army chief.

Over the past 15 months, at least a dozen generals and senior officers have been arrested under Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba, who is also the son of President Yoweri Museveni, in a crackdown that has unsettled the military's top ranks.

The arrests come amid growing political tensions over who will succeed Museveni, who has ruled Uganda for four decades.

Gen Kainerugaba, 52, is widely seen as a potential successor, although his ambitions appear to be facing resistance within the ruling party.

This week, he threatened Vice-President Jessica Alupo with dismissal and possible arrest, while suggesting he should take her position.

The ruling National Resistance Movement (NRM) has, however, rejected reports that its senior leadership had rejected a proposal to back Gen Kainerugaba as the next president, describing the claims as "completely false".

This has all fuelled speculation that the arrests are part of an effort to sideline military officers opposed to the general's presidential ambitions.

Others see the arrests as evidence of an anti-corruption drive in which senior commanders are held to account.

At the centre of the tension are two powerful powerful institutions: the military, where Gen Kainerugaba wields considerable influence, and the NRM, where questions about his political ambitions appear to be dividing senior figures.

A recent meeting of NRM's top leadership ended without agreement on a proposal to position Gen Kainerugaba as Museveni's successor, according to the AFP news agency.

Five party sources who attended the closed-door meeting told AFP that a vote was abandoned after several members spoke against the proposal.

Uganda's news website ChimpReports, however, said that most members who spoke backed the general's potential presidency, although some questioned his readiness for civilian leadership.

In a statement on Thursday, NRM Secretary General Richard Todwong Awany confirmed that the party had met on 10 November to discuss "political, social and economic issues".

He dismissed reports that the meeting had rejected a proposal to position Gen Kainerugaba as Uganda's next president, saying the party would communicate any decisions "through the right channel, at the right time".

President Yoweri Museveni's grandson (standing up, shaking the president's hand) has joined the army, alongside his father (sitting down, wearing camouflage)

Dr Gerald Bareebe, a Ugandan-born political scientist at Canada's York University, sees a connection between the arrests and political manoeuvring over Museveni's succession, often referred to as the "Muhoozi Project".

"Senior officers believed not to support the project have been arrested, detained or charged with corruption and treason," he tells the BBC.

He says the allegations against some officers were widely viewed as politically motivated, reflecting growing divisions within the military over the succession question.

Some of those detained have since been released, apparently after securing the general's forgiveness.

The detention of one of the country's most prominent former commanders, Lt Gen Peter Elwelu, has brought the crackdown into sharper focus.

The former deputy army chief was detained on 2 November over allegations that he had plotted to destabilise the eastern Teso region.

His fall from grace followed a series of social media posts by Kainerugaba, who accused him of treachery and announced that he had been stripped of his three-star rank and demoted.

"The traitor Peter Elwelu is hereby stripped of his ranks. He is demoted to Private," Kainerugaba wrote on X.

He also claimed that more than 20 soldiers linked to Elwelu had been arrested.

The announcement raised legal questions, with Ugandan media reporting that military regulations do not allow a senior officer to be stripped of his rank through a social media post.

The army later confirmed Elwelu's detention, saying they had recovered 15 guns, military uniforms and two pickup trucks linked to him. His family has rejected the allegations.

Elwelu is among at least a dozen generals and senior officers detained since April 2025, according to an investigation by Uganda's Daily Monitor newspaper.

They include three former military intelligence chiefs who once oversaw some of Uganda's most sensitive security operations.Maj Gen James Birungi, a former head of defence intelligence and security, was arrested in August 2025, on allegations including treason, terrorism and corruption.

He was charged before a military court but later released after Gen Kainerugaba announced that he had "forgiven" him.

Another former intelligence chief, Maj Gen Abel Kandiho, was detained in September this year over allegations of providing false intelligence and treachery. He remains in detention, according to the Daily Monitor.

His predecessor, Brig-Gen Charles Bakahumura, was also arrested in September over similar allegations, but was later released after the army chief announced that he had forgiven him.

Other officers have faced accusations ranging from stealing military fuel to taking money to spy on military communications.

The military has defended the arrests as part of efforts to tackle corruption and criminality within the armed forces.

Maj Gen James Birungi was arrested in August 2025, on allegations including treason, terrorism and corruption

Ugandan security analyst Freddie David Egesa says the arrests reflect investigations involving different security agencies, rather than an army-led purge.

He argues that detaining senior officers helps protect witnesses and demonstrates the seriousness of the anti-corruption drive.

"Gen Muhoozi has the overall duty to permit the investigation team to arrest these high-profile people, in consultation with the commander-in-chief," Egesa says, adding: "The arrests are not summarily done."

But Bareebe sees a wider political motive, arguing that officers suspected of opposing to Gen Kainerugaba's presidential ambitions are being targeted.

"The result is a broad purge that has affected both serving and retired officers perceived to be anti-Muhoozi," he says.

He points to divisions between the elite Special Forces Command (SFC), which he says is largely loyal to the president's son, and army commanders who remain unconvinced about his succession.

The allegations against the officers are at different stages, with some facing charges, others in detention without publicly announced charges, and several having been released.

Bareebe also questions whether military trials can deliver independent proceedings.

"Many Ugandans regard the charges as politically motivated and therefore expect little justice," he adds.

He alleges that some officers have had charges dropped after closed-door negotiations with the president and his son, during which they were pressured to declare support for Gen Kainerugaba.

Government spokesperson Allan Kasujja dismissed the claims of a succession fallout as "hogwash".

Unlike his predecessors, who communicated through official military channels, Gen Kainerugaba frequently uses X to announce arrests, criticise public officials and comment on domestic and international affairs. Some have sparked diplomatic controversy.

On the night of 9 November, he turned his attention to Vice-President Jessica Alupo, demanding to take her job.

"Whoever is in that office should prepare to hand it over soon," he wrote, in posts that he later deleted.

He also questioned Alupo's loyalty and threatened her dismissal, adding that the government would operate "on military terms", if he became his father's deputy.

The following day, his X account, which had nearly 1.4 million followers, became inaccessible.

It was unclear whether he deactivated it himself, which he has done before, or the platform had suspended it.

Alupo remains in office and has yet to respond publicly.

Vice-President Jessica Alupo is yet to respond to Gen Kainerugaba's posts questioning her loyalty

Egesa says Gen Kainerugaba's controversial posts reflect his preferred style of communicating, but adds that security analysts are assessing their implications for Uganda's political and military stability.

Bareebe, however, sees them as part of a broader effort by the army chief to extend his influence into civilian politics.

He says the public confrontation with senior political figures illustrates how the succession debate was spilling beyond the army and into the ruling party.

Gen Kainerugaba was appointed army chief in March 2024, after previously commanding the SFC, which is responsible for protecting the president and strategic installations.

Under Uganda's military structure, he reports directly to Museveni, giving him considerable influence over the army.

Bareebe argues that the SFC's loyalty to the president and his son could prove crucial in any future transfer of power.

"The regular army remains important but has been sidelined by the SFC, which now functions as a personal army for Museveni and his son," he adds.

At the heart of the tension is the question of who will succeed Museveni, 82, who has ruled Uganda since 1986, when his rebel National Resistance Army seized power after a five-year guerrilla war.

He was sworn in for a seventh elected presidential term earlier this year, extending his rule into a fifth decade.

Gen Kainerugaba has been regarded as a possible successor and has indicated that he intends to seek the presidency in 2031, when his father's current term is due to end.

He also leads the Patriotic League of Uganda, a political movement that has mobilised support around his leadership.

But recent developments suggest that a transfer of power from father to son may be more complicated than his supporters anticipated.

At the recent meeting of the NRM leadership, one official reportedly urged Museveni to retire his son from the military and give him a civilian role to gain administrative experience, AFP reported.

Local media reported that some party officials consider Gen Salim Saleh, Museveni's younger brother, better suited for civilian leadership.

There is, however, no indication that he is interested in becoming president.

Others reportedly defended Gen Kainerugaba, pointing to his military leadership, anti-corruption campaign and grassroots political mobilisation.

Bareebe says opposition to the proposed succession has grown within the NRM, with both veteran figures and younger members concerned about what they see as an attempt to secure power through coercion.

He suggests Museveni's reluctance to move his son out of the military could reflect the importance of retaining control of the army during any transition.

"The underlying calculation appears to be that, so long as Muhoozi controls the SFC, he can use it to capture power even in an event of a contested transition," he says.

The military has been central to Museveni's hold on power, making the loyalties of senior commanders particularly important as succession questions intensify.

The family's military influence has also drawn attention to the possibility of a political dynasty spanning generations, with Gen Kainerugaba's son, Ruhamya, recently graduating from Britain's Sandhurst military academy.

The succession debate is unfolding against a backdrop of sustained pressure on the opposition.

Veteran opposition politician Kizza Besigye remains in detention on treason charges, which he denies.

Bobi Wine, who came second to Museveni in this year's presidential election, has gone into exile in the US, after being threatened by Gen Kainerugaba.

The government has consistently defended its security operations as lawful and necessary to maintain stability.

For now, Museveni remains in power.

But the arrests, his son's threats and competing accounts of divisions within the ruling party have intensified questions about how Uganda's next political transition might unfold, and what role his family may play.
