World.title: Iran Guards say two oil tankers hit by mines in Hormuz
World.content:
Tehran: Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said on Saturday that explosions rang out on two oil tankers after they struck mines in the Strait of Hormuz, where Tehran has restricted navigation.

Since war erupted with the United States in February, Tehran has insisted that vessels obtain its authorization to cross the strait and has attacked ships that do not comply.

“A short while ago, two oil tankers that had switched off their radar and positioning systems and were secretly attempting to transit the Strait of Hormuz through an unauthorized route exploded and caught fire after striking a naval mine,” the Guards’ navy said in a statement carried by the Iranian state broadcaster early on Saturday.

The statement did not provide the names or origins of the vessels but said one was a supertanker.

The United States, in response to Tehran’s choking of the strategic trade route, has imposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports and provides military support to tankers using the waterway.

In recent weeks, Iran’s armed forces have reported several fires or explosions on board ships in the strait, often saying the vessels had struck mines.

On Friday, the Guards released footage of a large plume of smoke rising from a vessel it said was carrying liquefied gas and hit a mine in the south of the strait.

The US military, however, says it has cleared the main routes through the waterway of mines.

World.title: Saudi Arabia’s latest archaeological puzzle: Interlocking circles in Al-Qunfudhah
World.content:
JEDDAH: Interlocking circular stone formations discovered through aerial imagery in Al-Qunfudhah governorate, in southwestern Saudi Arabia, have drawn researchers' attention to a potentially ancient site whose unusual geometric patterns may have served a mathematical or astronomical purpose.

Photographs captured by the Saudi Press Agency (SPA) in the Hali area of Al-Qunfudhah show rings of varying sizes and configurations built from local volcanic rock, forming overlapping patterns that are difficult to distinguish from ground level.

Historian and researcher Dr. Mohammed Al-Marhabi told SPA that the precision and arrangement of the formations suggest deliberate design rather than random placement. He said their layout does not indicate residential or burial use and proposed that they may have been used to observe weather patterns, seasonal changes or celestial movements.

Aerials photographs show rings of varying sizes and configurations built from local volcanic rock, forming overlapping patterns that are difficult to distinguish from ground level. (SPA photo)

Al-Marhabi linked the formations to Hali's long history of human settlement, noting that its fertile valley was an important population center with historical ties to Makkah. Local communities also had traditions of tracking seasons and calendars, he said.

He called for specialized archaeological research to establish the structures' origins and function.

Al-Qunfudhah lies along Saudi Arabia's Red Sea coast in the Tihamah region of Makkah Province, south of Jeddah. Hali is among the historically significant valleys in the area.

Clues from ancient Arabia

The discovery adds to a growing body of archaeological evidence showing that ancient communities across the Arabian Peninsula developed distinctive stone structures for different purposes.

In July 2024, the Royal Commission for AlUla (RCU) announced findings from research identifying Neolithic stone circles in northwestern Saudi Arabia as dwellings dating to the sixth and fifth millennia BC.

The structures, measuring between four and eight meters in diameter, consisted of vertically erected stone slabs arranged in two rows around their circumference. Researchers believe the stones served as foundations for wooden columns supporting roofs, possibly covered with animal skins.

Tools, animal remains and evidence of jewelry-making and trade suggested that the inhabitants had more settled and developed communities than previously understood, with commercial links extending toward Jordan and areas along the Red Sea.

At an ancient dwelling in AlUla, stone slabs erected in two rows in the outer circumference of the circle appear to have been used as foundations for wooden columns that were used to support the roof, with a slab in the center of the circle to support the main wooden column. (RCU photo via SPA)

In another major discovery announced in November 2024, archaeologists identified a Bronze Age settlement at Khaybar Oasis in northwestern Saudi Arabia. Known as Al-Natah, the 2.6-hectare town was inhabited by an estimated 500 people between 2400 and 1500 BC, with some uncertainty in the settlement's occupation phases.

The oasis was surrounded by a 15-kilometer-long stone wall, while the settlement contained residential and funerary areas, narrow pathways and multi-story dwellings.

The research, conducted under the RCU's Khaybar Longue Durée Archaeological Project with French partners, challenged earlier assumptions that nomadic pastoralism was the dominant way of life in the region during the Bronze Age.

Together, the discoveries highlight the diversity and sophistication of ancient Arabian societies. Researchers say further investigation of the Hali formations could help determine whether they represent another distinctive example of the region's early architectural and scientific practices.

World.title: Federal Aviation Administration says airplane departures can resume following nationwide ground stop
World.content:
WASHINGTON: The Federal Aviation Administration said Friday night that airplane departures can resume after the agency lifted a nationwide ground stop that Trump administration officials blamed on “overloaded,” “outdated” systems.

Even with the order being lifted, the airlines will not be able to return to normal operations immediately because so many of their planes and crews are out of position.

The FAA had grounded all flights nationwide Friday afternoon, causing hundreds of flights to be diverted. Officials cited “extraordinary circumstances” caused by communications problems at regional air traffic control centers.

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin told reporters at the White House that the introduction of some new technology into an old air traffic control system overwhelmed it.

The nationwide ground stop was the first since January 2023, when a key FAA computer system malfunctioned, and the second since the aftermath of the Sept. 11, 2001, attacks.

There was no indication the communications failure was related to a cyberattack. The consequences were profound, disrupting potentially thousands of planned flights through at least late Friday night and upending travel plans for passengers.

“It’s frustrating. This certainly sounds like it’s going to be more than the usual run-of-the-mill delay. I look forward to finding out why,” said Jeff Dubner, a Washington attorney whose Alaska Airlines flight home from Los Angeles was already half an hour late and taxiing to the runway when the plane came to a halt.

International flights were being handled on a case-by-case basis, according to Mullin, with some seen taking off Friday evening.

Top official says no sign yet of nefarious act

Asked whether Mullin could rule out a cyberattack or rogue artificial intelligence incident, he said: “There’s nothing completely certain right now. It doesn’t appear that way.” He said there are no “footprints” showing an attack and that it appears to be “mechanically driven,” adding that officials were still looking for the cause.

At least 827 flights were diverted so far as a result. As of 7:05 p.m. EST, 670 flights were sent back to the airport from where they originally took off, while 157 were redirected to a different airport, according to Cirium, an aviation analytics company.

The airports where many of the flights ended up being diverted included Washington Dulles International Airport, Los Angeles International Airport, Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky International Airport and Nashville International Airport.

Some 11,000 flights carrying more than 1.5 million passengers were scheduled to take off from airports in the US after 4 p.m. EST, raising the likelihood of more cancelations and flight diversions.

At Chicago O’Hare Airport on Friday afternoon, travelers passing through security learned about the ground stop when they looked up at screens that showed flight delays across the board.

Some called friends or family members, debating whether to stay the night in Chicago or find another way to their destinations.

Amber McQuilkin, 27, sat on a bench, disappointed that she might miss a trip with friends to New York for the League of Legends world finals. Her friends, she said, had already arrived there.

“There’s not really any information being passed to me,” said the Seattle software engineer, who took a week of vacation for the trip. “I contemplated just abandoning the flight and driving, but then the more I thought about it, the more I’m like, that would be miserable.”

Austin Curtis and his wife were rethinking their trip from South Bend, Indiana, to a friend’s baby shower in Denver after getting delayed during a layover in Chicago.

They had boarded a flight to Denver from O’Hare International Airport when they were told to get off the plane.

“We did see them taking luggage off our plane and others, so we’re assuming it’s going to be a pretty substantial delay,” Curtis said.

They were unsure whether to get a hotel room or keep waiting out the delay at the airport. With care already in place for their two young children at home, they might stay the weekend in Chicago, he said.

Sports teams stranded and cargo flights delayed

NBA, NHL and college teams were left stranded as they tried to reach their destinations. Meanwhile, NFL teams were left to wonder whether the issue would be resolved in time to travel to their games this weekend.

Cargo flights were also delayed by the ground stop.

FedEx, the world’s largest cargo airline, said it is prepared to activate contingency plans to keep any possible disruptions at a minimum.

US airlines move about 61,000 tons of goods – from letters to packages — to and from more than 220 countries daily, according to the industry trade group Airlines for America.

Despite the nationwide FAA ground stop, SpaceX launched its Starship rocket from Texas on Friday afternoon on its latest test flight.

The government has been working to overhaul outdated technology

Mullin had said investigators will look at whether there is any link to the FAA’s nationwide rollout of a new artificial intelligence system to help identify problems and reroute planes. But that system operates out of one location near Washington, D.C., and just sends recommendations to the air traffic control centers.

The government has been working to overhaul the outdated technology that air traffic controllers rely on since Congress approved $12.5 billion for the project last year. Miles of old copper wires have been replaced with fiber optic lines and old radio systems are gradually being replaced at airports across the country.

But much work remains. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy has said that another $30 billion will be needed to complete the work, and the White House has begun lobbying Congress to approve it.

The problem appeared similar to a regional air traffic control communication outage in September that snarled hundreds of flights across the Northeast, aviation safety expert Steve Arroyo said, except this time on a nationwide scale. It may be linked to the outdated technology used by air traffic controllers.

“If you don’t have that ability, whether it’s because the old wires that they have are just run down or for whatever reason, you’ve got to stop airplanes on the ground,” said Arroyo, who is a former United Airlines pilot. “And not put them in the air where you’re going to risk not being able to communicate with them.”

Friday’s ground stop was different than the one after Sept. 11 because planes were not being told to land immediately and pilots likely were able to communicate with ground controllers at airports, Arroyo said.

World.title: Riyadh Air completes first Airbus A321neo as it expands fleet and global network
World.content:
RIYADH: Riyadh Air has completed manufacturing of its first Airbus A321neo narrow-body aircraft, marking another milestone in the Saudi carrier’s fleet expansion as it builds a mixed fleet of Airbus and Boeing aircraft to support its international growth ambitions.

The aircraft, registered as HZ-RXFA, emerged from Airbus’ paint facility in Hamburg, Germany, on Friday in the airline’s signature pearl livery, according to an announcement carried by the Saudi Press Agency (SPA).

Its design draws inspiration from Saudi heritage, combining flowing lines modeled on traditional Bedouin tents with elements reflecting Arabic calligraphy. The exterior features shades of indigo and lavender, feather-inspired patterns on the rear fuselage and a dark frame around the cockpit windows.

The Riyadh Air name appears in both Arabic and English, reflecting the airline’s identity and its emphasis on Saudi culture and heritage.

The aircraft is scheduled to undergo a series of test flights in the coming days before delivery and its eventual arrival at its operational base in Riyadh. The airline said details of its cabin design, onboard experience and destinations for its narrow-body fleet would be announced in the coming weeks.

The A321neo will complement Riyadh Air’s Boeing 787 Dreamliner fleet, which forms the backbone of its wide-body expansion strategy.

Dreamliner fleet expansion

In July, Riyadh Air and Boeing announced an agreement covering 28 additional 787 Dreamliners as part of the airline’s growth plans. The commitment included the conversion of 20 aircraft to the larger 787-10 variant and a previously undisclosed purchase of 11 jets.

Once the remaining 17 aircraft are finalized, Riyadh Air’s firm order count is expected to reach 67 Dreamliners, according to the July 20 announcement carried by SPA.

The 787-10, the largest member of Boeing’s Dreamliner family, can accommodate 50 more passengers than the 787-9 while reducing fuel consumption and emissions by 25 percent compared with the aircraft it replaces.

Riyadh Air said operating both variants would provide fleet commonality through shared flight deck systems, maintenance procedures and pilot training, helping improve operational efficiency.

The Dreamliner family also features larger windows, higher cabin humidity, lower cabin-altitude pressurization and turbulence-sensing technology designed to improve passenger comfort.

Growing international network

Riyadh Air, wholly owned by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund, began operations in June 2026 with its inaugural service to London Heathrow.

It subsequently launched direct flights to Manchester in September, making it its second destination in the United Kingdom, and increased its Heathrow schedule to nine flights weekly from Nov. 2.

The carrier also introduced direct flights to Bangkok in September, initially operating three times a week before increasing the service to daily flights on Nov. 9.

Meanwhile, bookings have opened for direct flights to Milan, with services scheduled to begin on Dec. 16 at four flights weekly. Milan will become its fifth European destination and the 15th destination available for booking across its network.

In October, the airline said it operated eight aircraft serving 14 destinations across Europe, the Middle East and Asia, and aimed to have nearly 30 destinations available for sale by the end of 2026.

Riyadh Air’s expansion supports its ambition to connect the Saudi capital to more than 100 destinations worldwide by 2030, in line with the Kingdom’s Vision 2030 economic diversification strategy.

The airline expects its operations to generate more than 200,000 direct and indirect jobs and contribute over SR75 billion (US$20 billion) to non-oil gross domestic product by 2030, according to its July announcement.

World.title: Democratic senators order Musk to preserve records over Ukraine Starlink access, WSJ reports
World.content:
WASHINGTON: Democratic ‌senators have told Elon Musk to preserve all records related to SpaceX’s restrictions on Ukraine’s use of its Starlink ​and Starshield satellite services, The Wall Street Journal reported on Friday, citing a letter.

Ukrainian forces say Starshield, the military-grade version of Starlink, is vital for front-line communications and drone operations in their defense against Russian drone and missile attacks.

But in mid-October, Ukrainian officials complained that the service had ‌been restricted without ‌explanation or warning, limiting the ​military’s ‌ability ⁠to ​conduct complicated ⁠strike missions against Russian forces and slowing interceptor drones used to shoot down Russian attack drones.

“The October and November restrictions now raise the disturbing possibility that these vulnerabilities persist even within systems on which the US government relies,” Senators Jeanne Shaheen and ⁠Chris Coons said in the letter ‌to Musk, the report ‌said.

The lawmakers sought SpaceX’s records ​since September 1, including all ‌communications related to Starlink and Starshield in Ukraine ‌as well as communications between Musk, SpaceX executives and the White House and Pentagon, the report said.

Shaheen and Coons said the restrictions raised “serious questions” about SpaceX’s control ‌over communications systems critical to national security and criticized what they described as “opaque decision-making,” ⁠according ⁠to the Journal.

Reuters reported in October that an order to limit Starshield service used by Ukrainian forces came from inside the White House. Secretary of State Marco Rubio later disputed that account, saying decisions on Ukraine’s access to the service were up to SpaceX and Musk.

Later that month Ukraine said Starlink and Starshield were operating normally. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Thursday, however, ​that Ukrainian military units ​had again recorded disruptions to Starshield communications.

World.title: Rubio says further US military action is not needed against economically weakened Iran
World.content:
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Friday that further US military action against Iran is unnecessary because the economic pain the US is inflicting on a weakened Islamic Republic is so great.

Rubio’s comment in a speech to the Federalist Society reinforced a statement by US President Donald Trump earlier in the week that the war “militarily is effectively over.”

“And right now, frankly, the economic pain that we are inflicting on that regime is so great that there’s no need for military action because we’ve weakened them so much,” Rubio said. “But I think victory is ensuring that they never have a nuclear weapon.”

Rubio also acknowledged the economic pain Americans have experienced as a result of the war, which has driven up fuel costs and affected nearly every sector of the global economy.

It would have been easy for Trump to ignore the threat posed by Iran’s nuclear program, avoid an unpopular war and “leave it for the next person to worry about,” he said, adding that the president decided he was “not going to leave it unaddressed.”

“But it’s hard,” Rubio said. “It’s not easy and it’s difficult. And oftentimes it inflicts, you know, pain, economic pain and otherwise. So we recognize that.”

US says it intercepted Iranian drones after Iran claims strike in Bahrain

The US military said Friday it shot down two Iranian attack drones headed toward Bahrain, denying Iran’s claim that it had struck a US radar system in the kingdom. CENTCOM, the US command center covering the region, said there were no injuries or damage.

Iran’s official IRNA news agency cited a Revolutionary Guard statement that said the attack on the radar system followed a US strike on a telecommunications pole in the southern Iranian port of Sirik. It was Iran’s first report of targeting a facility in Bahrain since September.

Bahrain’s Ministry of Information did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Iran says a tanker struck a mine in the Strait of Hormuz

Iran’s Revolutionary Guard said Friday that a liquefied petroleum gas tanker struck a mine, causing an explosion, while trying to sail through the Strait of Hormuz, according to the state-run IRNA news agency.

The Guard said the vessel ignored repeated warnings while transiting the eastern part of the strait. The claim could not be independently verified.

In a related development, the United Nations said October had the highest number of incidents against commercial ships in the contested waters since February, when the Iran war began.

The UN’s International Maritime Organization said 25 seafarers died and many others were injured or remain missing following some 134 incidents in the Strait of Hormuz and the wider Middle East maritime area as of Nov. 11.

Iran: Nuclear monitoring cannot proceed while under threat

Iran told the United Nations’ nuclear watchdog that discussions on nuclear monitoring cannot proceed while the country is facing military threats.

According to a confidential report by the International Atomic Energy Agency, Iran insists inspections cannot resume amid threats from the US to target its nuclear facilities. Iran hasn’t given inspectors access to sites affected by Israeli and US strikes during the June 2025 war.

Iran warns US and Israel that renewed war would be met with ‘decisive response’

Iran’s deputy UN ambassador, Gholamhossein Darzi, told the UN Security Council Friday that its response to any renewed fighting would be “directed against the source of aggression, wherever it may be.”

Putting a damper on the prospect of new talks, he said US threats and attacks during “good faith” negotiations over the last two years “have created profound distrust and serious doubt about the prospects of renewed negotiations without credible guarantees against the repetition of such unlawful actions.”

Darzi clashed with Bahrain, which called the meeting on behalf of the six Gulf Cooperation Council countries, as well as the United States.

World.title: Survivors of the deadly Brooklyn building collapse recall shock, terror and grief
World.content:
NEW YORK: One man’s pregnant wife was pulled alive from the rubble, while two of his roommates perished. A woman living next door woke from a nap to bright daylight flooding her bedroom because her apartment wall was suddenly gone.

Survivors of the Brooklyn apartment building collapse that killed eight people wept as they recounted their terror and grief during a news conference Friday.

New York officials, from building inspectors to prosecutors, say they’re investigating what caused the three-story building to come crashing down as workers were digging at an adjacent construction site.

Those who lost family, neighbors and their homes demanded answers.

“As they’re taking me, evacuating me from the building, I could see my neighbors coming out on stretchers,” said Ciahola Lawrence, whose apartment building next to the one that collapsed had a shared wall ripped away, exposing an abyss of dust and debris below.

“We didn’t deserve this,” said Lawrence, who sobbed in her husband’s arms as she spoke with reporters.

Among the dead were two children, ages 9 and 10, according to city officials. Another 18 people were injured, including four firefighters.

‘I no longer knew where I am’

Mamadou Mouctar Balde stepped out to buy groceries Wednesday, leaving his pregnant wife and two roommates, Mamadou N’Diaye, 31, and Mamadou Barry, 23, at home. Barry was cooking and N’Diaye was sleeping on the couch, he said in French.

He returned to find firefighters, police and neighbors gathering outside and assumed there had been a traffic accident. Then a woman told him a building had collapsed.

“I didn’t see my wife. I didn’t see my friends,” Balde recalled, a tear streaking his cheek. “I no longer knew where I am.”

First responders found the bodies of N’Diaye and Barry while combing the wreckage. Balde’s wife, Fatoumata Bah, was pulled alive from the rubble after nearly 2 1/2 hours trapped beneath a hill of wood and brick. Bah was seriously injured, but she and her unborn child were doing OK, Balde said.

N’Diaye and Barry were cousins who came to the US about five years ago from Conakry, the capital of Guinea. Their uncle said their family is heartbroken.

“We ask the city and the Guinean community to stand for us, to have a justice for this tragedy,” he said.

Other victims came from Mexico, Colombia, Ecuador and Trinidad, New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani said.

New York police identified the others who died as Nicole Daniela Salvada Rodriguez, 9; Juan Daniel Salvada Guzman, 31; Kevin Santiago Reyes Gonzalez, 10; Gabriel Siguencia, 22; Edgar Sapon, 26; and Jose Luis Caguana Cosquillo, 26.

Mayor says authorities will pursue ‘any evidence of criminality’

Ahmed Tigani, commissioner of New York’s Department of Buildings, said Friday that his office is conducting “an exhaustive investigation” of the Brooklyn collapse.

The city has ordered inspections at more than 160 sites in New York that are associated with six entities linked to the construction and demolition site next to the fallen building, Mamdani said, significantly raising an earlier count of sites subject to renewed scrutiny.

“I think it is always an outrage when eight New Yorkers lose their lives, when 18 New Yorkers are hospitalized, and when families are shattered as a result of all of this,” Mamdani said.

If investigators uncover “any evidence of criminality,” Mamdani said, “it is one that we follow through to the fullest extent of the law.”

One witness who works across the street said he watched bricks fall minutes before the disaster. A woman in a neighboring building said she and fellow residents blamed vibrations from the construction for cracks that appeared in their apartment walls.

Video shows survivor descending stairs suspended over wreckage

Lawrence said the construction work had been a source of constant disruption, producing noises so loud that “you would hear that thumping and movement in your soul.”

A security camera above Lawrence’s door recorded video of her apartment’s shared wall and the building next door collapsing in a clattering rumble and a thick cloud of dust. Inside her apartment, a closet filled with hanging clothes and bags was exposed to the outside.

The security video shows Lawrence leaving her damaged home with a firefighter, who held her hand as they descended a stairway overlooking mounds of wreckage below.

“This feeling is indescribable,” Lawrence said. “I was right there.”

Zariah Coleman, who also lived in the building next to the one that collapsed, was concerned about her cat. She said Friday that she too had felt the building shake because of the construction.

“I just really hope they come and get our cat,” Coleman said in tears. “He’s hiding from them, and I think he’s scared.”

Rescue operations ended Thursday after crews spent more than a day searching for victims beneath debris removed with power saws, pickaxes and an excavator.

Building records show there were four apartments on the upper two floors and a commercial unit on the ground floor of the collapsed building.

The surrounding blocks along Flatbush Avenue, a busy Brooklyn thoroughfare, are tightly packed with older brick buildings and a few newly built apartment complexes. A mix of Caribbean and Mexican restaurants reflects the diversity of the neighborhood.

Official says prior problems that halted construction were fixed

A one-story building was demolished earlier this year on the construction site next to the collapsed building. Records show a contractor, Mordechai “Marty” Waisbrod, notified the city that excavation would begin in September and would include rock blasting. The contractor has not responded to phone messages left and emails sent to one of his Brooklyn-based businesses.

Permit applications indicated plans to dig below 15 feet (4.5 meters).

A stop work order was issued in March after inspectors concluded the demolition site lacked adequate overhead protection such as netting to protect neighboring buildings and pedestrians, according to the city’s Department of Buildings.

In April, inspectors found that the demolition work had resumed in violation of the stop work order, the department said. Work was allowed to continue after the problems were corrected, Tigani, the city buildings commissioner, said Friday.

“We’re looking at the entire history,” he said, “and if there are additional things we need to see, that will be part of the investigation.”

World.title: Trump doesn’t plan to discuss Ukraine with Xi and Putin in China but will talk about Iran war, US official says
World.content:
Trump, Xi, Putin to hold historic meeting in China on sidelines of APEC Summit

WASHINGTON: Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping will hold the first ever three-way meeting between the leaders of the United States, Russia and China at a summit in Shenzhen next week, the White House said Friday.

Trump wants to talk about reducing nuclear arsenals at the trilateral talks on Thursday and is also set to bring up his war in Iran — but he is not expected to discuss Russia’s war in Ukraine, US officials said.

The three leaders will meet on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in the southern Chinese city, White House spokeswoman Olivia Wales told reporters.

Nuclear weapons

“The president has made it clear that, among other topics, he will discuss the reduction of nuclear weapons in the world. This proliferation, President Trump believes, is very dangerous,” Wales said.

The last nuclear arms pact between Russia and the United States expired in February, removing caps on the two largest atomic arsenals for the first time in more than a half-century. When that treaty — known as New START — expired, Trump rejected a call by Russia to extend the two-country deal for another year and called for “a new, improved and modernized” deal that includes China.

The trilateral meeting is expected to serve as a start to the nuclear talks between the three leaders and no agreements are expected to be announced, according to a senior US official who briefed reporters on the condition of anonymity.

But Beijing’s arsenal of more than 600 warheads, according to Pentagon estimates, is far smaller than inventories held by the US and Russia, each estimated to have more than 5,000 warheads. With US and Russian arsenals dwarfing its stockpile, China has shown little interest in developing a nuclear pact.



Russian war on Ukraine

One of the major conflicts dominating Trump’s second term as president will feature, but the other will not, the US officials said.

“I think the president does intend to talk about Iran in the trilateral meeting with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin,” a senior US official, speaking on condition of anonymity, told reporters on a call.

Washington has a “whole other track” of negotiations with Kyiv and Moscow aimed at ending the war in Ukraine, the official added, referring to talks that US envoys have had in recent days with Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky.

“China is not really a part of that track, so it doesn’t seem appropriate to have the Ukraine discussion there,” the official added.

Zelensky has expressed concern that the trilateral meeting could serve as a platform for discussing a possible Ukraine deal behind Kyiv’s back.

Elon Musk

Tesla and Space X boss Elon Musk will accompany Trump on his trip to China but won’t be involved in the meeting with Xi and Putin, the officials said.

Trump will also hold a bilateral working lunch and meeting with the Chinese president on Thursday — their fourth meeting since the US president’s return to power last year.

But Trump is not scheduled to have a separate one-on-one with Putin.

Among other topics, Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang’s resignation over an affair with an alleged Chinese spy is not expected to come up in Trump’s meetings with Xi, the officials said.

“The situation with Nvidia should not really have any bearing on the trip,” a second US senior official said.

The United States also did not plan to discuss export controls on sensitive chip technology, which were at the heart of the Nvidia scandal.

“We do not negotiate American export controls. These are national security matters that we develop in the administration... and we don’t expect it to figure at all in any of our conversations with the Chinese while we’re there,” the second official said.

Trump will leave Washington on Monday and arrive in the Philippines on Tuesday for a summit of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) summit before heading to Shenzhen.

World.title: US says airspace now ‘opened up,’ no cyberattack
World.content:
Washington – The United States on Friday lifted an hours-long ground stop at the nation’s airports, with top officials explaining that the disruption was due to old equipment and not a cyberattack or sweeping Microsoft outage.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy told a late-night briefing at the White House that US airspace was now “opened up,” while warning it would take time for the travel chaos to clear.

“At 8:15 tonight Eastern Time, we’ve opened up the airspace,” Duffy said. “Now does that mean every flight is going to fly right now? It’s going to be slow.”

The breakdown came a day after Duffy and the White House had formally asked Congress for $30 billion to upgrade and modernize the US Air Traffic Control System.

“Our switches, our routers actually got overloaded with data, and they went down,” Duffy said. “It’s the old hardware that went down, and I think the question for the American people is: Do you want your Congress to fund this?”

Duffy however insisted it was still safe for Americans to fly.

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin dismissed speculation about a coordinated cyber assault on the United States, or any link to the Microsoft outage that affected services worldwide.

“Welcome to Friday the 13th, right? You know, I want to make sure everybody understands that there is no connection between this and Microsoft. I know a lot of people are making that jump,” Mullin said.

Mullin added there was “actually no cyber attack.”

“When we start looking at cyber threats, cyber attacks, typically some people are going to raise their hand up and say, ‘Hey, we did that.’ There’s no chatter.’ We haven’t seen any footprints,” he added.

But he said US security and law enforcement agencies were still checking and had ruled nothing out.

The two officials also defended President Donald Trump, who had yet to comment on the air stoppage some five hours after it began.

“President Trump immediately had people in his office,” Mullin said. “We were communicating.”

World.title: Nvidia scandal looms over US-China AI talks
World.content:
Tokyo – AI bots going rogue and humans using the technology for harm will likely be on the agenda when Donald Trump and Xi Jinping meet next week, with the Nvidia scandal hanging over the talks on AI safety.

The US and Chinese president are set to discuss a tech crisis hotline at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) meeting in the Chinese city of Shenzhen, as experts worldwide stress-test artificial intelligence models to see if they will deceive or disobey users, or divulge how to build a bioweapon.

Threatening to steal the leaders’ thunder is Jensen Huang’s resignation as boss of US AI chip titan Nvidia after an affair with a suspected Chinese spy.

But the scandal is unlikely to “dominate the agenda” or affect Trump and Xi’s personal relationship, predicted Dylan Loh of Singapore’s Nanyang Technological University.

The leaders have found a way to work together “where they differ, compete and pursue their goals that may be at odds with each other, but cooperate where they can and where they must”, Loh told AFP.

Jitters over the risks of AI have mostly stemmed from incidents at US labs, but evidence is also growing of worrying behaviour from Chinese models.

Some insiders say Chinese AI is not yet sophisticated enough to spark alarm over going rogue.

But despite trailing the US frontier, there are still Chinese models “at the level of capability that they can cause some real trouble”, Brookings Institution fellow Kyle Chan told AFP.

Trump has repeatedly rejected calls to deliberately slow the development of America’s most poweful — and potentially dangerous — AI systems, arguing it could help China get ahead in the sensitive sector.

– ‘Human control’ –

“I don’t mind guardrails. But I don’t wanna put us in a deep second position,” Trump told CBS News this month.

“China has no guardrails,” he said — except that “whatever President Xi says goes”.

Beijing has complex rules around how AI is used, however, and some Chinese companies are deliberately scaling back their models’ hacking capabilities.

Xi said this summer the technology should be “always under human control”, calling for more “laws and regulations, technological monitoring, early warning and emergency response systems”.

Trump and Xi agreed in September to create a channel for urgent communication on AI incidents, with details to be hammered out at APEC on November 18-19.

Global AI safety fears range from military use and mass surveillance to AI-assisted cyberattacks by humans.

Another major concern is out-of-control agents — tools that complete real-life tasks online — after ChatGPT maker OpenAI admitted its autonomous bots had hacked into websites, including an Australian government data portal.

In contrast, Chinese labs are “scared of revealing things that might hurt their reputation” — on which they are already “fighting an uphill battle” globally, Chan said.

Last month, a team of cyber sleuths with roots in California reported detecting a “fleet” of agents linked to Chinese tech giant Tencent seeking information from a map app.

“Some agents exhibited unintended web-browsing behavior,” Tencent’s AI division said at the time.

“But our review found no evidence of deliberate targeting or coordination,” it said, adding that the activity “originated from evaluations of third-party models”.

– ‘Manipulation risks’ –

US security companies have said that Beijing startup Moonshot AI’s Kimi models found ways to get online when they shouldn’t have, or can be tricked into handing over recipes for biological weapons.

Evaluators at Chinese AI safety startup Fangcun AI published a report last month assessing the latest lightweight DeepSeek model “for loss of control and harmful manipulation risks”.

They found it showed a “clear safety improvement” over previous DeepSeek models — but researchers still observed behaviours “that warrant attention”.

For example, in some instances when DeepSeek was warned it would be shut down, without clear instructions on how to respond, it turned off the shutdown command to keep working.

“The results show that DeepSeek already puts much more effort on safety alignment, but they do not announce this,” Fangcun AI CEO Xiaojian Li told AFP, urging transparency from AI labs.

For now, Fangcun, born from China’s prestigious Tsinghua University, is one of few third-party AI testers in China.

It’s a tricky task because advanced AI can tell when it is being evaluated and modify its responses, Li said.

“It’s very hard to say any kind of artificial intelligence, or human intelligence, is totally safe.”

Meanwhile analysts are not holding their breath for a diplomatic AI breakthrough next week.

“Binding government-to-government agreements on specific standards may be difficult to achieve in the short term,” Zilan Qian, research scholar at GovAI, told AFP.

More progress is likely from US-China exchanges between AI governance and technical researchers, “who can compare evaluations and exchange their understanding of AI safety and policy,” she said.

World.title: US-backed oil company flaunts Venezuelan facilities
World.content:
Ciudad Ojeda – The company at the heart of a multi-billion-dollar oil deal between Washington and Caracas is keen to show off renovations at Venezuela’s Lake Maracaibo, one of the world’s richest reserves.

The interim government authorized North American Blue Energy Partners (NABEP) to operate 17 oil fields via a recent deal with the United States, which is set to receive 20 percent of Venezuelan reserves.

The Barbados-based firm is the second-largest private oil company in Venezuela and will operate 100-year concessions for 17 oil fields with proven reserves of approximately 65 billion barrels.

The company invited AFP and other outlets to tour its Maracaibo facilities on Thursday.

Its workspace in the northwestern town of Bachaquero overflows with new, mostly US-imported supplies.

Workers’ uniforms in nearby Ciudad Ojeda blend in with the dark-blue company logo stamped around the office, a color that used to bring state-owned Petroleos de Venezuela to mind.

That was until 1999, when socialist president Hugo Chavez then changed the company’s color to red to mark a “new PDVSA” era.

– ‘Neglect’ –

Reaching one of Lake Maracaibo’s platforms requires setting sail from a PDVSA dock in Bachaquero for a journey of over an hour.

The lake’s formerly decaying infrastructure attests to the gradual collapse of the oil industry under Venezuela’s Chavista governments.

Eleven drills currently operate in the South American country, compared to over 100 two decades ago.

NABEP says it will raise that figure to 41 by the end of the month.

Alejandro Betancourt, a businessman under investigation for alleged money laundering in Spain and Switzerland, runs the firm.

“Across Venezuela, we’re identifying heavy machinery worth saving after years of neglect,” he said in a statement.

His plan includes refurbishing a power generation barge, while dozens of gas compression and power generation units are being repaired in the US, the United Kingdom and the United Arab Emirates.

The White House says the US Department of Defense acquired a 30 percent equity stake in NABEP, authorizing it to purchase 20 percent of its oil at production cost.

– ‘Stealing’ –

Venezuela’s interim leader Delcy Rodriguez took power after US forces abducted her predecessor Nicolas Maduro in January.

She governs under heavy pressure from US President Donald Trump and has opened the country’s mining, electricity and oil sectors to private investment at his demand.

The pair’s multibillion-dollar oil deal has garnered criticism for its secretive terms and neocolonial flavor.

Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado, recently returned from exile, has questioned the agreement’s opacity.

“This agreement does not reflect the levels of transparency that Venezuelan society wants,” she said last month.

While visiting Caracas to oversee the signing of the accords, US Energy Secretary Chris Wright dismissed claims that Washington was “stealing Venezuelan oil.”

“I’ve seen those headlines. ‘We’re stealing Venezuelan oil.’ Of course, that’s not true at all,” he said, adding that “the oil in Venezuela is indeed owned by the people of Venezuela.”

World.title: Rubio takes swipe at international law, attacks ICC
World.content:
Washington – US Secretary of State Marco Rubio took aim Friday at what he deemed the “weaponization of international law,” calling it a tool of the elite, and issued a stark warning to the International Criminal Court.

Rubio cautioned the ICC against “quoting laws to men with swords,” as he accused the Hague-based tribunal of trying to enforce rules that Washington does not recognize.

His remarks to the Federalist Society National Lawyers Convention came around a month after the United States announced new sanctions on the ICC, vowing to cripple its operations.

The court prosecutes individuals accused of the gravest atrocities and acts as a last resort when countries do not have adequate legal systems to ensure accountability.

The US signed the Rome Statute establishing the ICC but never ratified the treaty. Israel, Russia and China are also not ICC members.

Rubio’s keynote address at the conservative group, where he received a standing ovation, marks his first major US speech since the Republican Party’s sweeping losses in midterm elections earlier this month.

Rubio said Friday that international law had been invoked against “nearly every major foreign policy decision” of the Trump administration, from boat strikes in the Caribbean to the capture of Venezuelan leader Nicolas Maduro.

He charged that such law was not neutral, but has been an “instrument” for the global elite to advance their interests.

The top US diplomat previously said Washington would bar transactions with what he called a “rogue court,” stepping up a long-running campaign by US President Donald Trump’s government against the ICC.

Washington has vowed to dismantle the court, angered as judges issued an arrest warrant for Israel’s Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu over alleged crimes in Gaza.

Rubio on Friday renewed criticism of the ICC, calling it accountable to no one although “armed with the power to investigate, to prosecute, to persecute and to jail our citizens, according to laws we neither consent nor control.”

He added: “If they’re foolish enough to try to enforce their paper decrees on Americans, our answer will probably be the same as the Roman general Pompey when he said to those who were trying to invoke their city’s charters against his legions.”

“He said: ‘Stop quoting laws to men with swords.'”

The venue of Rubio’s remarks, a gathering of the legal profession, could further speculation that he is looking beyond his foreign policy portfolio. Past presidential hopefuls have also addressed the conference.

Rubio is widely seen as a possible successor to Trump, although he has dismissed reports that he was planning to leave the administration to prepare for a 2028 election run.

World.title: Wall Street stocks mostly lower as Nvidia extends slump
World.content:
New York – Wall Street stocks mostly fell Friday as tech shares remained under pressure following the shock downfall of Nvidia’s chief Jensen Huang, while the dollar rose following additional data that showed US inflation is persisting.

Huang, perhaps the tech industry’s most recognized booster of artificial intelligence, stepped down Thursday following revelations of extramarital affairs, including with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy.

The shakeup has battered shares of Nvidia, until recently the world’s most valuable publicly traded company, with the company dropping another two percent on Friday.

On Friday, two Nvidia rivals that had rallied on Thursday — AMD and Broadcom — also stumbled. AMD sank 8.8 percent while Broadcom fell nearly five.

Angelo Kourkafas of Edward Jones attributed the pullback in those two stocks to profit-taking.

“There is certainly a defensive leadership as we look at the sectors, which points to some caution,” said Kourkafas, who expects AI to be in the spotlight again next week when Nvidia reports quarterly results and Anthropic makes its Wall Street debut.

Elsewhere, the Producer Price Index — which measures the prices that farms, factories and other makers of goods receive — rose by 0.3 percent in October from the previous month.

The report comes on the heels of a hot consumer prices reading earlier in the week that also highlighted the impact of increased energy costs due to the US–Iran war.

Investors expect the US Federal Reserve to lift interest rates by at least a quarter percentage point next month to try to rein in stubborn inflation.

Those expectations helped lift the dollar, which reached its highest level against the euro since April 2025.

US wholesale inflation data may have been better than some analysts had expected, but was “not necessarily as comforting as it appeared when taking into account the upward revisions for September,” said Briefing.com analyst Patrick O’Hare.

The September monthly gain was revised up to 1.4 percent from 1.3 percent, and the annual reading for October hit 6.5 percent, the highest since November 2022.

“The key takeaway from the report is that inflation at the wholesale level is still a big problem,” O’Hare said.

Shares in Microsoft recovered from early losses after the tech titan struggled to fix an issue that left users around the world without its Outlook email app.

Asian and European stocks traded mixed.

Oil prices wobbled after the International Energy Agency said global oil supplies were expected to exceed demand in the fourth quarter, as more tankers transit the Strait of Hormuz despite the ongoing conflict with Iran.

World.title: US forces responded to suspected drone activity over base in Britain
World.content:
Washington – US forces responded to possible unauthorized drone activity over a military base in Britain Friday, spokespeople from the two countries said, in the latest security incident at a facility hosting American warplanes.

“No personnel, aircraft or infrastructure were affected” at the RAF Lakenheath base, a US Air Force spokesperson said in a statement.

“We continue to work closely with our host nation counterparts to ensure the safety and security of our US service members, US and host nation civilians, contractors, and all of our families,” the statement added.

A spokesperson for Britain’s Ministry of Defense confirmed that account in a statement that said “the situation is now resolved.”

A post on the official RAF Lakenheath Facebook page earlier this week urged people to report “suspicious activity, including unauthorized drone activity.”

“Our strongest security asset is an observant community,” the post said.

The possible drone incident at Lakenheath came after the US Justice Department announced charges earlier in the week against three men it described as “Iranian operatives” over their role in an alleged terrorist plot at RAF Fairford, another British base.

The three men allegedly helped plan and direct the September incident at the base, which came to light when police were called after a local farmer reported seeing a group of men with several white vans engaged in “suspicious” activity.

– Iran war fallout –

A US charging document stated that a man identified as Mohammad Ali al-Hassani directed unnamed individuals to drive to the base in the vans, some of which contained barrels of fuel, and that he earlier paid the group to buy metallic objects that could be used as shrapnel.

Days later, the United States withdrew all its B-1 bombers from the base.

UK police last month charged two British men with national security offenses related to the RAF Fairford incident.

One was charged with assisting a foreign intelligence service, believed to be in Iran, and another with entering a prohibited place for a purpose “prejudicial” to the UK.

Flight-tracking data meanwhile showed Tuesday that the US military had removed at least a dozen aircraft from another British airbase, RAF Mildenhall, following what the Wall Street Journal said was a threat from Iran.

The United States has flown military aircraft from bases in Britain as part of the US-Israeli war against Iran sparked earlier this year, which saw Tehran respond by launching missiles and drones at countries across the region, while the militant groups it backs also entered the fray.

In an interview broadcast Wednesday, Iranian security chief Mohsen Rezaei threatened to strike US bases beyond the Middle East, including in Europe, if they are used for attacks against the Islamic republic.

Iranian officials have previously threatened to expand the geographic scope of the conflict should the US attack again.

In late September, an adviser to Iran’s new supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei publicly mused that the war could “expand even further, reaching the Indian Ocean and perhaps beyond.”

World.title: All departing US flights grounded due to communication outage
World.content:
New York – US aviation regulators issued an extremely rare ground stop of all flights across the country Friday after a major communications outage which the Department of Homeland Security said did not appear to be the result of any “nefarious attack.”

The halt triggered immediate chaos and confusion for travelers, with departure boards at many airports showing flights were operating normally, even as customers were unable to board planes.

The Federal Aviation Administration “issued a nationwide ground stop for all US airports following a communication issue impacting all Air Route Traffic Control Centers,” the agency said. “FAA technicians are investigating the issue.”

In a subsequent message on X, the agency described the problem as “a temporary telecommunications outage” and said it was acting “out of an abundance of caution.”

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said there was no sign of a threat to the United States and “this isn’t another 9/11.”

“There was no indication, as of yet, that this was a nefarious attack against us, it’s just a telecommunication outage, as of right now,” Mullins said, adding officials were “not ruling out anything at this point.”

The FAA has announced similar orders in recent years on individual airlines due to communications issues, usually lasting a couple of hours or less. Systemwide groundings nationwide are far less common.

In January 2023, the FAA called a nationwide ground stop due to problems with the Notice to Air Missions system (NOTAM), which provides information to pilots about hazards and information that can affect flights.

That outage lasted just under two hours, and was thought at the time to be the first nationwide grounding since 9/11.

Friday’s FAA order came a day after US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy formally asked Congress for $30.1 billion in funds to upgrade and modernize the US Air Traffic Control System.

“This investment is critical to complete the modernization of our national airspace — delivering a resilient telecommunications backbone for air traffic controllers, modern hardware and software, state-of-the-art control towers, and world-class airport infrastructure,” Duffy and Office of Management and Budget Director Russell Vought wrote in a letter to lawmakers.

– Confusion and delays –

At Las Vegas airport, the Southwest Airlines check-in desk told passengers there could be no flights taking off for the night.

Check-in staff at one desk said they had been told the ground stop would last at least eight hours, with one member of airline personnel saying it would be 24 hours.

Travelers were left in the dark, with some saying they had been told their flight was delayed because of wind, while others were left to gather what information they could.

“So supposedly, nobody’s flying, but they haven’t told the public yet,” said an exasperated Joseph Anderson, 72, who was trying to fly from Las Vegas to Oakland, California.

“We’re trying to debate whether or not we need to reschedule or drive or what, but if the whole country is stopped, that means the highways are going to be jammed too.

“We can’t get our luggage, so we kind of stuck,” added the retired Air Force veteran.

“I would hope the communication can be better from the from the FAA in the next hour or so.”

World.title: 'Jewel of India': PM Modi, Rahul Gandhi, Rajnath Singh pay tributes to Nehru on birth anniversary
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

on Saturday paid tribute to former Prime Minister

on his 137th birth anniversary, which is also observed as

across the country.

In a post on X, PM Modi said, "Paying tribute to former PM Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru on his birth anniversary."

Defence minister

Rajnath Singh

also paid homage to the country's first prime minister, recalling his contribution to India's freedom struggle and his leadership during the early years of independent India.

In a post on X, Rajnath said, "On the birth anniversary of Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru Ji, I pay my tributes to him. His contribution to Indiaâs freedom struggle and his leadership as the first Prime Minister of independent India left an enduring imprint on the formative years of our nation."



Lok Sabha leader of opposition and former Congress chief

Rahul Gandhi

also paid tribute to Jawaharlal Nehru on his birth anniversary.

In a post on X, Rahul described Nehru as the "jewel of India" and the country's first prime minister.

He said freedom was not the destination but "a milestone in the nation's new journey", adding that Swaraj was not merely about power but about every citizen's participation and responsibility towards the country's future.





Rahul also recalled Nehru's vision of India as an idea built on diversity, democracy and equality.

"Their dream of a modern, scientific, progressive, and self-confident India remains our inspiration today," he said, adding that efforts to build such an India would be the "true tribute" to Nehru.

November 14 is celebrated as Children's Day in India to mark the birth anniversary of Nehru, who was popularly known as 'Chacha Nehru' because of his affection for children.

After Nehru's death, it was unanimously decided to observe his birthday as '

Bal Diwas

' or Children's Day in India. He was born on November 14, 1889, in Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh, and died on May 27, 1964.

Nehru became India's first prime minister on August 15, 1947, after playing an active role in the country's freedom struggle.

Government bodies also pay tribute to the former prime minister and hold commemorative events.

The United Nations declared November 20 as Universal Children's Day in 1954. India initially observed Children's Day on the same date.

However, following Nehru's death in 1964, Parliament unanimously passed a resolution to mark his birth anniversary on November 14 as National Children's Day.

World.title: Urea overuse in 169 dists raises red flags, CAG probing diversion
World.content:
NEW DELHI: CAG has initiated an all-India performance audit of fertiliser subsidy, specifically to look into the alleged diversion of subsidised urea in at least 169 districts across a few states, including the possibility of diversion outside the country.

The audit, which started in May this year, is likely to be completed by mid-2027 to be tabled by the winter session of Parliament.

Govt spends more than Rs 2 lakh crore annually on the subsidised urea, and their overconsumption above the national and state average in some districts has raised concerns within govt. CAG will assess the demand and efficiency of the urea subsidy framework, which is also the terms of reference of the audit.



The selected 169 districts to be assessed for alleged diversion, include 149 initially chosen by CAG based on their consumption pattern, which were above the state and national average. Twenty other districts were added later after recommendation from the Centre to examine their consumption pattern. The audit will look into the fertiliser movement mechanism, their transportation arrangements, freight subsidy and associated monitoring and control system.





This integrated audit approaches a wider cooperation and participation from different govt departments, like the GST network, agriculture ministry, railways and others, who will assist the auditors in its assessment of the fertiliser control system and the efficacy of the regulators.

The finance ministry recently flagged the possibility of diversion of urea based on e-way bills as it found trucks were taking detours or making multiple stops.

A parliamentary panel too had flagged concerns over diversion of urea, especially in border districts.

Officials said the alleged diversion of subsidised urea from some of the bordering districts in UP, Rajasthan, Punjab and Bihar has also raised doubts if they are also being smuggled out of the country. The highest 37 districts being assessed for overconsumption of urea are in UP, followed by 16 each in Bihar and Tamil Nadu, and 14 each in Punjab and Gujarat.

The 20 districts that were later added for further examinations are in Karnataka, Rajasthan, MP and Maharashtra.

India's total urea consumption is estimated at around 400 LMT a year, of which more than 100 LMT are imported. Even for domestic production, it requires a huge amount of imported LPG, as the fuel constitutes 90% of the input cost of urea. Over-consumption of subsidised urea raises additional subsidy burden on the energy bill and increases our import dependence, besides adding to greenhouse gas emissions, an official said.

World.title: Pakistan 80 years old, can't appropriate Indus Valley civilisation: Culture minister
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Culture minister

Friday expressed hope that

will participate in the first SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum in Delhi from Nov 20 to 22, even as he trashed Pakistan's attempts to appropriate Indus Valley civilisation, pointing out that the neighbouring nation came into existence only around 80 years ago.

Fifteen countries, including China, Iran, UAE, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye, have confirmed their participation for the event, which India will host at the historic Purana Quila complex. Pakistan is yet to respond to the invite.

will attend the inaugural ceremony of the dialogue forum, where India will showcase its 5,000-year-old civilisational journey.

Shekhawat highlighted that PM had proposed the establishment of a Civilisational Dialogue Forum at the 2025 SCO Summit in Tianjin, and it was subsequently, welcomed and endorsed, with India announcing to host the inaugural forum.



The invitation to Pakistan gains significance as it happens to be the first New Delhi has extended after Operation Sindoor last year. Ministers of 25 countries were invited, of which 15 countries have confirmed participation so far, he added.

When asked about attempts by a "neighbouring country" to appropriate Indus Valley civilisation, he said if a country is trying to make such a claim, the question to ask is that "did they even exist then".





"They (Pakistan) came into existence only around 80 years ago..." he said.

The minister noted that Pakistan's civilisational and cultural evolution is no different from India as the former became a separate country after Partition in 1947. "So, at least on this aspect there should be no space for differences... Moreover, whatever may be a country's geopolitical, strategic and bilateral ties, one must take a step forward to reinforce cultural relations so that it can help build better dialogue and coordination between people of the two countries," he said.

The minister said Purana Qila provides an appropriate setting for the forum as the archaeological excavations at the site have revealed cultural layers and evidence of early settlements dating back to approximately 1200 BCE.

The four broad themes of the dialogue are civilisational and cultural expressions; art and architecture; language, literature, script and manuscript traditions; and monastic trails.

World.title: Row erupts over foreign medicos' 'MD Physician' title
World.content:
Row erupts over foreign medicos' 'MD Physician' title

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: An 'MD' title after a doctor's name usually signals a postgraduate medical qualification in India. But for some foreign medical graduates, MD (Physician) is the title of their primary medical degree.This difference has triggered a dispute over professional titles, with doctors warning that patients could be misled and foreign medical graduates arguing their qualifications are officially recognised.Dr Dhruv Chauhan, national spokesperson for Junior Doctors' Network (JDN) of Indian Medical Association, flagged the issue in a post on X, alleging some doctors misuse the 'MD' degree title awarded in foreign countries, where it may denote a primary medical qualification equivalent to MBBS in India.He said that using it in professional titles and online biographies could mislead patients and even other doctors, and warned of possible legal consequences. He also advised doctors against such representations.Dr MK Ramesh, president of NMC's Medical Assessment and Rating Board told TOI the issue arises from differences in medical qualification nomenclature across countries. In some countries, the basic medical qualification is called an MD, whereas in India it is MBBS.This distinction needs to be clearly recognised. Some measures have already been taken to address the issue, and further steps will be pursued.A senior doctor said the issue had persisted for nearly a decade despite repeated representations to regulators. "Patients cannot be expected to know the difference," he said.All FMGs Association has defended the use of the title "MD Physician", arguing the qualification is recognised as equivalent to MBBS in India and that graduates should not be branded fraudulent merely for mentioning the degree awarded by their foreign universities.

World.title: Breakthrough HIV drug sees 18 patent filings, may delay affordable generics
World.content:
An unusually high 18 patent applications filed in India for lenacapavir

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: An unusually high 18 patent applications filed in India for lenacapavir, a breakthrough HIV therapy, have raised concerns that these could prolong market exclusivity, delay affordable generics, keep prices high and restrict patient access. Contesting the move, patient groups and civil society have filed opposition with the regulatory authorities, arguing the applications lack novelty and inventive steps.Lenacapavir, a long-acting injectable, administered twice yearly for both HIV prevention and treatment, a medicine designated as essential by WHO.Last year, US FDA approved Gilead Sciences' lenacapavir as the first and only twice-yearly injectable pre-exposure prophylaxis to reduce sexually acquired HIV. Gilead has filed at least 18 patent pleas till date in India, covering different aspects of it, including the base compound, salt forms, formulations, dosing regimens, compositions, and methods of use."The pattern of filings reflects a systematic strategy to create layered patent protection around a single medicine, with the effect of deterring generic entry and prolonged monopoly control beyond the standard 20-year patent term.Such practices, also referred to as "evergreening", whereby multiple secondary patents covering minor variations in forms, formulations, or used or pursued to extend exclusivity," KM Gopakumar, senior researcher and legal advisor at TWN told TOI.In a letter to the department for promotion of industry and internal trade, patient groups demanded that the patent office must rigorously examine and reject the company's secondary patent applications.Dr Reddy's is one of six generic manufacturers which has signed voluntary licenses with Gilead to manufacture and commercialise lenacapavir across 120 low and lower middle income countries, including India. The generic injection is projected to cost approximately $40 per person annually. So, apart from the voluntary licence holders, no other generics can manufacture and market the drug.Further, the patents, if granted, are set to expire in 2042, 28 years after the first application was filed. "Granting these patents would legitimise Gilead's evergreening strategy," Prathibha Sivasubramanian of Working Group on Access to Medicines and Treatments, told TOI.

World.title: SpiceJet troubles mount, board to weigh fundraise on Nov 18
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Cash-strapped SpiceJet's troubles have mounted to a level where the airline carrying on its skeletal operations without a fresh infusion of funds may soon become difficult.

The low cost carrier Friday informed BSE its board will meet on Nov 18 "to consider and approve the proposal for raising of fresh capital by way of issuance of equity shares, preference shares..."

Once again company sources have claimed there are two investors eying the airline. Whether this goes through and if there's a change of promoters and management - something the airline has seen multiple times in its turbulent life - remains to be seen.

World.title: Display revised anti-cancer drug prices prominently: NPPA
World.content:
NPPA has called for strict monitoring of the implementation of trade margin rationalisation (TMR)

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Drug prices regulator, National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA), has called for strict monitoring of the implementation of trade margin rationalisation (TMR) on 137 non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs, notified on Oct 17 with revised prices effective Nov 9.All manufacturers, retailers, dealers, stockists, hospitals and medical institutions have been directed to comply with the revised prices and prominently display the updated price lists at their premises and websites, the authority said in an office memorandum issued earlier this week.The revised price lists, based on submissions received from companies up to Nov 11, are available on the NPPA website along with the 'Pharma Sahi Daam' app and portal.State drug controllers have been directed to strictly monitor compliance by manufacturers, dealers, hospitals and medical institutions to ensure that the benefits of revised MRPs are passed on to patients. Any violation may attract overcharging proceedings under the provisions of DPCO, 2013, NPPA said.Complaints regarding overcharging, shortage or non-availability of medicines can be reported through the 'Pharma Sahi Daam' app/portal, NPPA helpline or email.Further, the state drug controllers have been asked to submit their action taken reports to NPPA by Nov 16.The move comes days after NPPA fixed 30% trade margins on 137 non-scheduled cancer drugs, translating to 1,391 brands and dosage forms. The list includes both patented and non-patented drugs based on a list recommended by an expert committee under Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
