World.title: Special forces officers convicted of assaulting protesters jailed for five years each
World.content:
Special forces officers jailed for assaults

A court has sentenced special forces officers convicted of physically assaulting journalist Guram Rogava and protester Zviad Maisashvili during demonstrations in November and December 2024 to five years in prison each.

The special forces officer convicted of assaulting Guram Rogava, a journalist with Formula TV, was also banned from professional duties for three years. Lasha Gamkrelidze, the new prosecutor in the case, informed the journalist of the verdict by telephone.

According to Formula, Rogava had expected to testify as a victim during the trial. However, the prosecutor explained that his testimony was unnecessary because the court and the defence had accepted the charges as undisputed. Rogava himself believes that the person who directly assaulted him remains at large.

Two other special forces officers arrested in connection with the assault on Zviad Maisashvili were each sentenced to five years in prison. Lawyer Dimitri Mchedlishvili confirmed the information to Tabula.

On 30 November 2024, at around 06:30, special forces officers kicked Zviad Maisashvili in the face during a protest on Rustaveli Avenue, causing him to lose consciousness. Footage of the assault circulated on social media.

On 7 May 2026, Georgia’s Prosecutor’s Office announced that it had identified and detained five people in connection with assaults on Rogava, Maisashvili and opposition politician Levan Khabeishvili.

According to the Prosecutor’s Office, four of those detained were current or former special forces officers, while the fifth was a serving officer with the Interior Ministry’s Security Police Department. Two of the suspects were already serving prison sentences at the time of their arrest.

Prosecutors said that on 29 November 2024, during a protest on Rustaveli Avenue, an officer from the Interior Ministry’s Special Tasks Department assaulted Guram Rogava while the journalist was carrying out his professional duties.

The detainees were charged under Article 333(3) of the Criminal Code with abuse of official powers involving violence. The officer detained in connection with the assault on Rogava also faced an additional charge of unlawfully obstructing a journalist’s professional activities.

According to the Prosecutor’s Office’s initial statement, the charges carried prison sentences of five to eight years.

Maisashvili said both special forces officers detained over the assault on him had admitted their guilt and apologised to him.

Guram Rogava and Zviad Maisashvili

Background

The assaults on Guram Rogava and Zviad Maisashvili were among several high-profile incidents of police violence during pro-European protests in Tbilisi in November and December 2024.

The protests began on 28 November 2024, after Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze announced that the government would take the issue of opening EU accession talks off the agenda until the end of 2028.

In the following days, law enforcement officers used water cannon, tear gas and other crowd-control measures against protesters on Rustaveli Avenue and near the parliament building. Numerous incidents of physical violence against demonstrators, journalists and human rights defenders were documented.

Both protesters and members of the media sustained injuries during the demonstrations. The assault on journalist Guram Rogava attracted particular attention. On 29 November 2024, a special forces officer attacked Rogava while he was reporting live from Rustaveli Avenue, leaving him seriously injured.

Media representatives and human rights organisations called for investigations into these incidents. On 30 November 2024, the OSCE Office for Democratic Institutions and Human Rights (ODIHR) said the police’s use of water cannon, pepper spray and batons, including against peaceful demonstrators and journalists, had been disproportionate.

According to Georgia’s Public Defender’s 2024 report, the ombudsman and his representatives visited 624 people who had been detained or injured during protests between 15 April 2024 and 1 March 2025. Of those, 360 reported ill-treatment.

The report also noted that no police officers had been held accountable for violence committed by law enforcement personnel during that period.

According to the Prosecutor’s Office statement of 7 May 2026, more than 550 witnesses were questioned and thousands of investigative and procedural actions were carried out as part of the investigations into the cases involving Zviad Maisashvili, Levan Khabeishvili and Guram Rogava.

The Prosecutor’s Office said the investigations would continue to identify other possible perpetrators and bring them to justice.

World.title: Strategic partnership signed in Dublin: What does London want from Baku, and what does Baku gain?
World.content:
Azerbaijan-UK partnership

Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev and UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham signed a joint declaration on strategic partnership on 12 November at the European Political Community summit in Dublin. The British government published the text of the document on the same day.

The declaration covers three main areas: defence and security; trade, investment and economic growth; and education and innovation. The two countries agreed to hold annual strategic partnership meetings to assess progress in these areas.

The document builds on a 1994 friendship and cooperation agreement and a 1998 declaration on friendly relations and partnership between the two countries.

Six months earlier, the UK signed a similar declaration with Armenia. A comparison of the two documents raises the question:

What does the UK prioritise in its strategic partnership with Azerbaijan, and which issues does it leave unaddressed?

What does the document entail?

Defence and security. The two countries intend to expand defence cooperation in training, capacity building and interoperability, as well as explore opportunities for cooperation in the defence industry. The document also provides for cooperation between law enforcement agencies, collaboration on border control and judicial and legal cooperation aimed at strengthening the rule of law and institutional resilience.

Trade and energy. The UK will support the development of the Middle Corridor, a transport route linking China to Europe via Central Asia, the Caspian Sea and the Caucasus. The two countries also intend to cooperate on renewable energy, green finance and low-carbon technologies. The main platform for cooperation in these areas will be the bilateral Intergovernmental Commission on Trade and Economic Cooperation.

Education and innovation. The document provides for cooperation in higher and vocational education, digital skills development, civil servant training, artificial intelligence and digital governance.

In the declaration, the UK welcomes steps towards normalising relations between Azerbaijan and Armenia and expresses support for efforts to achieve a “lasting peace”.

However, the implementation of all commitments is subject to the availability of resources and the domestic laws of each country.

How does the declaration signed with Armenia differ?

The declaration, signed on 5 May by then UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer and Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan, also identifies three main areas of cooperation. The first two are similar to those outlined in the declaration with Azerbaijan: defence and security, and economic growth and development.

However, the third area differs. In the declaration with Armenia, it is titled “Governance and Democratic Resilience”, while the document with Azerbaijan focuses on “Education and Innovation”.

In the declaration with Armenia, the two countries commit to protecting democracy, human rights and the rule of law. The document also provides for creating an enabling environment for independent media and civil society.

By contrast, the declaration with Azerbaijan makes no mention of democracy, human rights or the media. The term “civil society” appears only once, in the context of strengthening people-to-people ties between the two countries.

Furthermore, the declaration with Armenia provides for the development of a joint “Results Framework” to monitor the implementation of the agreements. No equivalent mechanism is included in the declaration with Azerbaijan, with the two countries agreeing only to hold annual meetings.

The declaration with Armenia also explicitly states that it does not constitute an international treaty and that either party may terminate cooperation by giving six months’ written notice.

What is the wider context behind these differences?

The declaration was signed amid continuing international criticism over the arrests of journalists in Azerbaijan. According to Amnesty International, 12 people detained in connection with the Meydan TV case are being persecuted for their journalistic work. The human rights organisation has also reported serious health problems among some of those detained.

In February this year, the detained journalists appealed to diplomatic missions in Baku, including the British embassy, asking them to monitor the court proceedings.

In response to calls for the journalists’ release, Azerbaijani officials have said that the legal proceedings are ongoing and that a fair decision will be reached.

The British government’s statement announcing the signing of the declaration makes no mention of the issue.

What do the two countries expect from each other?

The UK has long been one of the largest foreign investors in Azerbaijan, largely through BP, which operates the Azeri-Chirag-Gunashli and Shah Deniz oil and gas fields. According to Azerbaijani officials, British investment in the country’s economy has exceeded $39bn.

However, the two countries’ figures for bilateral trade differ. According to Azerbaijan’s State Customs Committee, trade turnover between the two countries reached $3.72bn in the first nine months of this year.

According to official UK government statistics, trade in goods and services totalled £1.2bn in the 12 months to June, making Azerbaijan the UK’s 89th-largest trading partner.

British exports to Azerbaijan amounted to £724m, down 2.9% from the previous year. Imports from Azerbaijan, meanwhile, increased more than 2.6-fold to £453m.

Preparations for the declaration began well before its signing. In August 2025, UK Minister for Europe Stephen Doughty announced during a visit to Baku that the two countries had agreed to upgrade bilateral relations to a strategic partnership.

In December, UK Minister of State for Defence Lord Coaker visited Baku. In October this year, UK Trade Minister Lord Anas Sarwar announced at a meeting of the Intergovernmental Commission in Baku that the text of the declaration had been agreed.

The two countries also signed a roadmap for developing transport and digital infrastructure. Sarwar outlined the areas the partnership would cover:

“Of course, it will include energy and port infrastructure, investment, education and other areas.”

The UK government’s statement on Doughty’s 2025 visit also mentioned the peace process, the Russia-Ukraine war, the Middle Corridor, energy, defence, cybersecurity and education.

Human rights and media freedom were not mentioned on that occasion either.

What meetings took place in Dublin?

The signing of the declaration was one of several events on Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev’s busy schedule in Dublin. On the same day, he met Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan and the prime ministers of Bulgaria, Greece and the Czech Republic. His meeting with the Bulgarian prime minister focused on a proposed electricity corridor between the two countries.

According to the Azerbaijani side, Aliyev and Pashinyan discussed the peace agenda under the joint declaration signed in Washington in August 2025, border delimitation, transport links and the Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity (TRIPP).

The two leaders also welcomed the transit of goods through Azerbaijan to Armenia and in the opposite direction.

The UK signed strategic partnership declarations with Armenia and Azerbaijan six months apart. Both documents provide for support for the peace process in the South Caucasus. However, the third area of cooperation differs: the declaration with Armenia focuses on democracy, while the one with Azerbaijan emphasises education.

Azerbaijani human rights activists and opposition figures have yet to comment on the signing of the declaration.

World.title: Azerbaijan advances UNESCO geopark project on Absheron Peninsula (PHOTO)
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, November 14. The Ministry of Ecology and Natural Resources held a meeting of the Working Group, comprising representatives of the ministry and relevant government agencies, to discuss a project to establish a Geological Park in Azerbaijan to preserve the country's geological heritage and develop geotourism, the ministry said.

Aynura Karimova, Deputy Chief of Staff at the Ministry of Ecology and Natural Resources, noted that the meeting reviewed the work completed on the conceptual aspects of the geopark project, discussed the progress made on developing the final version of the geopark concept, defining the territorial boundaries, conducting a survey of the territory, and preparing the nomination dossier in accordance with international requirements.

According to a ministry representative, creating the geopark will help preserve Azerbaijan’s unique geological heritage, promote the mud volcano group on the Absheron Peninsula, develop ecotourism, and pave the way for our country’s future membership in the UNESCO Global Geoparks Network.

The initiative to establish the Geopark is being implemented in accordance with the “Strategy for the Socio-Economic Development of the Republic of Azerbaijan for 2022–2026,” approved by a Decree of the President of the Republic of Azerbaijan dated July 22, 2022.

The new geopark is planned to be established in areas selected by international experts from among the mud volcanoes located in Baku and on the Absheron Peninsula.

World.title: 3.8-magnitude earthquake strikes Mediterranean off Türkiye
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, November 14. Magnitude 3.8 Earthquake Recorded in Mediterranean Sea

An earthquake with a magnitude of 3.8 has struck the Mediterranean Sea.

According to Türkiye’s Disaster and Emergency Management Authority (AFAD), the earthquake occurred at a depth of 10.76 kilometers.

The epicenter was located 300 kilometers off the coast of Türkiye’s Muğla Province.

World.title: Khuzestan's point-to-point inflation reaches 100.3% in seventh month
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, November 14. In the 7th month of the current Iranian year (September 23 through October 22, 2026), point-to-point inflation in Khuzestan Province, located in southwestern Iran, rose by 100.3% compared to the same month last year (September 23 through October 22, 2025).

According to Trend’s calculations, based on statistics from the Statistical Center of Iran, point-to-point inflation refers to the percentage change in the price index compared to the same period last year.

In the 7th month, the consumer price index in Khuzestan Province stood at 807.5.

In the 7th month, point-to-point inflation in Khuzestan Province rose by 116.2% in the food, beverages, and tobacco products category, and by 86.8% in the non-food goods and services sector.

During that month, monthly inflation in Khuzestan Province, compared to the 6th month (August 23 through September 22, 2026), stood at 4.7%.

Monthly inflation refers to the percentage change in the price index compared to the previous month.

In the 7th month, monthly inflation in Khuzestan rose by 2.4% for food, beverages, and tobacco products, and by 7.1% for non-food goods and services.

Based on the results of the 7th month, annual inflation for the period from October 23, 2025, through October 22, 2026, stood at 85.5% compared to the same period the previous year (October 22, 2024, through October 22, 2025).

Annual inflation is defined as the average percentage change in price index figures over the past year.

At the end of the seventh month, annual inflation in Khuzestan rose by 109.7% for food, beverages, and tobacco products, and by 66% for non-food goods and services.

In Iran, both the Central Bank and the Statistical Center publish statistics on the country’s inflation rate. Differences in inflation figures may be observed in the statistical data.

In the seventh month, point-to-point inflation in Iran rose by 88.7% compared to the same month last year.

For the record, Iran uses the Solar Hijri calendar, also known as the Persian calendar. The country is currently in the year 1405. The Iranian year begins on March 20 or 21. The first six months of the year each have 31 days, the following five months have 30 days, while the final month has 29 days in three out of every four years and 30 days in the fourth year. Consequently, the months of the Iranian calendar begin on the 21st, 22nd or 23rd day of the corresponding Gregorian calendar month.

World.title: A-Quatro plans two weekly China-Poland cargo flights via Uzbekistan (Exclusive)
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, November 14. Polish company A-Quatro is targeting an initial frequency of two cargo flights per week on a proposed China-Uzbekistan-Poland logistics route, with Tashkent expected to serve as a regional cargo consolidation and transfer hub, the company told Trend in an exclusive interview.

The initiative was discussed during a November 5 meeting in Tashkent between A-Quatro Director Adrian Aleksnin and representatives of Uzbekistan's Centrum Air. The parties explored potential cooperation on charter cargo flights from China to Poland via Uzbekistan, as well as multimodal transportation options.

A-Quatro said discussions with Centrum Air had been positive, although the project remains under development and no final commercial agreement has been concluded.

"Our initial operational target is two cargo flights per week," the company said, adding that this would amount to approximately eight flights per month.

A-Quatro is developing the logistics concept independently and is responsible for sourcing cargo in China, coordinating transportation through Uzbekistan and organizing operations in Poland. The company views Centrum Air as a potential strategic aviation partner.

The proposed operation would build on existing cargo access in China, while also consolidating shipments from other Chinese exporters and importers to establish a broader cargo base.

China departure points and cargo profile

Guangzhou, Chengdu and Shenzhen are all being considered as potential departure points. The final choice will depend on cargo availability, shipment volumes, supplier concentration, logistics costs and operational efficiency, the company said.

A-Quatro has not yet established final freight rates. Its pricing model will account for the entire logistics chain, including cargo transportation within China, consolidation in Uzbekistan, aircraft capacity, ground handling, customs procedures and final processing in Poland.

The company said the precise cargo volume per flight would depend on aircraft configuration, shipment composition and confirmed customer demand.

The target cargo portfolio includes consumer goods, electronics, textiles, clothing, e-commerce shipments and industrial products.

Tashkent as a regional logistics hub

Under the proposed model, Tashkent would serve as a central consolidation and transfer point, where shipments arriving from China could be processed and prepared for onward transportation to Poland.

Depending on the final operational arrangements, the logistics chain could include warehousing, cargo consolidation, customs clearance coordination and ground handling services.

"We see Uzbekistan as much more than a transit point. Its geographical position provides an opportunity to develop a logistics platform connecting Chinese suppliers with European markets," A-Quatro said.

The company is also considering a multimodal model combining road and air transportation from China to Uzbekistan. Road freight could be used to consolidate shipments from different Chinese production centers, while air cargo would serve time-sensitive deliveries to European markets.

"By combining these options, we can develop a flexible logistics model that balances transportation costs, delivery times and operational reliability," the company said.

A-Quatro added that the proposed initiative is part of a broader effort to develop international cargo operations at an airport in Poland, using existing infrastructure to attract additional cargo operators and international business.

The company aims to establish an integrated logistics chain connecting Chinese manufacturers and suppliers, Central Asian transport networks and European markets. The project would be developed progressively, with the possibility of increasing flight frequency and cargo capacity as demand grows.

World.title: Earthquake hits Türkiye
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, November 14. An earthquake with a magnitude of 3.9 has struck the Sea of Marmara in Türkiye.

According to the country’s Disaster and Emergency Management Authority (AFAD), the epicenter was located in the Gulf of Gemlik, off the coast of the Mudanya district in Bursa Province. The tremors were also felt in nearby areas.

The earthquake occurred 6.42 kilometers from Mudanya, at a depth of 13.65 kilometers.

World.title: Iran’s Qom attracts $59.2M in new industrial investment in seven months
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, November 14. Over the past 7 months of the current Iranian year (March 21 through October 22, 2026), a total of 113 trillion rials (approximately $59.2 million) has been invested in enterprises that have begun operations in Qom Province, located in central Iran.

According to the Qom Province Department of Industry, Mines, and Trade, this was announced by the department’s director general, Vahid Karimi.

"Over the past 7 months, licenses have been issued in Qom Province for the commissioning of 109 industrial facilities, and they have officially begun production," he noted.

Karimi stated that the commissioning of these enterprises has created jobs for 3,700 people in the Province.

Furthermore, Karimi emphasized that in recent years, Qom’s industrial potential has been the focus of attention.

"Currently, many investors are interested in engaging in manufacturing activities and have chosen Qom Province as a destination for their investments. In this regard, Qom Province is now considered one of the leading provinces for attracting investment in the industrial and manufacturing sectors," he added.

The official noted that private-sector investment in Qom’s industrial sector contributes to its development. With the full support of the provincial leadership, bank loans also contribute to the development of the industrial and manufacturing sectors, as well as the region’s economy.

According to Trend's calculation based on data from Iran’s Ministry of Industry, Mines, and Trade, 490 trillion rials (approximately $256 million) are earmarked for the establishment of manufacturing enterprises in Qom Province over six months (March 21 through September 22, 2026). These funds will be used to establish 252 enterprises and provide jobs for 6,500 people.

World.title: Kazakhstan's crude oil output falls 4.9% year over year in Q3 2026 - EIA
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, November 14. Kazakhstan's crude oil production averaged 1.74 million barrels per day in the third quarter of 2026, down 4.9% compared with the same period last year (1.83 million barrels per day), according to the November Short-Term Energy Outlook (STEO) report by the US Energy Information Administration (EIA).

Trend's calculations based on the report show that Kazakhstan's crude oil production declined by 5.9% compared with the second quarter of 2026, when output averaged 1.85 million barrels per day. In the first quarter, Kazakhstan's oil production averaged 1.39 million barrels per day.

For comparison, Kazakhstan's crude oil production averaged 1.73 million barrels per day in the first quarter of 2025, increasing to 1.78 million barrels per day in the second quarter and reaching a peak of 1.83 million barrels per day in the third quarter. Output then declined to 1.67 million barrels per day in the fourth quarter.

Overall, Kazakhstan's average crude oil production stood at 1.75 million barrels per day in 2025.

According to the EIA report, aggregate crude oil production by OPEC+ total countries (OPEC members subject to OPEC+ agreements plus Azerbaijan, Bahrain, Brunei, Kazakhstan, Malaysia, Mexico, Oman, Russia, South Sudan, and Sudan) averaged 33.33 million barrels per day in 2025. The figure is projected to decline to 30.08 million barrels per day in 2026 before increasing to 33.61 million barrels per day in 2027.

Crude oil production by OPEC members averaged 24.63 million barrels per day in 2025. The EIA expects this figure to decrease to 21.05 million barrels per day in 2026 and rise to 24.07 million barrels per day in 2027.

Global crude oil production stood at 79 million barrels per day in 2025. According to the EIA projections, worldwide output is expected to decrease to 76.1 million barrels per day in 2026 before rising to 80.87 million barrels per day in 2027.

World.title: ING sees Kazakhstan’s GDP growth accelerating to 4.8% in 2027
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, November 14. Kazakhstan's real gross domestic product (GDP) is projected to grow by 4.5% in 2026, accelerating to 4.8% in 2027 before moderating to 4.5% in 2028, according to the latest forecasts by ING Group.

Data from ING's report shows that quarterly GDP growth is expected to reach 4.4% year-on-year in the third quarter of 2026, rising to 5.5% in the fourth quarter of 2026 and the first quarter of 2027.

Growth is projected to gradually slow thereafter, reaching 5% in the second quarter of 2027, 4.5% in the third quarter, and 4% in the fourth quarter.

Meanwhile, preliminary data from Kazakhstan's Bureau of National Statistics shows that the country's real GDP grew by 4.5% in January-October 2026, up 0.3 percentage points from the growth recorded in January-September.

The non-resource sector was the main contributor to economic growth, expanding by an estimated 5.6%, while industrial output increased by 3.5%.

Manufacturing growth accelerated to 9.3% in January-October 2026, compared to 8.6% in the first nine months of the year.

Among manufacturing industries, the strongest growth was recorded in pharmaceuticals, which expanded by 50.9%. The production of fabricated metal products increased by 30.4%, machinery manufacturing by 22.2%, the chemical industry by 21.9%, rubber and plastic products by 18.1%, food production by 13%, and construction materials by 5.4%.

Other sectors also recorded growth, with construction expanding by 13.1%, transportation and warehousing by 7.5%, trade by 6.2%, agriculture by 5.2%, and information and communications by 4.9%.

According to the International Monetary Fund (IMF), Kazakhstan's GDP is expected to reach nearly $398 billion by the end of 2026. The Fund projects the country's economy to grow by 4.4% in 2026 and 4.9% in 2027.

World.title: Australia's newest fast-bowling sensation tipped for big things from a young age
World.content:
While Mahli Beardman's record-setting demolition of England may have stunned the visitors, those who watched his development as a junior say it's no surprise.

On a day when fresh hostilities in the Sandpaper scandal dominated the headlines, the West Australian fast bowler's 6/24 skittled the visitors and gave Australian cricket a much-needed bit of good news.

But for West Pilbara Cricket Association secretary Christy Reed, Beardman's talent was always obvious.

Beardman (right) receives a representative cap while playing junior cricket in WA's Pilbara. (Supplied: Christy Reed)

While hailing from Cowaramup in WA's South West, the 21-year-old played his initial junior and representative cricket for Dampier in WA's Pilbara.

Initially spotted by scouts at a talent clinic in Karratha in 2017 as a 12-year-old, Beardman progressed quickly through the junior representative ranks, eventually landing at WA Premier Cricket Club Melville when he moved to Perth.

Ms Reed said he made an impression early.

"He was a tiny little kid, but his bowling was absolutely natural talent," she said.

Beardman (left) was identified early as a talented young bowler. (Supplied: Andrew Hayes)

"So fast for his size, and he absolutely loved his cricket.

" He would even go down to the senior team, Dampier Taverners, training and bully them in the nets. "

She hoped Beardman's success would show other talented junior cricketers across the Pilbara what could be achieved.

"For years it was really hard for kids to have a pathway through to that upper level, but I imagine this would get more kids interested in the sport," Ms Reed said.

"I couldn't be happier for him, his family and for Cricket Australia."

WA Cricket country area manager Andrew Hayes was working in the Pilbara around the same time Beardman and fellow Dampier quick Josh Vernon were making their way through the system.

"To take six wickets against our old foe on debut is an incredible achievement, and we couldn't be prouder," he said.

Mahli Beardman (back row, second from right) representing the West Pilbara at Junior Country Week. (Supplied: Christy Reed)

Hometown pride

The pride was echoed in Cowaramup, who are keen to embrace Beardman as a favourite son despite competing claims from nearby Dunsborough and Margaret River.

Loading...

Cowaramup Cricket Club stalwart and secretary Bob Biddulph coached a six-year-old Beardman before his family moved north.

"Unfortunately, he was only there for one year … but it was the start of his cricket journey, so we're very proud of him," he said.

"We're claiming it down at Cowaramup that's for sure; I think everyone associated with the cricket club is very proud of that."

Mahli Beardman walks off Perth Stadium after taking 6/24 on debut for Australia in ODI cricket. (ABC News: Sam Tomlin)

Mr Biddulph echoed the importance of seeing regional cricketers performing well at international level.

"It just goes to show that it doesn't matter where you are; if you start off and you enjoy the game and stick at it and keep practising, the sky is the limit," he said.

"We've got quite a few junior teams this year, so for them to actually see one of their own making it on the big stage is quite exciting."

Game two of the three-match ODI series is at Adelaide Oval on Sunday.

World.title: Newcastle climate protest goes ahead, no arrests made
World.content:
Protest organisers and NSW Police say no arrests were made as hundreds of kayakers took to Newcastle Harbour in New South Wales, to protest against coal exports and fossil fuels.

Climate activism group Rising Tide began promoting its "Paddle for the Planet" event in August, but Newcastle Council this week moved to ban the group from holding any of its events on council land.

NSW Police attempted to block the protest, citing safety concerns and potential resourcing pressures.

However, the court dismissed the application on Friday, deciding the event was in the public interest.

The Supreme Court of NSW dismissed an application by NSW Police to stop the on-water protest. (ABC Newcastle: Bridget Murphy)

Speaking after the paddle-out, Rising Tide spokesperson Joe Hallenstein labelled Anthony Albanese "hypocritical", as the prime minister and climate change minister engage in the COP31 summit.

"[Albanese] is over in Türkiye telling the world that Australia is a leader in climate action, when the opposite is true," Mr Hallenstein said.

"Both Albanese's federal Labor government, and Chris Minns's state Labor government continue to approve new coal and gas projects, which is the opposite of action on climate change."

Rising Tide spokesperson Joe Hallenstein spoke out at the event. (ABC Newcastle: Bridget Murphy)

The event was held off Horseshoe Beach, which is managed by Transport for NSW.

A NSW Police spokesperson confirmed, by the completion of the event, officers had not made any arrests.

On-water demonstration

Organisers say more than 900 people registered for the event, with more than 600 taking to the water.

Hundreds more lined the shore of Horseshoe Beach for the hour-long demonstration.

"I'm tired of governments, from the federal government down to the local government, not doing enough about reducing [climate impact]," attendee Scott Alcorn said.

"I can see there's plenty of enthusiastic people who feel just the same way as I do."

Protesters formed a line across Newcastle's harbour during the one-hour paddle-out. (ABC Newcastle: Bridget Murphy)

A limited police presence, mostly on foot, attended the protest.

In the Supreme Court hearing, Assistant Commissioner David Waddell and NSW Police's legal representative argued there were serious safety concerns for large amounts of people on the water.

A cap of 785 vessels was placed on the event.

The Port of Newcastle did not run any shipping movements between 10am and 2pm.

Election approaches

NSW Greens spokesperson for climate change and justice Sue Higginson said climate change and fossil fuel projects must be a key concern in the NSW election, scheduled for March 13, 2027.

She argued while the cost of living is the biggest issue for voters coming into the campaign period, it "does not mean people are not also concerned about the health of their local environment".

"Labor and the Coalition, all they want to do is talk about One Nation … what we are doing is providing the people with a real alternative and a real vision for their future."

NSW Greens MLC Sue Higginson declared her support to the Rising Tide movement. (ABC Newcastle: Bridget Murphy)

Ms Higginson also referred to a recent decision by the Minns government to make legislative changes allowing the Mount Pleasant coalmine in the Upper Hunter to increase its life and output.

The premier announced the move despite a High Court ruling relating to the mine that concluded global climate emissions must be considered in approvals.

"[The government] is literally carving laws that defy the High Court's ruling because a coal company is threatening to lay off workers before Christmas," she said.

Ms Higginson said the matter is set to be debated in NSW parliament next week.

A Rising Tide spokesperson confirmed the group plans to hold a larger on-water protest at the end of February on Newcastle Harbour, a fortnight before the election.

World.title: Camping, sightseeing booking portal disabled while data breach investigated
World.content:
The ACT government is stressing vigilance after a cybersecurity breach of a booking platform for campgrounds in territory parks and reserves.

The government said another of its departments, VisitCanberra, used for accommodation and attraction bookings in the ACT, had also been compromised.

The third-party platform, Bookeasy, processes bookings and permits for the National Parks booking system in the ACT and other Australian states, storing personal data from emails to addresses and phone numbers.

It comes as systems in Queensland, Victoria and South Australia were hacked this week.

In a statement, Bookeasy said it was continuing to investigate, and so far had identified potential compromising of customers' personal and booking information.

The platform says it has not identified any breaches of financial details. (Supplied)

"Following a security alert, we were able to take immediate containment action. This included engaging cyber experts to assist with our investigation and provide advice," Bookeasy said.

It said it had not detected any access to credit card details.

The ACT government said it has emailed around 6,000 users, warning them of attempts to scam or phish in the wake of the breach.

Platform suspended

The territory government said some Canberran campers had received "suspicious messages via email of WhatsApp applications".

"We urge extreme caution and to consider that there is a risk of being scammed," the department's executive group manager Bren Burkevics said.

Mr Burkevics said the government has temporarily disabled the platform while it assessed the fallout.

National Parks hacked The National Parks booking system for Queensland, Victoria and South Australia has suffered a data breach, with hackers stealing personal user information.

"Bookeasy has notified the ACT government that they have incurred a cyber incident and potentially the unauthorised release of information," he said.

"So in the abundance of caution, the ACT government has suspended the use of that website."

Mr Burkevics said people could make bookings directly via the parks government website.

"The usual message is that avoiding scams is critical in these times," he said.

"Further information is available from scamwatch.gov.au, but avoid clicking on links and providing sensitive information, particularly credit card information, to third-party applications."

World.title: Cape Town inquiry spoke to all Aussie bowlers, ABC understands
World.content:
All four bowlers from the 2018 Cape Town Test spoke to investigators as part of the inquiry into ball tampering, the ABC understands, running counter to claims by former opening batter David Warner.

Warner wrote on social media that Cricket Australia's investigation — which saw him and Steve Smith banned for a year, and Cameron Bancroft rubbed out for nine months — was poorly handled and had a pre-determined outcome.

"As far as I am aware, CA did not interview Josh Hazlewood, Mitchell Starc or Nathan Lyon in their 2018 investigation. If that's correct, then how can CA push the idea that the bowlers didn't know?" Warner wrote.

But sources connected to the bowling group said Nathan Lyon, Josh Hazlewood and Mitchell Starc were interviewed. The other front-line bowler from Cape Town, current Test captain Pat Cummins, said during a marathon press conference on Friday that he spoke to investigators.

A source close to the bowlers said they all spoke to investigators. (Getty Images: Scott Barbour/Cricket Australia)

"They were all interviewed. [Warner's] comments are just not true," one source told the ABC.

The ABC also understands Tim Paine was interviewed as part of the investigation.

Cummins is sadly mistaken In his detailed 70-minute press conference, Pat Cummins said he hoped he could draw a line under the brewing Sandpapergate civil war. David Warner quickly proved that won't be happening.

After Cummins's press conference, Warner said Cummins had "thrown [Usman Khawaja] under the bus" by rejecting Khawaja's claims that more people were responsible for sandpaper entering the field of play than Warner, Bancroft and Smith.

"The way it was handled in the first place, it was hard for us to go back and give more evidence," Warner said on Fox Sports before Friday's ODI between Australia and England.

"I feel like it was a botched investigation. It was a quick one to get it over and done with. Some of the questions were quite challenging in the way it was being planted on us [Warner, Steve Smith and Cameron Bancroft] and we had to move on and just accept responsibility."

Usman Khawaja (right) said it wasn't fair for three players to bear all the responsibility for ball tampering. (Getty Images: Nick Potts/PA Images)

And Warner has doubled down on social media.

"It looks like they had decided who they wanted to blame from the very beginning, ran a shoddy investigation to serve the purpose and now they want to maintain the false narrative that bowlers had no idea," he wrote.

"That stinks of a cover-up."

Cricket Australia said in response: "As we have stated previously, all players were given the opportunity to speak at the time of the initial investigation and have had the ability to come forward with new evidence in the eight years since.

"Subsequently, CA has respected every player and former players right to provide their own version of events."

In his new book, Khawaja said he was never spoken to despite sitting next to Cameron Bancroft during discussions about using sandpaper on the ball.

What did Khawaja say about Sandpapergate in his book? Much has been written and said about Usman Khawaja's new book — but what's actually in the pages of Sabr?

Cummins on Friday said he spoke to investigators and there were calls at the time for anyone with more information to come forward.

On Tuesday, Starc was one of the first players to be asked about Khawaja's claims and said there were "differing opinions of eight years ago".

"We were heavily grilled through the process at the time and since," he said.

"I won't speak on behalf of the bowlers but, from where I stand, my opinion hasn't changed, and my recollection hasn't changed from what we said in 2021."

In 2021, Bancroft implied in an interview that the bowlers likely knew what was going on.

"Obviously what I did benefits bowlers and the awareness around that, probably, is self-explanatory," he said.

Starc, Cummins, Lyon and Hazlewood released a joint statement in response, saying they were disappointed to have their integrity questioned.

"We did not know a foreign substance was taken onto the field to alter the condition of the ball until we saw the images on the big screen at Newlands," they wrote five years ago.

World.title: 'The line-up is huge': Australians caught up in US flight chaos
World.content:
Australians have been caught up in widespread flight disruptions across the United States after a communications outage forced aviation authorities to ground flights nationwide.

More than 11,000 flights were delayed or cancelled, with passengers left stranded at airports across the country after the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) issued an unprecedented ground stop.

The grounding has since been lifted, but airlines are warning it could take time to clear the backlog, with disruptions also affecting flights departing Australia for the US.

Look back on our live blog for the latest on the issues affecting flights in the US and Australia.

Sydney Airport said flights to the US would now resume from Mascot after being temporarily grounded on Saturday morning, and urged passengers to contact their airlines.

The disruption has affected travellers at major airports including New York's JFK, Los Angeles International Airport and San Diego.

Adelaide traveller Trish Crabb snapped this photograph while in line at JFK airport in New York. She was among thousands of travellers caught up in US flight cancellations. (Supplied: Trish Crabb)

Trish Crabb, from Adelaide, was among those caught up in the chaos after her flight from New York to Miami was grounded.

She and her husband were due to fly out of JFK Airport when they discovered their Delta flight had been cancelled.

"The line-up is huge, at least 200 people in front of me and that's just for our Delta flight," Ms Crabb said.

The couple are holidaying in the US and had planned to drive from Miami to Fort Lauderdale to board a cruise.

"My husband is going to try and find us a hotel room somewhere close by, and hopefully we will be able to get a flight out at some stage," she said.

Despite the disruption, Ms Crabb said passengers appeared to be keeping their composure.

"Everyone was very calm," she said, adding most people were taking the situation in their stride.

Rivkah Brown, from Myrtleford in Victoria, was stranded at San Diego Airport after her Delta flight was cancelled.

Rivkah Brown from Victoria was stranded at San Diego Airport following a cruise in the US. She's now boarding a bus to get to Las Vegas. (Supplied: Rivkah Brown)

Ms Brown had just disembarked from a cruise and was stopping over in San Diego before travelling to Las Vegas, where she was due to meet her fiancé.

"I was supposed to be on a Delta flight, we're not being told anything, other than it's been cancelled," she said.

She said she would now take a bus to Las Vegas instead, a journey of almost 10 hours.

"It's disappointing but it is what it is," Ms Brown said.

What caused the disruption?

The FAA ordered the nationwide ground stop on Friday, local time, after communications problems affecting air traffic control centres across the United States.

US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the issue was affected all Air Route Traffic Control Centres, with technicians investigating the cause.

What we know about the US flight groundstop Aviation authorities cited "extraordinary circumstances and reasons of safety", with the White House blaming outdated air traffic control technology for the outage.

The FAA said the decision was made because of "extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety".

US Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said preliminary investigations pointed to a telecommunications outage, with no immediate indication of a deliberate attack.

"There's no indication as of yet that this was a nefarious attack against it. It's just a telecommunications outage as of right now," he said.

The outage affected the 22 regional air traffic control centres responsible for directing aircraft between airports across the country.

At least 600 flights had been diverted, including aircraft sent back to their departure airports or redirected elsewhere.

The order to ground all departing US flights was finally lifted after more than five hours. (AP Photo: Tony Gutierrez)

About 11,000 flights carrying more than 1.5 million passengers had been scheduled to depart US airports after 4pm Eastern time on Friday.

Planes already in the air were able to continue to their destinations, with authorities prioritising their safe landing.

The nationwide ground stop was the first since January 2023, when a computer system failure at the FAA caused thousands of delays. It was also only the second nationwide grounding since the September 11 terrorist attacks in 2001.

Advice for Australian travellers

Australian travellers caught up in the disruption are being urged to contact their airline or travel agent if they are due to fly within the next 72 hours.

The Australian Travel Industry Association (ATIA) says those passengers are being prioritised, while people travelling later are being asked to hold off contacting travel providers so urgent cases can be dealt with first.

Travellers should also check their airline's website or app for flight updates.

ATIA chief executive Dean Long said passengers travelling soon should contact their provider if they had not already heard from them.

"If you're travelling in the next 72 hours, that's our priority. If you haven't heard from your travel agent, tour operator or airline yet, get in touch with them," he said.

"We know this is unsettling for travellers. Our members are there to help, and we are monitoring the situation closely."

The Federal Government's SmartTraveller website is telling Australians to monitor media and contact airlines for updates and to reschedule flights.

It advises travellers to exercise "normal safety precautions" in the US.

World.title: Hauser ends stunning triathlon season with silver
World.content:
Australia's leading triathlete Matt Hauser has claimed a silver medal in the season-ending World Triathlon Championship Series race in Abu Dhabi.

Gold Coast-based Hauser finished 18 seconds behind Brazil's Miguel Hidalgo, with New Zealand's Paris Olympics silver medallist Hayden Wilde in third.

The result confirms Hauser's second place finish in the overall season standings, with newly crowned world champion, Vasco Vilaça of Portugal, not racing in Abu Dhabi.

"I could really feel the legs in the back end of that race, I think I could feel the whole year in the back end of that race to be honest," said Hauser, who won four golds this season, as well as the Noosa Tri earlier this month.

"Miguel had too much out there today, you could tell he was really locked in and credit to him he did a lot of work on the bike as well.

"So all round a really great race and good to see him back on top as well."

The 'world champion persona' didn't come overnight for Matt Hauser Despite being Australia's first male triathlon world champion in 20 years, Matt Hauser is still building the blocks towards his aim of Olympic success in 2028.

The race, originally scheduled for March but postponed due to security concerns in the region, took place after the grand final in Pontevedra.

However, the competition still provided valuable qualifying points for the LA 2028 Olympic Games.

"I always think about LA, it's always in my mind, without overexposing my thoughts. It would be silly not to think about it," Hauser told AusTriathlon in the lead up to the Abu Dhabi event.

"It's a process and journey we've been on since Paris, I'm really focused on performing well at those Games."

The qualification period runs until May 18, 2028, with an athlete's 12 best results until then counting towards their overall ranking.

Fellow Australian Luke Willian came home in fifth place, with Luke Schofield 29th, Brandon Copeland 35th and Cal McClusky 40th.

"[It was good to see] Luke Willian having a sprint finish for fourth and fifth," Hauser said

"I'm just really stoked on the podium, it's been a big year and a long year at that."

Hayden Wilde (right) is shaping up as one of Matt Hauser's biggest challengers for Olympic gold in LA. (Supplied: World Triathlon)

In the women’s race, Matilda Offord was the best placed of the Australians finishing in 35th, with Sophie Malowiecki not finishing.

Russia's Diana Isakova claimed her first World Triathlon Series victory, surging away from Luxembourg's Jeanne Lehair, with American Gwen Jorgensen in third.

The race marks the end of the World Triathlon Series Championship races, as the tour combines with the Professional Triathletes Organisation to form a new Triathlon World Tour.

The new circuit will combined the existing T100 Triathlon World Tour and the World Triathlon Championship Series (WTCS), rebranded as the T100 World Championship Tour and T50 World Championship Tour respectively.

The Professional Triathletes Organisation (PTO) and World Triathlon today announced what the Triathlon World Tour brand will look like to fans and athletes when it starts next year, as well as the initial 2027 T50 and T100 World Championship Tour calendars.

"Our sport was really fragmented from a competition and commercial perspective, which was holding it back," World Triathlon president Antonio Arimany said earlier this year.

"We could have waited until the end of the current Olympic qualification before making the changes, but the changes we're making were too important to wait.

"By introducing the Triathlon World Tour now, we are creating one unified structure and brand, which can unify as many events as possible, creating a win-win situation for all of us in the sport."

World.title: What we know so far about why US flights were grounded
World.content:
The United States has lifted its order to ground departing flights nationwide as a major communications outage continues to disrupt air travel.

The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) cited "extraordinary circumstances and reasons of safety", with the White House blaming outdated air traffic control technology for the outage.

Thousands of flights into and out of the US were delayed or cancelled, leaving airlines and passengers scrambling to work out their next steps.

Look back on our live blog for the latest on the issues affecting flights in the US and Australia.

The ABC understands the US "ground stop" has caused some delays to a small number of US-bound flights from Australia.

Here's what we know about the unfolding situation so far.

What caused the problem?

US Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin has attributed the disruption to a telecommunications issue.

"It's just a telecommunications outage as of right now," Mr Mullin told reporters at the White House earlier on Friday, local time.

" Everybody's safe. There's no reason to be concerned about your loved ones if they're flying. "

It is not yet confirmed what specifically caused the communications failure.

Loading...

Mr Mullin had earlier said investigators would examine whether there was any connection to the FAA's nationwide rollout of a new artificial intelligence (AI) system designed to help identify problems and reroute aircraft.

However, the system operates from a single location near Washington DC and provides recommendations to air traffic control centres.

US President Donald Trump has also rejected suggestions the new AI technology was responsible for the disruption.

In his latest press conference, US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy blamed "old technology" for the outage.

"What we have is an incredibly old air traffic control system," he said.

"We have analogue telecoms, our routers actually got overloaded with data … and they started to give us inconsistencies in the data … because of that we shut the system down," he says.

" It is the old hardware that went down. "

Speaking to ABC News, Shawn Pruchnik, an associate professor in Ohio State University's aviation department, said officials made the right call by grounding departing aircraft as a precaution.

"We have this significant problem of airplanes at higher altitudes that cannot communicate with air traffic control, so the solution to that is less airplanes up there," he said.

"Keep everyone down, let everyone land."

Was it caused by a threat to the US?

Mr Mullin said there was currently no indication the outage was the result of a nefarious attack.

However, he later added:

"We're not ruling out anything at this point.

"The first thing is [to make sure] everybody that is flying in is safe."

In a subsequent press conference, Mr Mullin reiterated that there were no signs pointing to a cyber attack for now.

"Typically, somebody's going to raise their hand up and say, 'Hey, we did that'. There's no chatter. We haven't seen any footprints … of people that have got into the system," he said.

"It appears this was mechanically driven. However, we are still looking."

Is it linked to the Microsoft outage?

Microsoft has denied any known connection between its recent global outage and the FAA's nationwide stoppage.

"We have no indication that the FAA's nationwide ground stop is related to any Microsoft services," the company said on X.

The statement came amid speculation about a possible link to Microsoft's 21-hour global outage, which was resolved earlier on Friday.

Mr Mullin also dismissed the suggestion of a connection, telling reporters: "I don't see any reason to connect those two at all."

Which flights were affected?

The FAA's order applied to departing flights across the US, grounding nearly all aircraft scheduled to take off during the five hours it was in effect.

The agency also asked Eurocontrol, its European counterpart, to suspend flights to the US from its 42 member states, including Türkiye, Morocco and Israel.

Aircraft that were already in the air when the order was issued were allowed to continue safely to their destinations.

The order to ground flights resulted in mass delays and flight cancellations. (AP Photo: Mike Stewart)

The full scale of the disruption is still emerging, but the impact has already been felt by tens of thousands of travellers.

Flight-tracking website FlightAware reported about 9,814 delays on flights into and out of the US, alongside more than 4,749 cancellations. Those figures are continuing to change as the disruption unfolds.

Meanwhile, the ABC understands Australian airlines are dealing with a backlog of delayed flights.

Australians caught in US flight chaos Thousands of flights have been delayed or cancelled across the US, leaving Australian travellers stranded at airports.

Before the US order was lifted, a Sydney Airports spokesperson had said all US-bound flights from Sydney were grounded.

Since the order was lifted, the spokesperson said:

"Flights scheduled to depart Sydney for the United States are expected to depart as planned. Passengers should continue to check with their airline for the latest information."

The ABC is continuing to stay in touch with Sydney Airports for further updates.

Can planes already in the air land safely?

Yes. Aviation experts say pilots and air traffic controllers are trained to manage communications failures.

Skip Bailey, an aviation professor who spoke to The Associated Press, said pilots were expected to maintain the headings and instructions given by air traffic controllers before communications were lost.

If the outage continued, they could revert to their filed flight plans.

Airlines and passengers were left scrambling to work out their next steps. (AP Photo)

Pilots may also be able to communicate with other aircraft over the radio, even if they cannot reach air traffic controllers. Commercial aircraft also have their own radar systems.

"It's not mass chaos out there," Professor Bailey said.

"There are plenty of ways to try to communicate."

He said preventing additional aircraft from taking off had been crucial to avoiding further complications.

"We don't want to put more aircraft into a system that's already having an issue."

When will flights resume?

Mr Duffy said US air space was reopened at 8:15pm Eastern Standard Time, about five hours after the grounding order was issued.

However, he warned that flights could be "slow" to take off again.

"If you are watching, if you are at an airport, check with your airline; it depends on [if they] have crews available," Mr Duffy said in his latest press conference.

"We are going to try to move as many of those [flights] as we can tonight if we have capacity.

"If not, we are going to start tomorrow morning with our airline partners to move those aircraft, but it is going to take us some time to unwind what has happened this afternoon."

The FAA has assured travellers the country is now safe for air travel.

"Before clearing flights to resume, we thoroughly tested our systems to confirm they were stable and that operations remain reliable," it said in a statement.

What's the advice for Australian travellers?

Australians travelling to the US should expect to hear from their airlines or travel agents as the disruption continues, the Australian Travel Industry Association said.

"We're absolutely expecting the domestic network within America to be disrupted for at least the next 24 hours," the industry body said in its latest statement.

"If you have a stand-by ticket, the reality is you probably aren't getting on a plane, but if you've got a confirmed ticket, you can rest assured those planes will be taking off safely and on time."

It has also issued the following advice:

World.title: 'Plastic farmers' in Indonesia unaware of the dangers of burning waste
World.content:
Ahmad Yani spent hours each day sifting through piles of rubbish, searching for recyclable materials to sell to help make ends meet.

For decades, his family and other people in his village in East Java in Indonesia would buy truckloads of waste residue from factories recycling imported paper and cardboard.

They would spread the waste on the ground, and separate plastics from paper and cardboard.

The paper would be sold back to the recycling factories and most of the plastics to industries that needed fuel for furnaces.

"It had become a source of livelihood for many low-income residents," Mr Yani said, adding he would make about 300,000 rupiah ($24) a month.

Any plastics still left over would be used in his village to fire limestone kilns, to produce building materials to sell or use.

Ahmad Yani says plastic waste from overseas has been coming to his village for decades. (Supplied: Brawijaya University)

Mr Yani said among the rubbish he noticed food sachets and cat and dog food packaging with Australian labels as well as labels of countries in Europe.

While burning plastic has helped support the family's livelihood, the smoke from their home and neighbouring households may be having devastating health impacts.

He said some people he knew who had operated the limestone kilns had died from respiratory diseases and causes were never determined.

Mr Yani said the burning of plastics in his village was no longer happening. It stopped about a year ago.

Several local media reported companies had stopped distributing waste to his community to sort, which had sparked anger among locals who lost their source of income.

The ABC couldn't independently verify the reasons for the change.

But health concerns for people who have been exposed to air pollution from burning plastics remain.

Women sort through waste in East Java. (Supplied: Brawijaya University)

'Unaware of the dangers'

Researchers from the Climate and Health Centre at Brawijaya University were investigating the health impacts of air pollution in East Java when they found locals were burning plastic waste.

One of the researchers, Sekar Aqila Salsabilla, said pre-screening tests earlier this year on those in their study produced some worrying findings.

She said at least 20 per cent of the more than 4,000 participants across six East Java villages were at high risk of cardiovascular disease and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.

Sekar Aqila Salsabilla has been researching the health impacts of air pollution in villages in East Java. (Supplied: Sekar Aqila Salsabilla)

"When we first entered these communities, one of the most distressing findings was that many people were unaware of the dangers associated with burning plastic waste," said Ms Salsabilla, who worked with more than 30 researchers as part of a broader study, the majority of whom had medical backgrounds.

People earning money from sorting waste, known as "plastic farmers", knew their health was "slowly declining" but did not understand the source of the problems, she said.

"Despite the income they generate, many do not realise that the long-term health burden they may face is likely to be far greater than the money they earn from handling and burning this waste," Ms Salsabilla said.

Environmental activists say Australian plastic waste was in this rubbish heap in East Java, Indonesia, in 2024. (Supplied: Ecoton)

Most plastic waste was no longer burned in people's homes but rather converted into refuse-derived fuel (RDF) and burned in a designated facility, she said.

"But I think this only relocates the problem rather than actually solving it," Ms Salsabilla said, adding the facility still required humans to sort the waste.

Emissions from open waste burning, such as burning plastics, include a variety of air pollutants, some of which have particularly harmful effects on both the climate and health, according to the World Health Organization (WHO).

"Exposure to these pollutants, whether short or long-term, can lead to adverse health effects such as coughing, skin irritation, respiratory diseases, and other negative outcomes," the WHO says on its website.

Environmentalists say plastic waste from Australia is often found in East Java. (Supplied: Ecoton)

Ms Salsabilla said the waste imported to East Java was coming from places including Australia, the US and Europe.

Agus Rusly, the waste reduction director at Indonesia's Ministry of Environment, told the ABC the lack of accessible waste management services, irregular waste collection, and limited recycling facilities had contributed to open waste burning in Indonesia.

Mr Rusly said the Environment Ministry was working to improve waste governance, in collaboration with regional governments, through a national framework "aimed at achieving comprehensive waste management by 2029".

Enforcement is 'weak'

In 2019, Indonesian environmentalists called on Australia to tighten its regulation and enforcement of waste exports to foreign countries, saying Australian exporters were effectively "smuggling" huge amounts of plastic and waste paper supposedly sent for recycling.

Daru Setyorini, executive director of local environmental activist group Ecoton, said plastics with Australian labels could still be found in East Java and people in villages were still "secretly" burning plastics.

Environmentalists have long called for Australia to tighten waste exports to countries such as Indonesia. (Supplied)

"To this day, it [the plastic waste] still exists, although it has decreased significantly compared to 2024 and the years before that," she said.

"The monitoring and enforcement are still weak. Ideally, these imports from Australia should just be stopped altogether."

Australia exported 701,000 tonnes of paper and cardboard to Indonesia in the recent financial year, according to Joe Pickin at Blue Environment who analysed data from Australia's Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water (DCCEEW).

While Australia can legally export recyclable plastic waste to Indonesia, concerns have centred on plastic contaminants in paper and cardboard exports.

'Take your s*** from Indonesia' Environmentalists in Indonesia claim that among the thousands of tonnes of paper bales sent to East Java are household waste items including faeces-contaminated nappies.

Indonesia applies a 2 per cent contamination limit on paper waste imports, meaning contaminants such as plastic, food residue, soil and other non-paper materials must not exceed that threshold.

A spokesperson for Australia's Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) said it took "allegations of unlawful waste exports seriously".

"The National EPA assesses allegations of non-compliance with Commonwealth environmental laws and takes a proportionate, risk-based approach to determining appropriate regulatory responses," they said.

Many Australian material recovery facilities have invested significantly in upgrading their operations to meet these standards and ensure that materials exported for recycling met appropriate quality requirements, according to the Australian Council of Recycling.

"Failure to enforce these rules not only risks environmental harm but also disadvantages operators doing the right thing, undermining their investments," CEO Suzanne Toumbourou said.

Ms Setyorini said each country should be responsible for its own plastic waste.

"Indonesia has got enough waste problems, so developed countries like Australia shouldn't export their waste here," she said.

The DCCEEW has been contacted for comment.

A first home buyer raising her paddle for the first time won the keys to a one-bedroom apartment in Elizabeth Bay on Saturday, paying $760,000 at auction. As a crowd of about 40 people gathered on the footpath outside the art deco building, bidding for 6/39 Roslyn Gardens opened at $620,000. A further bid of $20,000 followed, then it fell into a steady rhythm of $5000 and $10,000 increments. When the price reached $735,000, auctioneer Dave McMahon declared the property was on the market. Five further bids of $5000 followed before the hammer fell. The opening bidder was also the person who eventually won the keys. She had been renting, but had more recently moved in with family in preparation for entering the property market.



Related Article Luxury property Five of the best Sydney homes with facades we love Six parties registered to bid with five active. Most of the underbidders were also first home buyers. The property had a guide of $700,000 and a reserve of $745,000, which was adjusted to $735,000 during the auction. There is no legal requirement for a vendor’s reserve to be in line with their property’s price guide. The apartment has retained many of its original features, including patterned ceilings and timberwork, and has been held as an investment for some time. Sales agent for BresicWhitney East, Melinda Antella said market conditions had created space for new buyers.



“There are some opportunities for first home buyers because they are not competing with investors,” she said. McMahon, the auctioneer, said while he expected little change in the market into 2027, buyer sentiment was linked to stability. “People are looking for more stability [in terms of] interest rate movement, but once we have clarity, it will give them confidence to enter the market,” he said. The apartment’s study enjoys a view of jacarandas. Sitthixay Ditthavong Most bidders took shelter under the trees on a hot and humid morning as auctioneer Dave McMahon competed with passing traffic and the occasional plane during the auction of 6/39 Roslyn Gardens. Sitthixay Ditthavong



The property was one of 646 scheduled to go to auction in Sydney this week. At Mount Kuring-gai, a six-bedroom home passed in on Saturday when the sole bidder failed to attend, citing delays associated with Friday’s Microsoft outage. Two parties were expected to register to bid for 5 High Street, but the strongest bidder was not confident about doing so without seeing the requested changes in the contract documents before the auction. The Microsoft outage hit Australia early Friday morning and affected Copilot, Teams and Microsoft Outlook, resulting in issues accessing and sending emails.



“It all fell apart because the solicitors couldn’t talk to each other,” sales agent for Stone Real Estate, Dean Finch said. “I ended up having to send things through WhatsApp to get the changes requested. Related Article Architecture Renovate or detonate. How two heritage homes had very different fates “But they were still not confident [about bidding].” The auction was held but closed without a bid, although a second party arrived after the auction ended. Both groups were families from the wider local area. The property had a listed guide of $1.95 million and a reserve of $2.3 million.



The six-bedroom home has five bedrooms in the main house – three with ensuite bathrooms – and a self-contained studio above the garage. Finch is hoping to sell the two-storey Hamptons-inspired home in the next fortnight, but if he is unsuccessful, he said the vendors, who want to downsize, will rent it out. In Enmore, a two-bedroom apartment sold under the hammer for $1.34 million, $10,000 below the reserve. Five groups registered to bid for the keys to 7/159 Enmore Road, which is positioned just steps away from the popular Enmore Theatre.



Four parties actively participated with bidding opening at $1.25 million. It went up in increments of $10,000 and $20,000 until it reached $1.32 million. Ray White Erskineville agent Ercan Ersan then negotiated with the bidder to make an additional offer of $1.33 million, and it was called on the market. The opening bidders made a further bid of $10,000 and the property sold. The two-bedroom apartment is at the back of the block of the Encore on Enmore building and has views across to Chatswood Domain It had a guide of $1.3 million and a reserve of $1.35 million. The successful bidders were a brother and sister who plan to use the property as a city bolthole and rent it as short-term accommodation. The underbidder was a first home buyer bidding with the assistance of her mother.



Ersan said he had noticed more interest from investors in recent weeks. “My last three auctions all had some investor activity,” he said. “They tend to come back where they see value and prices have now reached that level. If we’re not [at the bottom of the market], we’re pretty bloody close.” Property alerts are now available in the SMH app. Turn them on to receive the latest market news and trends.

World.title: The wildest, most shocking moments from You Can See Everything – ranked
World.content:
CultureMoviesDocumentaries The wildest, most shocking moments from You Can See Everything – ranked Nell Geraets November 14, 2026 — 4:00pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 No gift articles left You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month.
